title: WR Marvin Harrison Jr. Press Conference | AZ Cardinals
text: We haven't had a chance to talk to you about just like your thoughts on Mike coming here as coach and just the kind of offense that he's running and just your overall feelings over these past couple months. >> You know, it's been great. Um just learning the system. Uh it's been exciting. You know, Mike, Hack, Tony, uh they bring the energy every single day, man. They make, you know, coming to work really fun and enjoyable. Um we get out there and we compete and uh they're super competitive. So, you know, it's been a joy. >> So, everything that you feel like is going to change significantly for you personally in terms of your role now? >> In terms of what? >> In terms of what you're asked to do out on the field. >> No, I don't think so. >> After a season, what what's your process of just evaluating how you performed? >> After a season? Uh go back, you watch the film, kind of watch um all your reps, uh you evaluate and you look at the off season, uh figure out where you want to improve, uh and just get better. >> What did you What did you learn from last year? It was a difficult year just because of, you know, the the different injuries, but what did you What did you assess from your season? >> Yeah, just I mean, the injuries kind of sucked, um honestly. Uh you know, the appendix really was the most importantly just like it's unfortunate cuz nothing I really could do about that and kind of just wrong timing. And um yeah, man, looking back on it just just sucks in general because, like I said, nothing I could do about it, but um you just continue to move forward, continue to get better. Uh really just kind of whole off season I really just thought about how unfortunate that situation was for me. >> How long did it take you to get back to 100% physically from, you know, the various injuries that you went through last season? >> Uh I guess it's an ongoing process still. >> [snorts] >> So, yeah, yeah. >> Do you feel like you made that year one to year two jump, or did you think the injuries kind of prevented that from happening and that's something that can be done year two to year three? >> Um I think it's continue to just get better each year. Um I mean I don't really know what, you know, the jump necessarily, but just like continue always to improve, continue to get better. Um you know, it it does hurt and not playing what I think didn't play half the snaps of the team snaps. So, I mean that obviously um you know, doesn't look great, but obviously just continue to get better. Um and kind of stay healthy most importantly. >> With that being said, is there a fire then with how the season end? Like is there a fire within you to kind of turn [snorts] it around? >> Yeah, I mean it sucks not playing. Um I've never not played. I've never kind of been injured, never missed a game. Um little league to high school to college to so, staying on the sideline, I mean that definitely sucked. Um you know, almost half the year basically, so I think I don't want to say light a fire, it just one makes you appreciate the game more. You want to be out there, you want to be with your teammates, want to compete. Uh you want to win, but uh I I definitely learned a lot from not being able to be able to play. >> Last offseason, a lot of talk was putting on weight, 12-14 lbs and and being a little stronger, those contested What have been your priorities and steps you've taken this offseason and and what specific goals I guess in your game are you really focused on? >> Just health. Health. I mean I feel like if I'm out there, everything else is going to take care of itself. Um so, just doing the the best I can and make sure my body's right week in and week out. >> Is there any benefit to just having to sit and watch sort of grow >> Benefit? No, I don't think there's there's no benefit of not playing really, but uh I would say maybe you get a different perspective, but I wouldn't say benefit, no. >> With the feet injuries, you said it's still an ongoing process. Does that mean they're not 100%? And if not, how long do you think it'll take to be completely >> I don't think it's going linger into next season, for sure. I mean I think it's just I think with your feet, [snorts] you use them a lot of times, so that's kind of where that makes, you know, the process take probably a little longer than maybe usual, but um obviously it's definitely nothing that prevents me from anything at the moment. Like I go 100%. Uh, I'm still out there doing everything, you know, I normally would do. Uh, but obviously, yeah, it's just like an ongoing process, for sure. >> Was there ever a point with I mean, you had the the appendix comes out of nowhere, you have these feet injuries. You've never been injured. Are you Is there ever a point where you're just kind of like, "Come on, man. This can't be real right now." >> Yeah. I mean, >> [laughter] >> so I had really the concussion against the Colts game. That was back-to-back. I think the same week I had it with Green Bay last my rookie year, and had the concussion the Colts game the same exact year, and then you get the appendix, then you come back, the first game back you get your you know, the feet thing. It's just couldn't really catch a break last year, kind of felt like, but uh, that's life. You just got to, you know, got to keep moving. >> It it did seem though like before the injuries kind of picked up I want to say like in December, but before that point, it seemed like you were kind of finding your stride. Are you able to take some comfort in and some of the stuff you did put on tape? I'm thinking about the Dallas game and some other moments kind of that around that time of year. Does that kind of I don't know. Did that comfort you at all in the off season going into the off season? >> Uh, comfort me? No. Um, personally, I just never really look at any positives. I mean, you probably should uh, for your health, but um, I don't really look at any positives. It's always kind of the negative, so um, I mean, I don't really think about the Dallas game much or any other kind of games before. Just always what to improve >> Have you always been that way or is that >> Yeah. >> Why? Where did that come from? >> Probably my dad, truthfully. Just He Yeah. >> You've sat there and talked to us all the time about how what Michael Wilson can do. And then for him to actually put it on tape last year and on the stat sheet as well. When you go into this season, how much of the attention that now is going to be on Mike might be able to open up some stuff for you? >> Yeah, I mean, obviously, we have a lot of weapons In the offense, obviously have Trey and Mike. Just got a really good speed new car in the draft and Jeremiah. So, I mean I think we definitely have a lot of good weapons, cool pieces to kind of, you know, get everybody the ball. So, it's definitely going to be fun and interesting. I think the biggest thing is you can't really key on one person. Someone does, you get the one-on-one match up and I kind of have trust in everybody to go win those. So, it's definitely exciting. >> Last year you made the game-winning points in your career. What have you learned about how to quickly create chemistry with a different quarterback than maybe you played with before? >> I mean I think it's always just reps. It's always kind of the best things and that constant communication off the field. Just whether it's meeting with them, watching film together, or exchanging text messages of hey, this is what I saw, this is what you saw. I feel like that can kind of speed up the process, but there's nothing better than actual, you know, game practice. I mean practice reps help too, but game reps as well. >> Jeremiah said that you were one of the first guys to reach out to [snorts] him after he was drafted. How has your relationship kind of grown since he's got to the team? >> Yeah. So, obviously me and Jerry we have a connection because of New Balance. So, we're both New Balance athletes and we had an event, I want to say a month or two before the draft. I just like, you you know, I didn't know anything at first. I didn't know anything, but I was just like, hey, it would be really cool, really special to get a chance to play with you. I kind of know the talent, I was seeing the talent that he has and it kind of all worked out. So, yeah. >> What's been the early impressions of him with the chemistry element at? >> Have you and Jacoby been able to find ways to continue building that chemistry even with him not here right now? not much. Obviously, you know, he's got to kind of have to be here to do that, but I'm all in support of, you know, kind of what he's doing. I think, you know, he has to do what's best for him and his family. And so, yeah, that's kind of where I'll say that. >> What's been the early impressions of Carson? >> Great, man. He's a baller. He's a baller. I love that he kind of goes out there and just kind of has the attitude that, you know, I he has a lot of confidence in himself and he kind of can make any throw he wants to make. And I think I definitely kind of definitely admire that about him. He works very hard. >> Being a top five pick, maybe nothing has to be said, but do you say anything to Jeremiah about expectations or something for working with him? >> No. No. Definitely definitely don't put any expectations on him or any more pressure saying you have to go do this or we need you to go do that. Definitely don't do that. So, just go out there and be yourself. Obviously, you're here for a reason. You got drafted that high for a reason. Because of your abilities, your mental makeup. So, just kind of just be you. >> But, did you have that conversation with him at all? >> No. No. Yeah. No. >> I know you're really excited about Mike LaFleur's offense. You've heard so many good things about it. I guess like specifically for you, what makes you most excited to play in that system? >> I think just obviously the different things that we can kind of do with motions and shifts. And really just the different pieces we get to have. Really you know, having Trey, having Mike, having Jeremiah, James, just all of the backs, Tyler. We have so many weapons. So, KB. I think really that's kind of what biggest thing is we just having those different pieces around you to kind of free you up as well.

title: HC Mike LaFleur Press Conference | Arizona Cardinals 2026
text: You've talked uh before about Marv and just kind of where he is in his career. Like do you find now that you've interacted with him the amount that you have? Like do you worry about his his confidence level? Is it is it high? Like how how do you how have you judged that since you've gotten to know him? >> You know, no, I don't worry about that. You know, I I I know his intentions are right. I know his intentions are just to to show up every day and put his best foot forward and try to improve, learn this a offense. um you know, learn the guys around him and just kind of what we're trying to do. So, um again, I know you don't worry about guys that that intentions are right and I know his are. >> What do you kind of see from the tape that you watched last year where he can kind of take those next steps as a player? >> Well, one thing is just staying healthy, right? It's that year one to year two and then all of a sudden you don't have that full season. I mean, it just you never know what it can do and I and I haven't overly talked about to Marvin about last year or whatnot. I haven't talked to a lot of these guys about all the ins and outs of what happened because frankly not all of it matters. Only those guys really know individually and now we're trying to collectively be the best team we can be moving forward, you know. So, um, like I said, I like his approach in in terms of how he goes about his business every single day in the meetings. He's he's a he's a really good dude, but he's um he's super smart. Like he's really smart. Like it makes a ton of sense to him this game. So, uh, you know, again, just trying to improve every single day. So looking forward then instead of backward like what are the keys for him to maximize his skill set and kind of be the like what can he do over these next few months to be the best version version of himself come week one? >> Yeah I mean it's like all these guys you know first of all it starts with us as coaches putting him in those positions to to go be successful to to use his traits at the level that he's capable of. What he can do is a little bit different than Mike and what Mike can do is a little bit different than Trey and Kendrick Bourne and Jeremiah and all the guys that we have surrounding there you know. So again, I'm like I'm not as crazy as it sounds, but I don't want to sound like a broken record, but I'm not totally concerned about what Marv looks like in September. I'm concerned about what Marv looks like right now. And did he improve from yesterday? And I would say, yeah, I mean I mean, not that, you know, everyone's going to see the tape from today. Thought he thought he made a stride today. It's awesome. Like a lot like I thought a lot of guys did. And there are other guys that might have had a better day yesterday. Now, let's go improve and see how we can correct those mistakes. So again, just focused on the on the day-to-day with him and and keeping him and all these guys just where their feet are in the present, not worrying about, you know, come September and all those other games after. >> What's the thought of having a game plan against Miles Garrett now? >> Twice a week. >> Uh just the thought of game plan [snorts] against any really good football player, you know. So I mean again, it's great thing is I get to answer just like I did the last one. Like not you're not really concerned about that right now. That's not what kept me up at night yesterday, you know. What kept me up was, hey, we got two really good team periods. We got a two-minute. Let's see how that two-minute goes and and then we'll go from there. So, like all great players, whether it be offense or defense, you know, you you got to adjust and you got to to game plan for those guys. But, uh, not my concern. >> Is there an intimidating element though looking up at this division and seeing the reigning Super Bowl champions, Kyle Shanahan team, and then this Rams team is stacked with talent? >> Nope. >> Why not? >> Because it's not what we're concerned about right now, you know. And again, I'm trying I mean, it's just the this season's too long. This like it's that that stuff just at flat out doesn't matter. Like if we're not just focused on us right now and even when it gets in the season, like the best teams, they just they're worried about themselves and and like I want them concerned about themselves. It's it's our job as coaches when we get into that week to see, hey, what guys are available this week for us? What guys are available for them? So many things happen within a season um within the division, within the conference, within the NFL that like why worry about that stuff right now. We got enough stuff to worry about in terms of getting our systems in, making sure that these guys understand what we're asking from them from a standard perspective, how hard they're playing, and then techniques, you know, what we're asking them to do. So again, like what's going to happen in September is going to happen, and I'm not concerned about it, and I hope our guys aren't either right now. Marv, [snorts] do you see him more as an an X or a slot and why does his skill set fit both those roles? >> Yeah, I think it's a good question because I think you know like his his profile, I guess you could say, would be that of a typical X receiver. What does that mean? Like, and again, they come in all shapes and sizes, but just kind of that lengthier body that can play on the outside. But what's unique about this system and not just the Arizona Cardinals, but the systems that that run something similar is you can move them inside and outside on a whim, you know, just in terms of our formations, our motions, and all that kind of stuff. So, um you don't want to say you can get you can protect them by bringing people inside, but but you can just utilize their skill sets in different ways. So, yeah, he'll he he is our ex receiver, but again, you can um you know that you can move him around that sometimes he is, sometimes he's not, if that makes sense. You mentioned him and and Mike having slightly different skill sets. I guess what do you see as kind of their differing strengths and how can they complement each other as players? >> Yeah. So, you know, like I said with with Marv, like typically with the ex receivers, you know, let's just say Dvonte Adams last year in LA, Julio Jones, um, in Atlanta Falcons, like those typical ex guys, like they're not necessarily next to the core very often in terms of playing in between the tight ends, in between the tackles. Then you look at like what would be more so a Z receiver and Mike Wilson who's a little more compact of a guy. Those guys are a little bit more comfortable playing in in the C in the B in the D areas right there where you can insert for safeties. Buddha Baker comes down. You're going to have one or two of your receivers that are going to handle that stuff. You think of Puka Nua, you know, yeah, all the cool stuff Puka does with the ball in the air, but it's really all the cool stuff he does without the ball, you know, and so that's where you kind of see some of that same stuff from a guy like Michael Wilson. And then you think of a guy like Kendrick Bourne who's kind of in between right there. You know, we're asking Kendrick probably to play closer to the core than uh than we did, I guess, from 17 to 20, but he's capable. He's uh he's more adjusted to this game now than the first time I had him in 2020. He's seen a lot a lot more. So, the more that you have guys that that are versatile like that, but then you also want the guys that are used to just being a little bit further away from the course. So, um, you know, with the ball in their hands or or without the ball running routes, then you just figure out, hey, what are the best things that these guys can do, I just keep telling that whole room, the whole eligible room, we just need to get you between the defender and the ball because we do have a lot of size and we have really good hands within this group and if we have the mindset that if we can get between the defender and the ball, good stuff's going to happen. And I, you know, I hope they believe that because I know I certainly do. How do you how do you see with Rabbit and Dewey like h how that battle goes? Is it I mean you're going to have Buddha so kind of how do those other two fit in that sequence? >> Yeah, I think it's a it's a really cool uh problem to have but it's not a problem right anytime that we can get as many NFL good football players um on this roster. Um, those are going to be discussions and and obviously training camp like this thing will all play out the way it should and these guys are going to get a lot of valuable reps from here all the way till September. The other cool part is who says they all can't be on the field at the same time, right? And that those are things that uh obviously Nick and I have had those uh conversations uh Nick and the rest of the defensive staff. So again, I think it's it's too early to even get into like how is that all going to unfold. Um, but those are definitely, you know, kind of in the preliminary discussions of how you can keep, you know, get your best players out on the field because, uh, certainly both those guys can play. >> Over the last few weeks, guys have talked about how much of motion is used in your offense. How do you like to deploy? Is there a purpose to all the motion? Is it just kind of distract the defense? Like, how do you >> Yeah, I always say you don't want to just motion to motion. Like, there should always be a reason to why you're motioning, you know, whether you're changing leverages, changing uh matchups. You know, you think about basketball, right? and and the way the b the game has gone and just all the the picks to get the right matchups and stuff like that. It's kind of in that same vein in with motioning. It used to be, you know, um when you're going against defenses, you motion and and maybe that guy would run with them, the best corner would run with the best receiver. It's not necessarily like that anymore because people don't want to tell you what they're doing. They want to keep their guys anchored. They want to keep their nickel anchored. Not not everybody, but I mean that's where the league has been trending a little bit. So again, you're gaining your leverages and that's not just the the pass game, but that's also the run game. How can we get guys fitted up? Because if I'm blocking from outside the numbers and I'm I'm beelining in there to block Buddha Baker, well, I'm probably not going to be as strong as I need to be. But if I can short motion him down quickly, snap the ball and we're crisp and sharp, now I have a chance to get inside out with my my feet anchored and actually block the guy. And that can be the difference between one yard, five yards, 10 yards, however it gets sprung, you know. So, um there's there's a ton of different ways, ton of different reasons. And um but again, I I I hope these guys know we're not just just doing it to to look cute or you know, there's always a reason. >> Said last week that um the offense was a little bit complicated for the defense, but more so simple for you guys. What's the balance for you and who said that? >> Garner. Um what's the balance and like trying to dress it up, have all the eye candy with the motion, stuff like that, but also keeping it like simple for your guys as well? >> Yeah. Um I think it is simple, but I think our guys are pretty smart and I think they're they're they're catching on to it. Yeah, there's definitely that. Again, it's um there is a there is a illusion of complexity to this that it it's it's the same play we might have ran the day before, the week before or whatever, but it's just one little slight little adjustment with a motion or a formation. And then once you've shown that once or twice, now what's your compliment cut off of it? So, um I don't particularly right now through eight OTAAS, it's not like we're overly scheming our defense. really just trying to kind of figure out what these guys can do. It was kind of cool going through through seven practices now, eight. And as I was just kind of doing inventory on what Trey's done already in terms of he's caught this, he's caught that, he's done this, he's done that. And it's like, good, check some boxes right there because again, you don't need to be peing here in June. You're trying to figure out that they're learning us as coaches and we're learning them as players in terms of what they can do, what their strengths are. Definitely always want to go to their strengths, what their weaknesses are. do we need to stay away from those weaknesses or man it's this is a weakness but it actually can become a strength and those are all the kind of things we're learning right now um but again not trying to like trick our defense or do anything like that [snorts] >> so what's the benefit for having a guy on staff like Terrell Austin who obviously is better on the league and so you bring him in in in the role he's in like what's the benefit of having him >> it's been pretty cool because um I didn't know TA you know personally I I know coach Tomlin um decently I guess you could say uh obviously the respect that I have for him is probably the same respect that you guys all have for Coach T, you know. So, um, but being able to bring him in, he's had so many years of experience in so many different organizations. One that I respect in Pittsburgh and and he's been in been there since what whatever it's been 2019. So, a lot of years. Um, really neat that he has a home here and he was living here. Um, that he loves it. He loves being here. He loves the valley. Uh, having him being in this building has been really special. What's really neat about it that I've had discussions with him is because he's not a coordinator, he's a he's been able to kind of take a step back and just see it from a different lens. And sometimes those are, you know, the best lens that you can see something because you're not worried about this, that, and the other. And, you know, the Miles Garrett of an offense or something like that, you're looking at it from a different perspective. Um, and so just some of the things that he's been able to tell me about name that category. Um, it's been really unique and it's been really cool. It's going to be extremely valuable for me. It's going to be extremely valuable for Nick and the rest of the coaching staff, this building, then the players. So, um, really, really fortunate to have, [snorts] you know, TA >> first coach to also be a play caller, but first time in this role now that you've had some consistent practices out on the field. What has your process looked like working with Nick and just kind of getting caught up to speed on what's happening on the defensive side during practice? >> Yeah, I think um obviously those discussions happened going, you know, before we even got to OTAA, starting to to learn their language, sitting in in some of those meetings. I'm not going to sit here and say I sat in every single defensive meeting because obviously we had to get the offense ready, too. Uh, so that you obviously have a a pretty good knowledge of of what those calls are and what they're trying to get done, but you really don't totally understand until you get out there in practice and and kind of seeing those things and being able to say, "Hey, they didn't play that right or they did play this right." And that was pretty unique right there. So, um, those discussions obviously happened before practice, after practice, sometimes in practice to keep the rhythm of it. And it's not the the best. It's not the coolest thing for me, but like to keep the rhythm of it, you just got to go. Like it has to go to the next play because the moment you start over coaching one player on either side of the ball, it slows everyone down and the tempo gets slowed down and the rhythm gets slowed down and then it just looks like crap in my opinion. So we try to just go, you know, uh when those guys are out, hopefully the position coaches are coaching them up, but really the uh it really happens in the film room after that. >> The standard on on how hard to play in practice. How would you articulate what that what that standard is at practice? >> You know, it's um it's a good question because we don't have the pads on right now. But just because you don't have the pads on doesn't mean that you're not running to the football doesn't mean you're not coming off the football. Doesn't mean on offense, we had a good discussion today as a unit about playing without the football. One of the coolest things you can do as a teammate is strain for your other teammate that does have the ball. And you can you can practice great habits for yourself and for your unit by, hey, ball's thrown, I'm transition, I'm finding someone. I'm getting a body on a body. And then from a defensive perspective, how fast am I getting out of the stack? Am I running through two lines? If the ball, if it is a real play, and again, it's hard to determine what real plays are when you're not playing tackle football. But if it is a real play, and you can just tell no one's down, is everyone getting to the ball? Are they taking the right shots at the ball? If it's not a time to take a shot at the ball, are they tagging off? and everyone just kind of rallying right there. And I think that's um part of our job as coaches is to to hold guys to that standard. And once you do, then the players just kind of take over. Um coolest part is I do think we got the right people, the right players in this locker room to uphold that standard and make it their own, you know. But every year, I don't care where you're at, you have to reset that thing, you know. It just so happens to be we're in year one right here. And uh you know, just trying to show how we practice. >> With one uh with one practice, >> Josh, we'll make this the last one. with one OTAA left. How healthy are you guys right now heading into mini camp? >> Uh good. I mean there's some positions are a little bit thicker than others and that's okay. I mean that that happens when you practice. Uh but no, we're in a we're in a good spot. We got the one day, you know, then obviously the mini camp and like I've told you guys that that mini camp's going to really resemble more of just kind of two OTAA days just by the way you practice and kind of how the rules end up, you know, playing out.

title: Dave Canales breaks down the second week of OTAs | Carolina Panthers
text: Uh first of all, I want to wish luck to the Hurricanes tonight. Uh pretty exciting, you know, just the uh the championship environment and all that that's happening. We've been following it as a team uh throughout the series and um there's a couple hockey fans on our team and so I usually kind of quiet them down, ask everybody else, you know, where they play, you know what round they're in and but it's it's been great to follow that along. So wish them a lot of luck. >> Coach, uh just a couple thoughts on on the nickel corner. Seems like it'll be interesting battleh this summer. Uh, number one, how important is it for you to lock down the the slot with the, you know, arguably have two best quarterback quarterback duos in the league? And, uh, number two was Cory Thordon. How confident are you in uh, in his play and, you know, tip off by his interception today? >> Yeah, there are a lot of guys that um, that can help us in there. As you know, Trey Merik also plays the nickel spot in a certain package. Um, JC can go in there sometimes. Um, Cory's done a great job. You know, won the job at a certain point and Shaw Smith Wade knows our system like nobody else. And so, um, there's a couple of other younger guys too that uh that'll be competing in there. And that's the thing for us is is we want to make sure they know these are opportunities to compete to help our team. And we're open to whoever wants to do that by doing things right, showing up and making plays. >> Dave, did you hold out uh Brooks out of team? >> Yes. Uh, just a just a rest day. we have him on a on on a good rhythm of, you know, loading him up, getting some good work, and then just making sure we back off and continue to increase his load. Uh similar with uh Jaylen Phillips, uh Pat Jones, two other guys that we just were like, "Okay, in a in a scope of a week, and and how much volume we got yesterday, we got some really good work yesterday, we just had them take vet days. Today, they were working on the side, uh engaged in the huddle and all that, getting some conditioning. Um but, you know, it's it's uh even even in this time of year, you know, it's it's a lot of movement. It's a lot of speed out there and uh we just try to be smart with certain guys and make sure that the rhythm's right. >> Understanding it's very early, but what have you seen? What have been your initial assessments on Brooks? >> Yeah, JB's looked great. Um you know, in the run game certainly, but also in the past game, you know, half of his highlights when he was coming out are screen passes, wides, things down the field. Uh he has a great ability to catch the ball, track it, and and transition once he catches it. And so, uh just finding different packages and ways to get him involved in the offense. and um he's looked great so far. >> Does Robert Hunt also have a that day today? >> Yes, Rob. Rob's got some soreness. Um you know, the last two days we just brought him down a little bit and we'll get him back out there on Thursday, I think. Um but uh he's been doing an excellent job in there. Luke's doing great at the center spot, getting things coordinated um in there and I'm sure he really enjoys having Doo and Rob, you know, playing right next to him as you can imagine. But um yeah, that so we'll get them back rolling pretty soon. Dave, um, why did y'all sign Will Greer and what do you hope for him this year? >> Will's a guy that, you know, I evaluated when he came out and always loved his game. Fiery, um, aggressive style of play, big arm, accuracy, and just played with a lot of energy. Um, and so I've just kind of followed him and and tracked him, you know, all along this time. And he's been on a couple of other teams, bringing Kenny in. Uh, Will and Kenny were together in a QB room in Philly. So bringing some familiarity and then also just it's always good as you're building that quarterback room, bring guys in with experience who've been exposed to different systems, have seen defenses around the league so they they can add value. So, makes him a little taller. Trevor is another guy that's in the room that you've gotten to kind of know. What is it about his game that sticks out to you over the last, you know, 15 months you guys been together? >> Right. I mean I mean he's a he's a great player. He's elusive. He can do running back special teams. I mean he's he's been good for us. I mean he's a great player on and off the field in the locker room. He's like like I said, our running back room is so close. It makes it so awesome to see how we can get along with each other on and off the field. John, you seem to be doing quite a bit. I know today they held you out of team for workload purposes. Are you surprised at all about how much workload you've been able to handle? >> Um, no. I mean, because that roots back in my faith and I know that God is going to ultimately take control over everything that I do. I'm behind the scenes doing a lot of work to make sure that I can be able to handle that workload. and I'm just doing my doing my part, listening to the training staff, listening to the coaches, and following their plan for me and and it's been good so far. >> How do you keep from doing too, like you said, I know there's a plan to do too much too soon. >> Uh I mean I mean as as a football player, you can kind of know, but you know, like I said, just reverting back to their plan. We have GPS. We have all of that to track a lot of that stuff. So, um just following what they're playing, trusting them, trusting that they're they have my best interest, and it's been good. last year to sit and see how successful the running back group was with different guys coming in and out. How motivating has that been for you coming in now this year trying to get back off the field? >> I mean, it's obviously motivating just to see the the potential of of where we can go as a offense because we haven't even hit that peak yet in all phases, offense, defense, um special teams. So, the fact that that it's there and we can do that obviously gives us as a team a lot of joy. Um especially me coming back for me is like seeing that we can do that. um obviously makes it a lot of uh makes me more confident in in the coaching staff. >> How are you envisioning kind of yourself in that picture? >> Uh just doing what I can doing what I can do to help the team wherever that is. Um and just trusting the coaches plan wherever they put me. >> And going back to that word joy, teammates have said this when they see you out there, they've said it brings them a lot of joy. They've canal said the same thing. Have you been able to feel that from the rest of your team about how much they they just enjoy seeing you being out there playing football? >> Uh somewhat. Yeah. I just go out there and I'll be myself. Um I mean we we we all woke up today. I mean if there's no reason to be down, there's always a reason to be happy. Um and for me it's just I have a lot of reasons why I play the game. And for me is is is my father. So for me to get on that field and not be myself, not be happy, I feel like I'd be doing myself and him a disservice. Um, and so just to go out there and be able to play the game that I love every single day at the highest level and get to be out there with brothers and compete and have fun, you couldn't ask for anything better. >> How was your father? Sorry, my >> No, you're good. >> How was your father with you last season when it was >> um mentally? Um, any anytime I mean anytime I pray, anytime I do anything, I'm thinking of them. Um, and you know, just having a close-knit circle outside of the building, my my mom, my brother, my girlfriend. Um, just being able to be open with them and talk to them about problems that I have, and even just being open with my feelings to them. >> Jonathan, you guys have had a two pretty strict two back system under Canales. The third back hasn't really played a ton. When you factor that in and see how Rico was used and how Miles was used in concert with Tube over the last two years, how do you approach kind of that rotation right now or at least your your reps and how the system works? >> Right now, I'm just focused on OTAAS and and getting myself better. Um, when that comes that'll come, but just ultimately just trusting wherever they put me is is is the faith that they have in me. So, um, whether that be all the reps, whether that be none of the reps, you know, just trusting in their plan, >> you got to be kind of a fly on the wall to watch Chuba have to kind of take a step back and and kind of endure that type of adversity. From your point of view, how did he handle that whole situation? >> Um, I mean, he could tell you himself, he's big in his faith. Um, and we kind of, um, how do you say it? We kind of go back and forth with each other, ideas and and stuff like that. and just seeing his faith um it it pushes my faith a lot because I know what he's been through um on and off the field and that just becomes with how close you are as as brothers in the locker room. So just to see him revert back to his faith has been awesome. >> Said we hear from athletes that get injured that say it can kind of be isolating. You were here a lot last year. What was your experience in this locker room as you went through what you went through? >> Um honestly I didn't feel isolated at all. I mean I still felt welcome to the team. You know I was still here in meetings at practice every single day. um just building that relationship with every single one of the teammates, offense, defense, um anybody on the team, you know, it's just it's it feels good to be able to do that. And now whenever you come back, it it feels like a full circle moment. >> Jonathan, how close to 100% are you health-wise? And how has it been mentally getting back out there? Like have you had any hesitation with your knees or anything? >> Um I wouldn't say any hesitations. I mean, obviously getting back out there, it's been a little over a year before since I've went against the defense essentially. Um, just getting back to that. Um, obviously takes some time to get used to, but it's been good so far and I'm just trusting in their plan and like I said, the practices so far has been pretty good. >> On that note, Nick Scon mentioned how getting to face you for the first time this year, realizing how fast you are. Like, have you hit your full speed yet? And what did it feel like when you finally got to hit it again? >> Uh, I don't think I've hit my full speed yet, but uh, it feels good being back out there, man. It it it like I said, just trusting in my journey that God has for me and not looking at other people's journeys, other people's injuries, and be like, "Oh, he came back at this time." Just trusting in my process. Um, and and really making sure that I feel 100% and that I'm doing what's best for myself in terms of rehab to get myself back out there. you have certain benchmarks you're looking forward to hitting this this summer and and into the fall like first day in pads, first uh you know preseason game, first first hit you take, that sort of thing. >> Uh I mean right now right now I'm solely focused on OTAAS. I'm I'm I'm really focused on stacking good days, stacking days where I can be out there with my teammates and uh just getting better. Jonathan, I know they track all sorts of metrics. What is your top speed? >> Uh, share that. >> I don't I don't I don't know my full full top speed. I know in college I don't even remember that speed, but I I don't know yet. >> It's up there. >> Faster than faster than >> Did you get a lot of feedback? They posted a video of you yesterday kind of streaking through traffic. Have you gotten a lot I know I know you've gotten a lot of feedback on social media, good and bad, but when they post something like that, do you get to see kind of folks getting excited about your return? >> Um, yes and no. I I try not to pay attention to it cuz, you know, I I really don't too much care what people have to say. Um, I'm focused on my journey that that involves the people that are around me, which is in this building, and then my close family. So the I don't I don't too much see it, but it is what it is.

title: Anthony Weaver on Defensive Standouts During OTAs | Baltimore Ravens
text: I've got some shade. How's everybody doing? Is it all right? >> So, how would you describe >> You said you're still here? >> I'm still here. >> [laughter] >> How would you describe Jesse Buggs' coaching style? >> He is a cool customer. Yeah, he is very detailed in in his approach to both teaching to the team, talking to us as coaches, never flustered, right? Which which I appreciate. Because obviously like your your team and your staff is going to reflect how you act. So, I expect us to be very cool, calm, and collected regardless of the situation, and be at our best. >> How's that working relationship gone with you guys now? Obviously, kind of a tag team in the defense >> Yeah, it's great. It's great. Jesse, like I said, he's he's easy, man. He's very personal, he listens. He's not one of those guys who's constantly barking orders. He has his ideas and how he wants it to look, but he's always looking for information to try to make it as best as we possibly can. So, he's been great. He's been super collaborative. I feel super blessed every day I walk into the building. >> You guys have Zion who's high on you guys for What have you seen from him in the days and his kind of everything is advertised? >> Yeah, he's he's like you said, he's as advertised. The the physical nature that he plays with even out here without pads, you see it. How hungry he is to just want to grow and get better. He's constantly asking questions, so couldn't be more excited about a player than I am about that kid. Because you see just how bad he wants to be great. And inevitably, through repetition without being a mother skill, he'll get there. >> With Trey Edmunds, what why do you think he is so effective and just consistently getting better? >> Yeah, he is a pro. Like when you The way you see him move and operate and just his approach to work, he is as detailed a player as I've been around. So, the results obviously speak for themselves, but I think what people don't see is just how much work goes into that. How he takes care of his body, whether it's a walk-through, um whatever it is, he is trying to operate as if like it's the most important play in the history of football. And that's why he's had the success he's had. >> Anthony, Keiondre Jackson, the guy who had, you know, kind of made his mark on special teams out of Notre Dame today. And you know more here on Trip. What stands out to you about him on defense? >> Yeah, he's the same guy every day. He's going to be full speed. You're never going to find a clip where you stop at you stop at the end of the play and he's not around the ball carrier. And usually the ball finds energy, right? And he's a juice guy. He brings it on teams and he's had a success on on that side of the ball, and hopefully we can get that translated a little bit more to defense this year. >> Hey, Trev Sermon, I know you weren't here last year, but you kind of came on at the end of last year and played a couple of spots inside, outside. What do you see of him so far? >> I remember Trev as a rookie. And his growth and development from where I remember him to where he is now has just been astronomical. And it's a credit to him how hard he's worked. His his position coach, Tyler Santucci, I think is outstanding. Matt O'Donnell, so I am I'm just incredibly proud of that kid. Just knowing like where he was as a rookie and how green he was and just how much growth there's been this schematically, overall like offensive information, like there's just been leaps and bounds of growth, man. And again, I just look really look forward to this see how that shakes out for all those guys. >> Anthony, three weeks of OTAs, obviously not traditional like hitting football. But what what do you feel you've learned about this defense? What do you feel you've learned about your group? >> They care. They care. And and they all got a little bit of a chip. Right? You know they You know that there's a there's a history we've kind of we're kind of chasing defensively in this place. And I think everybody to a man knows we fell short of that a year ago, and we want to make that right. So, when they're in the building and truthfully, probably a lot of times they're not in the building. Like, they're trying to do what's required to make that happen. And it's a daily chase. But, we're just going to keep trying to do the next right thing. >> Anthony, we we know OTAs are voluntary, but we haven't seen Marlon Humphrey uh these last 4 weeks. How much, in a general sense, how much interaction have you had with him this spring? And what are you looking from him with him coming off of a season by his own admission wasn't the kind of season he wanted to have? >> Yeah. Mar- Marlon's one of those guys, again, he is a one-of-one, right? He is unique. So, the one thing I know with my experience with Marlon is when he is here, he is going to be full speed and all in. It's all he knows. You see it on tape. He takes the ball away constantly. He's he's that type of player. So, even though he's not here, I have no doubt that he's doing the things required to make to make that jump from he- from his play a year ago. So, admittedly, I know there's been some disappointment there with how he played for himself. But, I know we can help him reach whatever standard he wants to hold for himself. >> Anthony, last something here in 2023, Broderick Washington >> Yeah. >> the defense Um last year, maybe not the level that played a lot of guys In OTAs, what have you seen out of >> Simple answer. Yes. See it every day. Communicates. Captains our defense. Gets guys lined. And he's playing at an elite level and speed. There's some guys, when they operate, it almost looks like the game's in slow motion. When he's out there right now, I feel that way. So, I look forward to him shutting up some doubters. >> Anthony, you mentioned Marlon. Now here, we've seen a bit more of a T.J. Tampa. What's kind of impressed you during his approach to these practices? >> Yeah. TJ's just been like everybody else. Like he he's in here every day working to get better. His rapport with our DB coaches has been excellent with Mike Mickens. He's trying to go out there and apply the technique and fundamentals that they're trying to to give him and then he just works. And he's one of those guys where if he does if a negative play does happen, he's not a guy that that that lowers his head and gets in the tank. He just goes on to the next play, which is all we're trying to get all our guys to do. Right? So, um couldn't be more pleased with TJ and and his ceiling and where he can go. But, uh the one thing I do know is he's going to work to to reach that ceiling. >> I'll take two more for coach. >> Coach, how about freshman Colaeus? Someone a little closer to your age. >> Yeah, you know, we wanted to bring in somebody that I could relate to a little bit more. >> Uh same sense in music, you know, same taste in music. No. Uh you guys know Colaeus. He is I've said it countless times, he's a force multiplier. He's one of those guys that doesn't just make our our defensive line better. He makes our defense better. He makes our team better. And anytime you can you can inject that type of energy and leadership into a locker room, that's a win. So, I love the guy to death. Yeah, he is um he is like a human computer. Right? Like when he starts spitting out like offensive information and plays from his past, it's like he's got like this Rolodex of plays in his head. Like he's just like he's almost like he has a photographic memory. So, I look forward to all the things that we're going to that he's going to do with our offense. Even going against them, they do so many things right now from a from a cadence variation. Um some of their shifts and motions that that cause problems and make us have long conversations up there in the defensive staff room. So, anytime that's happening, you know they're doing the right things on that side of the ball. >> Coach, what do you see in from Mike Green and and the pass rush you got after it here today. In general, I know it's OTAs, it's early. What are you seeing from this pass rush? >> Yeah, I I I got to love that room, right? I love Mike Green. Uh a year ago when I was in Miami, Mike was one if not like he was top one, two on our board in terms of outside backer. So, to be here now and have the opportunity to kind of get my hands on him and work with him a little bit as long as and as well as coach Bauer who's been outstanding. Um super excited. There's so many players and I made this cut up for him where I showed him just how close he was to potentially having like a double-digit sack season. So, it's not an ability thing. We need the corresponding rush to I mean [snorts] the corresponding coverage to help out. But, he he is milliseconds away from having double-digit sacks and and we're going to do everything we can try to make that happen this year. >> All right, thank you, coach. >> Yeah, no problem. All right, guys.

text: [music] N feel. >> [music] >> Welcome to June inside the collective. It's the second here in 2026 and week three of voluntary Ravens organized team activities. [laughter] >> I mean, we like your polo, but >> yeah, you hate to paint. Um >> what's that? >> What's going on? I missed that. >> He's showing off his golf polo, Cole. >> Yeah, it froze. It was just beautiful weather. They had some fans there. Uh the only shame of it is I have to end the day talking to you guys. But beyond that, [laughter] it was uh really fun to uh get to see things and yeah, I think that was the highlight for me guys. One, just watching Declan Doyle in action on the field. I mean, he is into anything. He's high energy. He's vocal. You see him, you know, he bounces from conversation to conversation. You see him talking to one side of the field talking to Mark Andrews. 30 seconds later, you see him locked with Lamar Jackson. Then you see him talking to Derk Henry. And it's just he's constant. He's high energy. He's hands-on. Um he has a clear idea, you can tell, of how he wants things done. Detail oriented. And then after, you know, on the microphone after uh practice, it's just, you know, just composed, smart. You could just tell he's just an impressive dude. And guys, I hate to paint with a wide brush here. I think some of the groupings can be, you know, >> the narratives or whatever compared to Shawn McVey and like, you know, young coaches are all compared to Shawn McVey because they're young whiz Kid geniuses, but man, it's tough not to draw the comparison after listening to him. And it's not just I can't say I was around McVey a ton, but you've I've been around him enough at these meetings and at different things. I've seen enough press conferences and and it's just it's not just it's always thinking. He talks fast. He thinks fast. And you know, you have all that brainiac kind of stuff, but then you have a charisma and a swagger about him. And I see all those things in in Declan Doyle. I don't want to overreact, you know, it was just a a news conference after practice. We talked to Weaver and Lavine as well who are both impressive dudes who we who we know already because they've been around. But yeah, Doyle seems to have really made an impression and just some of the things he says just say, "Yeah, I'm I want to stress the players now. I'm to put them in stressful situations now so we're ready to handle it." And right now, okay, penalties, you don't get, you know, you don't get too uh worked up, but they better stop come the season. And uh he's been, you know, there's been no easing into this. He's high energy, he's thorough, and he wants these guys covering all the bases uh right away. Um and I I just think it's impressive. I just think everything about him, I heard amazing things. You know, I I just my understanding was you just absolutely blew team officials away in the interview process. Like you heard words like savant and and stuff like that. And um it seems guys are enjoying things and and there'll be a there'll be a kind of a rust period. Uh you know that's going to happen with a new coordinator and he this is his first year calling plays. Uh but I think the Ravens got themselves a pretty good one here. I couldn't have been any more impressed today. I think it's mind-blowing to think he's 30 years old. Like he's he's younger than some of these guys out there. And uh I think the big thing that stands out based on how he's been described at practice is, and you kind [clears throat] of hit on it, the command like to be that young and that inexperienced as an offensive com coordinator. And to have the confidence and, you know, the the the control of a veteran coach, I think, is a really really good sign. And it's it's really kind of, you know, been this whole youth movement that we've seen with this coaching staff by having, you know, a young head coach and Jesse Mentor, a young offensive coordinator in Declan Doyle. Um, I think it's it's just a great sign of things to come. And when you go through the comments, you know, the big thing that I've noticed is every time Declan Doyle's talked to the media, the big thing he's talked about is communication. It's kind of been the non-stop go-to. and pre-nap penalties, you know, little things like that that we've seen it a number of times where guys are running the wrong routes and key situations causing hiccups. And that communication being kind of the tone setter under Declan Doyle, I think, is a big piece cuz, you know, we talk about it all the time. These guys are NFL players. You know, they know they know the basics of know the snap count. like this isn't necessarily groundbreaking coaching stuff, but how you set the tone with how you have guys communicating, how you stress those pieces, that's how you avoid those things when you when you're playing professional football. So, I think it's really interesting to see that. But my big takeaway is just to be that young and not in control. um especially in coming into an an offense that has been, you know, at times historic, like quite literally historic. A two-time MVP quarterback. Um a rushing attack that has set multiple records in the last five years. Um and he's not even phased by it. He just coming in with his own vision and uh he's making it his own. I think it's a great sign. >> Yeah. I mean, one other thing, guys, like it's a shame you can't talk about current the current coaching staff without it taking being taken as a shot at the previous one. That's not my intention. I don't there's no thinly veiled shots here. But he's so detailoriented and you can just tell they're going to work on finding every possible edge. And that was something Ben Johnson was known for, being creative, finding edge. Shawn Payeyton, the same thing. Two of his mentors. And like today they were working a lot on cadence and how many times have we talked about that uh over the years and I know this was something Todd Monkin worked on last year too. So it's not like the first time we're talking about this but we are in OTAAS and you could tell that was a clear focus. Um and I think it should give people confidence that look this is they're going to you know cover everything like this is going to be a wellprepared offense. That doesn't mean there's not going to be some speed bumps. That doesn't mean there's not going to be a learning curve, but they will be [snorts] for the scenarios. They will work on a ton of different things and be very very detailoriented. And unfortunately, I think, you know, again, I'm saying don't, this isn't a shot at the previous coaching staff, but we've seen little things in the past sort of hold this team back at key moments. And uh that's the stuff you need to work on now. any advantage you can get and using cadence is certainly one of them uh should absolutely be explored. They have a lot of talent on offense but that doesn't that's not always the beall end all. So um it's good to see even now in a in a practice in the first week of June that they're focused on such things and and it's been such a priority. Here's a snippet from earlier this afternoon on exactly that Declan talking cadence >> way that we talk about all the time like trying to stress the defense and uh that can be you know personnels you play out of formations you play out of cadence is another element uh that I think a lot of times gets overlooked and and uh not worked enough because uh a lot of times guys in college they're coming from these faster systems where they're not utilizing cadence as much. Um, for us it's really important that it's a weapon that we can use and uh it's the one thing that that we know as an offense that the defense doesn't know and so we need to make it an advantage for ourselves. Um, and part of that too is like you know we have to stress our guys. We have to work on different cadences. We got to do things in practice. You're going to tow that line. Um, at times you know you're going to see pre-nap fouls and really by the time we get to the season that needs to disappear. That that's unacceptable in any snap. if we have a pre-nap foul, uh, we're putting ourselves in a in a position that's a very controllable stat. Um, and so we want to see that improve. We've seen that improve as we've gone. Uh, just the pre- snap operation. I think that's been a huge emphasis u, not only from myself, but like as Jesse talks to the team and can talk to the offense, he can piggyback on that. The pre- snap operation on both sides of the ball, uh, that being really like paramount that we can master that. >> Oh, I think that's music to our resident offensive line guru's ears there. unacceptable pre- snap fouls and this is the time of year obviously to make those mistakes pre- pads but once uh once it's it's season time Cole obviously that's that's an area that um I don't I mean would you have the red zone woes were bigger than pre- snap penalties last year but uh certainly something that with cadence that goes hand inand this time of year getting that all fleshed out >> well I I think another thing you got to [clears throat] excuse me consider is they're bringing back the pre-nap king penalty guy in John Simpson who he's been and I don't even mean to disrespect the guy, but I mean that's been part of him starting football games in the last couple years is pre- snap penalties. He's he's been top five in the league every year in the last three years, including his year with the Ravens in 2023. Um so his last two years with the Jets, he he was fault or at fault um with a number of false [snorts] starts. And uh it's going to be an issue. It's going to be something that they're going to have to work through. Um, you know, if you look at it statistically, it was an issue that appeared to be Ronnie Stanley's. Um, but I think almost half of his pre- snap penalties came in one week one Kansas City Chiefs game where the refs were very much trying to make a point. Uh, so I I thought they got a little bit better last year. Um, it wasn't as noticeable, at least with the pre-nap stuff. Uh but you know with with teams that use a ton of motion the big thing and this was a big thing under Greg Roman was how much he was swapping his packages as well. They went from 22 next snap 11 next snap 12 guys coming subbing in and out. We remember back, you know, they were always snapping the ball with about 2 seconds left on the play co clock. That's where you start to run in when you're speeding everything up because you're spending your your 40 seconds subbing. That becomes an issue. we saw that a little less under um uh under Todd Monkin. So, it'll be interesting to see how Declan Doyle manages that. What's his flavor look like? And I I keep I I kind of say this every week and I'm sure people are getting sick of it, but we still don't really know what truly to expect from a Declan Doyle offense. We can make some assumptions based on some of the stuff he's done. You can look at some of the stuff um that Payton does. You can look at some of the stuff that uh Ben Johnson has done, but we just don't know what is Declan Doyle's offense. Again, can grab some things. Uh but I think that's going to be the most interesting thing. How does he use motions relative to tendencies across the league? How does he use certain packages? I think it's going to be 11 12 dominant. I don't think we see a fullback this year, but who knows, right? Um so it's going to be interesting. Jeff Jerry de Monaco hit us with you already gave your impressions of Declan Doyle. You're very clear about that. Jerry says, "A lot of talk about the players, but what observations do you have about the new coaching staff? What coaches have stood out during OTAAS? Can you think of anybody outside of Declan, whether it's a non-coordinator or you've already mentioned, you know, Weaver and Lavine, the familiarity there with with those two guys that are, you know, have already had previous stints with the organization as players and in this case coaches. Who else has stood out throughout OTAAS? [clears throat] >> I think Leadford. Maybe it's because I've watched him closer because I think that's kind of one of the biggest stories of this off seasonason. Um the hiring of Dwayne Leadford and what he could do to help that offensive line take the next step. So very high energy guy, very hands-on guy, uh communicating a lot. It's quick to the line of scrimmage after they run a play to go over things with his guys. Um that's that's a guy that really has uh stood out uh to me. Um but it's a different group, man. It's a lot of young, really young coaches and you know it's all these guys are wearing the same sort of warm-up gear and coaching gear.
