Um, and that was the case in in this instance where um you know, it got to a certain point where we looked at uh you know, what the trade details were and we asked ourselves, okay, you know, do we hold here? um regardless of you know how you know because of how emotionally right it felt um or do we ultimately make a decision that that you know we think has a a huge benefit you know to the team in both the short um you know and long term you know I'd always told myself that if you know we were ever in a position where we were going to trade miles three things would have to be true number one it would have to have short and long-term benefits number two as part of the the trade paid a young costc controlled star at a premium position would have to be included. And the third piece is that there would have to be premium draft capital. Um, and there's a very small set of, you know, deals that really satisfy those constraints. So, when it got to the point with our negotiations with the Rams when, you know, all those things were satisfies, it really, you know, caused us to to take a step back and and and think about, you know, really think about the decision. Um, you know, Jared Verse, he's a obviously a huge part of this return for us. Um, you know, Jared is an outstanding football player. Uh, former defensive rookie of the year, two-time original ballot Pro Bowler. Um, he's a perfect DNA match for our attacking front. Um, he's really a terror in both phasers, excuse me, both phases, both as a, you know, a run defender and a pass rusher. And we are really, really excited to add him to our team. um he allows us to continue to play defense as a high level, which has been our standard over the past several seasons. Um and we're really excited to to welcome him into the organization. Um so we're excited about this transaction. Um it wasn't something that we anticipated certainly coming into this year or coming into the spring or quite honestly coming out of the draft. Um but it's a great opportunity for our team and I know there are a ton of questions. Um so I'll open it up. I guess why now? And do you regret not having made this when Miles asked to be traded after uh 24? >> Yeah, no, no regrets, Scott. And in terms of the why now, the why now is just honestly the the opportunity was too great. Um it wasn't something it wasn't like a plan A going into the offseason. Quite honestly, we would have operated differently if it was. Uh but sometimes things come across your path that you're just you're not expecting and you can't be so dogmatic in your strategy and planning that you can't adjust and be flexible to great opportunities. >> Were you able to were you able to have conversations with Miles leading up into this moment like meaningful conversations leading up into this? >> You say and let me just for clarification KM regarding the trade or just more generally? >> In general like I guess both. >> Yeah. No, both like you know M like Miles um Miles was a good communicator throughout the spring. We obviously talked through the coaching search, free agency um before the draft. He was good in terms of um you know sharing his travel plans in the offseason, things like that. So that was all very very normal as he's been accustomed to later in his career. Um we did not blindside Miles with the news yesterday. Um, obviously he's a he's a uh was a welltenured member of the organization, someone that, you know, we expect to retire Brown. Um, so he was made aware about a week ago it was a possibility. Um, and that's, you know, that's that's a courtesy that, you know, that obviously we owe him. Um, so the communication was good with him. So, you did not consider Miles's absence, travel plans, ghosting, a protest to to get up to to lead the team. >> Yeah, he he didn't ghost. And and and Tony, no, not at all. I mean, you know, Miles is Miles's offseason ritual is pretty consistent the past couple years. Um, and Miles was good in terms of communicating with us throughout the spring. So, no, I I know there's been a lot of conspiracy theories with that type of narrative, but um you know, that that had zero impact on the trade. Andrew, going back to the the contract restructuring, whatever you want to call it, in the offseason, when you did that, did you you've talked about flexibility, >> but did you ever think at that point that you were going to, you know, you got past June 1st that this was this was a distinct possibility or >> No, I mean, like I'd like to sit here and say it was some grandm, but it really wasn't. What it did do is honestly probably because of a lot that was reported. Um that is what originally caused LA to to to reach out and check in and we said hey look he wasn't he wasn't available to their credit they were really really persistent um and then really things kind of picked up after the draft. Were >> you able to like explain maybe provide further clarity on why the date was moved back because I mean it ultimately benefited you in terms of you know salary cap. Yeah, I don't talk about our contract management strategies as you know, Daniel. I understand the curiosity with it. Um, you know, it's one of those situations where probably the truth is a lot more boring than you all think, but I'm not going to comment on our our strategy. >> Andrew, >> in terms of fans, people thinking that this move means you guys are tanking. Um, what what can you tell the fans about that? And then also like a correlary to that would be uh does this mean that Denzel could possibly be on the trading block now or can you address that? >> I guess I'd say two things. I'd say number one, um all of our goals are still in front of us. You know, we have um you know, an excellent defense with with really good players and on three levels and um you know, Jared, he's he's an outstanding. He's one of the best players in the league. Um and so we're excited to to have him as part of our team. Um to the second part of your question, I I just I guess I'd maybe um clarify your your your line of question, Mary Kay, in the sense that like we weren't Miles wasn't on the training block. We weren't auctioning him off. Um this is not something that was was a primary consideration going into the spring. >> Miles indicated to you open to being tra? >> No, there was no there was no like, you know, trade request or anything like that. you know, Dan. Um, obviously you talked through it a little bit earlier because he did have the no trade clause and obviously he was he was he was pleased with LA, but that wasn't the primary consideration. >> Um, he wasn't on the block, you weren't auctioning him off. Were if they were there have been reports that this was the only team that you seriously engaged in in talks, why not open up the bidding and and try to to get a few more picks out of it? >> Uh, that wasn't the goal. That wasn't the goal of Miles. And uh probably what I mentioned on the onset, um if we were to trade Miles, it's a very narrow universe of deals that satisfy it. Um you know, everyone wants to have a Miles Garrett on their team, but you know, not everyone can afford that that that acquisition cost in terms of players, you know, picks and dollars and so um yeah, that was not the that was not the that was not the intent of any of it. Andrew, you can >> let me go here first and I'll come back to >> go back to Mary K's question asking maybe some of the other veterans. I mean, there's been so much change obviously for them these last few months now with Miles gone too. Like do you plan on having any conversations with them or do you feel like they know like hey our goals are are the same? Like do you feel that there's that sentiment there after a move like this? >> Actually change is common place in the NFL and um roster turnover is common place in the NFL. Um, you know, we have good communication with all of our players. Um, you know, we obviously for a move of this magnitude. Um, you know, we communicate directly with them. So, you know, they they hear it from us and they understand everything that's involved. Um, but we have a good group of guys in that locker room and and we're really excited about the court. >> Go ahead, Tony. >> Some some might argue that you got you received more for Travis Hunter than you did for Miles Garrett. Even if you don't acknowledge that, do you think Miles's age was the one factor that you couldn't get more. >> Oh, I tell you what, we're very pleased with the return we got, Tony. I mean, you know, I think for us, um, you know, getting a player of Jared's caliber, um, you know, plus the pick considerations, um, you know, was was excellent. It's, um, you know, something that we did certainly didn't expect coming into the >> Let me go Zach and then I'll go to you, Darl. When teams called in February 25, what did you tell teams then? >> No. >> Do you have a follow? >> Yeah. >> You just weren't you weren't doing >> Yeah. I was like, "Yeah, we're not we're not interested in training Miles." >> Look at where the Rams are and their I guess expectations, if you will. Um, a lot of people, you know, say those picks aren't as good because likely going to be in the back end uh of the rounds and and therefore it it wasn't enough even with you know Jerry just what would you say to that uh that you know um the first the second and the third likely could very well end up in the back end of those rounds. >> Yeah, I think that I'd say a couple things to that, Darl. I'd say number one um you know the combination of of picks and players is uh we think it's excellent. um we're really pleased with it short short and long term. You know, I'd say the the second piece of that in terms of um you know, us today on June 2nd, you know, assuming where we know those picks, like you know, we all probably have to have a little bit of humility because we just don't know how the season's going to unfold. And I probably the third part is, you know, realistically any team that is making a move for a player of Miles's cal caliber, um you know, they feel like they're in their their window or they are in their window. um you know there's there's unlikely to be a deal out there where you know you're getting a a top expected top five pick out of it. Um you know which is why the volume of picks um and particularly the inclusion of Jared was incredibly important. >> You said that you didn't have this on your card. So, I'm just wondering, is there a moment you can pinpoint where it went from being no, is this ever going to happen to, oh, this is seeming like it is? >> The inclusion of Jared in the deal. >> Let me go Fred and I'll come back to you, Tony. >> Hey, Andrew. I know quarterback's always a topic, but you look at Miles obviously his biggest asset. you see any way get the first pick how that can help you ultimately solve the quarterback issue? >> Yeah, I I I understand and respect, you know, the question. Um we're we're way too premature to figure out how we're going to deploy that that asset. Um we've got an entire season to play. Um we've got a group of players that we're really excited to see this fall. Um, and you know, we'll we'll deal with 2027 and 2027. >> Isn't that you know, one of the reasons maybe you delay a little bit to see if you could use that as a chip to get yourself in position? >> No, I I I'd say honestly it's independent of any present circumstance, Fred. Like, you know, the return with Jared plus um the resources we just felt was too great to turn down. >> I said Tony next then I'll go. Todd Mon came out strongly against pursuing Brendan source. What is your uh attitude toward the participation in the supplemental draft if he is in it? >> Yeah, we haven't had a supplemental draft in a while or I guess a couple years now. Um no different than we do every year. We'll do the work on all the prospects and then we'll make the appropriate decision for the organization. >> Andrew, let me go Spencer and I'll come back to Um, you mentioned that you have season to play. How do you kind of square with I guess mostly the fan base who see this trade and maybe feel like it's a concession of 2026 and maybe setting Todd Lincoln up for failure and all that and just kind of looking more towards the future. >> Yeah. You know, Spencer, I think I understand the, you know, emotional reaction of, you know, Miles, look, we've we've known him since he's 21 years old coming out of Texas A&M. Um, we've seen him grow up here and everything like that, and he's accomplished really great things for us on the field. Um, and so there's always, uh, an emotional tie for someone who's going to be one of the franchise, you know, the franchise great. So, certainly understand that. Um, you know, in terms of the second part of your question, um, you know, don't see it that way at all. We're we're we're really excited about Jared. We're really excited about this defense. Um, I know Monk's really excited about, uh, you know, bringing Jared into the to the organization. Um, but, you know, everything's everything's still right in front of us in terms of that regard. >> Yeah. Go ahead, Daniel. >> Think that you could have gotten a similar return for for Miles last year, correct? >> I I don't know, D. like we didn't shop them. >> I was ask like do you think the messaging and maybe your actions have been maybe a little bit inconsistent when you talk about you know adding talent and still wanting to be competitive and then going away and trading you know the best player you know arguably in the NFL. Um do you think your messaging and maybe your actions have been a little bit inongruous over the past few years? >> I'd say this look I didn't expect to be up here talking about a Miles Garrett trade Daniel. Um, you know, this is not my favorite thing to do because I, like I said, I didn't have it on the the bingo card and I realized how strong I've been with with Miles. But, you know, the reality is when you have an opportunity to to do something that um has strong both short and long-term benefits like we have to be have to be flexible with it. So, you know, we're real excited from a team perspective. >> Two questions. >> Let me go back. >> Two part questions. One, I know all trades are tough. Where does this rank in all the moves you've made in terms of emotional time? >> Uh, I don't know that I could rank him. Obviously, like it's tough because it's Miles and I've known him for so long. Um, but the benefit of that is, you know, look, Miles will be a part of, you know, many of our lives beyond his playing career. You know, it's it's um it's maybe more of a see you later as opposed to a goodbye to sound maybe a little bit corny. Um, so like that that part is is tough. Um, but they're all tough because these are human beings. They're not they're not commodities. Um, and and their lives change. >> The second part value of moving him post to first now versus let's say a couple weeks where you know a package from one team and now potentially shop around. Is it just package too good to see what other organization could offer? >> I don't I I guess I don't quite understand the question. saying what's the Do you mind repeating it so I can try and get it right? >> So I understand moving him at June 1st the money, >> but if you weren't willing to shop them around, could you have potentially looked later down the road in the summer? Like why now yesterday versus maybe in two weeks when in theory you could potentially shop him around to get a better offer versus what the Rams gave? >> So I think it goes back to two things that I said previously. We weren't shopping him around. Um we that was not the intention to trade him. And then number two, um the characteristics that I described in like any deal in which Miles Gear would be included like it fell at our feet. Um you know, and Jared's a big part of that along with um you know, the draft pick resources. So it's it's really as simple as that. Go ahead, Mary K. >> Two. First of all, on a follow up on Denzel. Last year, um when Miles was on radio at the Super Bowl, I I talked to Denzel and he mentioned that if Miles were traded, it would make him kind of question what his sit own situation is here. So I'm wondering um have you guys heard from Denzel and have reassurance that he's fully and committed to the program in the aftermath of this? >> So I'd say number one um I think it's probably most uh appropriate for Denzel to speak for himself. Uh number two, um Denzel's been great throughout the offseason. His communication's been good. Um he's a big part of the team. Um and we like him a lot. he's still playing at a really high level. Um that doesn't change with this transaction. >> And then the follow that I have there is that how has Jared Hurst reacted to the trade, you know, going from a Super Bowl contender to a team that's building towards that right now. >> He was very excited yesterday when we talked to him talked to him on the phone. Um he's ready to go. I think um he's really excited to play in this scheme. Um I think maybe some of you already know he's from Dayton, Ohio, still his sister still here and everything like that, but um he's gonna be fun. He's he's a ton of energy now. He'll there'll be some colorful quotes for everybody in this room. >> Well, the quarterback still remains the elephant in the room. Whether or not you have the solution in house right now is still in question. If it is not, can you still win and achieve the goal of finding that franchise quarterback because obviously the more games you win, the lower you are in the draft. Yeah, Darl, I I don't love dealing with hypotheticals, especially about the draft when we're in May and haven't played a played a season. All I can tell you is like we're focused on the guys that are in the building. Um they've had a really nice spring. I'm really pleased with Monk and the staff. Um and we're excited about the season. in terms of when he gets as a linebacker with the Rams who was defensive lineman in college. >> Uh so expect him to get here, you know, assuming no, you know, travel issues. Um oh, I guess today's Tuesday, Tuesday evening today, this evening. Um and then you guys should get a chance to to see him and meet him tomorrow. Um, you know, I think the blurring of outside linebacker and defensive end, that's really what you're seeing in today's today's game. Um, he's a perfect fit as a uh as an edge rusher for our defense. >> You feel you're thin depthwise defensively? >> I think you could add depth everywhere, honestly, Tony. Like we like, you know, the roster building process, it's it's literally every day. And if we can find, you know, guys that we think can upgrade uh at any spot, we'll look to do so. >> Kind of in the middle between, you know, the roster, you've gotten the roster so much younger and we've talked about that versus doing complete rebuild, right, which would require might require trading guys like Miles. Do you feel at all stuck in the middle trying to win, but also trying to redo this roster? >> I don't and I I guess I maybe go back to what I mentioned this spring. I don't I don't necessarily agree with the implicit assumption that younger means worse. >> You have talked about what who Miles was to this franchise, this organization, >> and obviously your your goal is on the football field primarily, but you lose a face of the franchise, a staple in the community. So, where do you feel like the roster stands in terms of that kind of player? you have those kinds of players to kind of step in and and fill those shoes of the role that Miles held not just in the locker room but around Northeast Ohio. >> Yeah, I'd say this. I think one of the toughest things in professional sports is when players who everyone knows their name locally leave and new ones that they don't know the names of, you know, take their roles. I think, you know, probably could have asked me the same question um, you know, with Nick Chub last year, right? Um, and you know, we saw, you know, Quinn Sean come in and and and make himself a household name in Northeast Ohio or, you know, David and Jooku this year. And, you know, we have Harold Fannon. So, I I think that look, professional sports can be cyclical at times. And, um, that's always tough, you know, in these in these moments. Um, but we are really excited about um, you know, a number of the players that we have in the locker room that I think our fans will either continue to get more familiarity with or gain familiarity with over the upcoming season. >> You Andrew, you talked about you talked a lot about Jared and how Jared was sort of the piece that made you do the deal. How long have you sort of I don't know if covet's the right word, but how much is how long have you sort of been kind of zeroed in on him as a player that you guys really liked? I mean, does this go all the way back to the 24 draft? I mean, just what is it about him that made him just such a a swing piece in this? >> Um, you know, we liked him a lot coming out. Um, you know, we weren't uh you know, really in position to take him, you know, obviously the year that he came out because he came out in 24. um you know that I would say that probably had less of a bearing on this you know this transaction but you know what made it really easy is he's like an outstanding player at 25 years old at a very very hard to find position. So um yes like we're excited to have him specifically but it's you know it's not necessarily like this was like a you know a two-year focal point in the making. >> You mentioned it being an emotional obviously decision for you guys as an organization. Can you speak at all to the emotions maybe shared with Miles and what his emotions kind of were like in in understanding what was kind of happening? >> You know, I I think it's more appropriate for Miles to comment on that, but what I can share is that um it was it just was a really good it was a really good meeting. It was bittersweet is maybe the way I would describe it. Um but I I' I'd probably let him comment on it more than me. Go ahead, Tony. clearly remember Todd at his introduction saying Miles was one of the reasons this job was attractive to him. >> So what was his reaction when you told him you're not going to have the best player in the league? >> Yeah, you know, Todd was excited in terms of the deal. He um you know, he he he understood the short and long-term, you know, benefits. Um again, it's not about, you know, not wanting a Miles Garrett on your team. Um but he's very excited to have Jared. He's very excited to have um you know the additional resources. Um and Todd's really smart like he he he understands the the short and long-term ramifications. And I think, you know, one of the things that's that's unique about this deal relative to, you know, maybe the other non QB like superstar deals that come out is that we made a trade with with, I guess, you know, multiple um, you know, players and picks. And usually when you make these trades, you're completely trading off present for future. and to get a player like Jared in the deal where the defense still maintains its excellence. Um, you know, that was really attractive to us. >> What do you think Jared's upside potential as an edge rusher is? I see, you know, he went from like four and a half to seven and a half. Where do you see that going? And do you feel like with what you have on the team now, uh, you can accomp accomplish the pressure and the pass rush that you want to generate? >> Absolutely. Um, I, you know, I wouldn't sit here and, you know, put a cap on any players, uh, ceiling. I just know the the list of of players that, um, have been defensive rookie of the year and original ballot Pro Bowlers in their first two seasons is very small. >> Been more of a pressures guy than a than a sax guy um, so far in his in his career. What is what are what is your philosophy on the relationship between those two um, statistical categories? Yeah, I'd comment less on that and just say this is a guy who really gets after the quarterback really well. >> Good. >> All right. >> Thank you.

title: Jordan Love: ‘It’s always nice to get back together as a team’
text: How much dad strength do you have now? >> I'm right. >> I got a lot. I'm benching like 400 now. >> Diapers. Okay. Got your treasure technique. Good. >> Yeah. I got good good technique. I've been uh doing speed runs and getting it down though. It's it's been great. It's been great. Dad life has been amazing so far. >> How much sleep are you getting? >> I'm getting sleep. Yeah. Veronica my wife is she's doing a great job. Fantastic job allowing me to try and get as much sleep as I can, but you know some nights where you just got to got to try and help out as much as I can. But, uh, no, she's doing a great job. >> What's the most life-changing thing about being a father? >> Life changing. I think, man, just coming home every day and and and knowing that, you know, I have a daughter now, and I know everybody's always said that. Some of the guys in locker room are always like, once you have a kid, it's just different. Like, all the stress and things you worry about kind of it's it's a new new worries and new stress about having just a kid at home that you get to come home to and spend that quality time with. So, uh, definitely is awesome. gives you a kind of new perspective of uh you know just raising a child and and and all the cool things that come with it. But uh it's changed a lot. We've been in the house a good good majority of the time. >> How would you describe the feeling of meeting Raina for the first time? >> Uh it was amazing. Uh you know obviously being just in the hospital uh we were there for about two days. So um you know it was a good experience just being there. It wasn't wasn't fun sleeping on the couch in there, but uh you know, obviously when we had her, it was uh you know, one of those very special life-changing moments of just seeing you know, your daughter for the first time. So, it was pretty cool. >> Jordan, what's been the vibe um of the offseason program, would you say so far? >> Working. Um I think it's always, you know, I think the beginning OTA is always nice just to get back together with the guys, uh you know, that probably haven't seen for a couple months. So, just be able to get everybody back here, get back together and uh just have your mindset on on work and and obviously the work we're putting in the weight room and on the field when you start just doing routes and some of the smaller uh basic stuff and then uh you know building up to now phase three, we're doing some team stuff and uh just by working and trying to get back to honing in on the details and uh building the foundation of what we're going to be this year. >> Have you guys absorbed internally the the news with Josh? How have you guys had meetings? You talk about it. How have you guys absorbed that internally? Yeah, we've talked internally. Um, you know, everyone knows what the situation is there. Um, and we we've talked, but obviously the details are, you know, we're keeping that, everybody's keeping that under wraps right now just out of respect for the the situation and, uh, obviously all the legal stuff that's, you know, going to be playing out. Um, but, you know, it's great to have Josh here with us, um, be able to work with us and and get back to work. But, uh, yeah, you know, we're just kind of everybody's just waiting and, uh, letting it play out on it on its own. >> Do you find yourself wondering, man, am I would I have my running back this year? Just the uncertainty of it all, especially for you as a quarterback, >> you know, it's, uh, yeah, there's always questions. You, you know, I was shocked when I when I saw it. Um, and like I said, it's one of those things. We're going to we're going to let it play out. Um, you know, there there's a lot of uncertainty uh when you when you hear something like that of of what might happen, but uh, we'll see. We will let it play out and uh go from there. >> Didn't seem that way, but is it awkward at all when you like when you first saw him at Brook after the incident or whatever happened? >> No. No. And uh you know, I'm just going to leave some of the stuff we've talked about and everything uh kind of internally, but uh No. Knowing who Josh is. No. >> What' you think of your new receiver uh >> Bo Melton? >> Oh man, you know, I love having Bo out there. It's nice to have him back on the offensive side, you know, fully and uh just keep him over here and and keep letting him work on his his craft as a receiver, but um he made a couple big time plays today, some some some down the field, uh plays. But it's it's nice. I mean, everybody knows in the locker room what kind of personality Bo is and uh he he he brings that kind of energy and that just infectious uh mindset wherever he's at. And he's just he's a great person to be around. So having him back on the offense side has been great. >> Why is he good on the deep ball? Why is he so good at deep ball? >> Oh, he's very fast. He's He's got a lot of speed. Um and uh yeah, that's that's all I can say. But he's making some plays, catching the ball today. >> Yeah. How rare is it to have a guy who's willing to do what he's done in the last couple years? Go to defense, do whatever the team needs, something that's not his position, and switch back the next year and do something like that. I take I take it it takes a special person to do that. >> It definitely does. Um, you know, I think that's a mindset everybody wants to have, but uh, you know, maybe some people get put in that position and, uh, you aren't as willing to to switch to a whole new position that they haven't played. But, uh, for Bo, it's it's that mentality, whatever it takes. You know, whatever he can do to, uh, to to be at the best and be on the field and and make an impact for the team, whether it's receiver, DB, special teams, you know, he's the guy that's he's going to do it. He's going to step up and he won't complain about it and he'll uh he'll go put his best foot forward. So, uh, like you said, it takes a special, you know, type of mentality and and just mindset to be able to do that. >> Jordan, I know you talk so much and you guys about turning the page and moving on to, especially when it's a new season, but, you know, for the game in Chicago, the way it ends like that, how long does it take you as a competitor to get through that and get over it and just kind of move forward? >> It's always tough. Um, you know, especially just when you get to playoffs, you know, we always talk about it. You got to you win or go home and everybody knows that. So, uh, it's when you got to play your best ball, find ways to win. And, uh, you know, that game in particular, uh, you know, obviously being up, um, and letting a game slip away and and losing it, uh, the way we did is is very tough. Something you think about, uh, throughout the offseason, but, um, you know, we we've moved on. Um, and it's, uh, it's all about improving and finding ways to to not let that happen again. Um, you know, we've had since I've been the starter here, we've had some tough playoff losses and, uh, it's all about trying to find ways to keep growing and getting better. Um, and now we get a new opportunity with this season coming forward where uh, it's just about getting back to work, you know, learning from mistakes that that are made throughout the whole course of the season, improving on those things as a offense, finding ways to, you know, put our best foot forward, find the best plays that work for us, uh, have the best guys out there on the field, things like that. So, it's just about getting back to work and, uh, you know, it'll be another long process before we get to training camp and the beginning of the season, but it's all about just getting back to work. starting to jump off that uh to jump off that. You've been doing this a long time now. When you get to June, where are you in the optimism level just going towards the next season? Starting to think about that and how does this June stack up with past Judes in your mind? >> No, like I mentioned, I think it's just it's always nice to get back together as a team. Um to see these guys, see the work guys have been putting in all offseason and then obviously get back out here and start playing ball again. Um and you know, the beginning is a little bit slow. Um but now we get to phase three and we're doing real football. Obviously, no pass, but you know, doing some overd is is nice. Um it's very nice. So, uh I think that's always the the beginning of all right, let's restart this thing, get back to work, and uh keep keep finding ways. It's going to be a new team. We got a lot of new faces. Uh some guys that aren't here that have been here. So, it's all about just finding ways to improve and um you know, building this new unit, building the chemistry, and uh you know, being able to start that foundation from from the bottom. >> What's it been like having Tyrod in the room with you? It's been great. Um, you know, Tyrod is a he's a pro. He's a vet. He's been at it for a long time. So, uh, you know, it's it's nice to have, uh, a guy in the room that's played a lot of ball. He's been a lot in a lot of different offenses. Um, and just somebody you can piggy back off and, uh, you know, pick his brain. You know, what are you seeing out there? What am I seeing? Kind of those things. And just have those conversations. But, uh, Tyro's been great, man. He's a pro. Uh, you know, just the way he handles his business, comes in the building and, uh, you know, just goes to work is, uh, it's cool to watch. and uh it'll be great to have him around all season. >> He was obviously Aeron's backup in New York. Did Aaron reach out anything? Be like, "You're going to love this guy or anything like that?" >> No. Uhuh. No, we haven't tal we haven't talked yet. Um but no, he's he's been with, you know, Aaron, like you said, been in these type of systems, uh similar to ours. So, uh you know, he brings a lot of wisdom, a lot of just uh you know, different ideas on on how, you know, their offense was running over there and and different things uh scheme wise. So, it's great. >> Jordan, how much are you looking forward to having a fully healthy Tucker craft back this year? He'll be great. Um, you know, Tuck's been he's been grinding um you know, since he got injured last year and, uh, all off seasonason. So, uh, another guy where it's just you watch these guys work on the on the side and it's sucks not having him out there. We all know what type of player he is, but uh, I know he'll be back and, uh, he'll be he'll be hungry to hit the ground running whenever, uh, he's able to, you know, get back with the team. some of your receivers and Romeo and Dante Von. Just what do you feel about the wide out group you have and who you think is kind of ready to pick up the slat with those guys that >> Yeah, like you mentioned, it's tough uh losing Rome, losing Wix, uh you know, wish those guys nothing but the best, you know, in their new journey on a new team, but it's always tough. You know, you never want to see guys go uh especially guys that were such you know, impactful players like those two. But, uh like you mentioned, we still got a very deep receiver room. We got Christian, we got Jay Reed, we got MG, guys who are all going to continue to keep building, keep taking those steps. Um, guys who played a lot of ball with Christian and Jay Reid. So, uh, we still got a great room and it's just, like I said, it's just about getting back to work right now, building, uh, the foundation and, uh, setting ourselves up for when we get back to training camp. >> Is the dynamic though any like you want as many great players as we always say your favorite guys, the guy that's open, right? But you did have a lot of mouths to feed before and the pecking order is a little bit different now with their departures. Does that change the dynamic for you and does it make it in any way easier? >> Um I mean like you mentioned you for me I love having you know as many options as possible. Um you know I loved having all those guys in the room. Um you know obviously for them everybody wants the ball and it is hard to to feed everybody. Um but like you mentioned as a receiver you don't play every play. you know, guys get tired. They're rotating in and out. So, you always want to have the best out there. So, now it's about um finding those next guys, you know, finding those next guys to take that step. Um and we got guys, we got Savon, we got Bo, guys who are going to, you know, build up and uh you know, hopefully be able to be there to take the load off when when Christian, Jay Reed, those are going to be the guys and and MG when they need a break. So, it's just about building that foundation and getting those next guys who are going to be the the next playmakers for us. But, um yeah, you know, I love having as many weapons as I as I can. So, I don't think it makes it easier. Um, but I think for the question, just trying to spread the ball around to those guys, give them as many touches. Uh, yeah, it'll be easier than that. >> The passing game has been very spread evenly for a few years now as a quarterback, especially with this depth chart at receiver. Is it incumbent upon you to make sure you're getting the ball to your best guys as much as possible, even if it doesn't mean that it's going to be as spread evenly as it's been? Um, man, I think once we get to the season and and and figuring out how we're going to game plan for guys and and and and where we're going to put guys on certain routes, things like that, uh, for me, it always comes back down to just reading the play out. Um, trying to make the best decision possible based on what the defense is doing and attacking them that way and not trying to, uh, be forcing the ball to certain guys just because I'm trying to get them as many touches as I can. Um, just trying to be a smart quarterback and play the game out. But, uh, yeah. No, we'll try and get these guys as many touches. And I think right now it's we're off to a great start. These guys are making plays and uh it's it's been fun to to get back to it with them. But uh we'll see how we keep building this thing. >> So you don't go into a week a game week thinking, okay, Tucker, he's got to have this many touches for us to be our best offensive. Christian, he's got to have offense. >> Not that many touches, but I think it's all, you know, matchup who you're going against. You might think, okay, I like the matchup we're getting on Tucker on some of these guys we're going against. So, uh, you might like, you know, I like attacking this corner on the outside. So, um, you might get those kind of matchups, but I never go into it thinking I need to get a guy a certain amount of catches. >> Not asking for spec, >> not asking for specifics, but going against Ganon's defense the first time these last few weeks. So, what are your initial impressions of kind of what you've seen on that side of the ball? >> Uh, it's been it's been great so far. Um, I think as a quarterback going against a new defense that you haven't really scouted is always just trying to trying to figure some stuff out, figure out what these coverages are, figure out what they look like, figure out what the disguises look like, and just trying to piece some stuff together. And, uh, you know, the first couple weeks was definitely trying to figure it out. And, you know, it's looking good so far for sure. They're flying around. Uh, they're in, you know, they're making a good impact so far, but I think as we get into it, it's starting to, you know, figure it out, understand what they're doing a little bit more and, uh, how we can attack it. But, uh, so far it's looking good. Um, you know, the DBs are all playing really well right now. They're in tune with each other and, uh, they're making some plays. >> Do you pay attention at all to like national NFL news? I mean, obviously Miles Garage to the Rams and PJ Brown, the Patriots. I mean, that's two teams you guys are going to see this year. Do you pay any attention to that or just kind of? >> No, you see it. You see it all. Um, you know, I definitely see whenever there's some some big trades, especially Miles Garrett going to the Rams. I mean, that's a that's a huge deal right there. Like you mentioned, a team will we'll face in the season. So, uh, yeah, you see all that stuff and, uh, that was a that was a big trade for sure. >> Maybe not hoping to have to play against Miles Garrett again. >> I mean, you know, when I when I heard it, that's the first thing I thought. It was, "All right, we're playing him again." So, uh, uh, it'll be great. You know, he's a he's a phenomenal football player. Um, and you know, they got a good defense already. They got a good team in general. Um, obviously, uh, so we'll see what it looks like. What has Jordan Morgan shown you in the off season and he's going back to a position he's known so well being at that position? Has that allowed him really to thrive do you think so far? >> Yeah. Um and J Mo I think uh since we've got back he's looked good. You know he's he's put in the work throughout the offseason just working out getting that strength right. Um and for him I think it'll be it'll be great be able to get him settled in at left tackle. We know he's bounced around um you know been at guard, moved around to tackle. So, uh, for him to be able to just settle in and and and get all these reps throughout the offseason and going into training camp at tackle, uh, it'll be great for him and just continue to to grow and, uh, be the best player he can be. But, um, I'm excited for him. >> You mentioned learning from last season. What were the lessons from last season because it wasn't just the last game. It was September on as a team. You guys were in position to win games and were able to close them. What did you learn from that? Yeah, I think uh you know it was disappointing how we finished you know all those games towards the end of the season. Um and you know as a team we always talk about finishing um and just you got to find ways in these games late in the season no matter what the circumstances are. You know guys get injured, things happen, your body's tired. uh you got to find ways to to to keep stacking, keep elevating going into the postseason. And uh you know, when you get a close game like some of the ones we had, you got to find ways to finish and win those games and uh set yourself up going into playoffs. And especially like you said, the just the Bears game, the last playoff game, uh you know, we didn't do that. So, we got to do a much better job finishing. I think situational ball is something that we'll have to keep improving, especially as a offense. Just keep improving at some of those, you know, two-minute situations. Uh just getting everybody on the same page of what we need to do in some of those situations and just growing from some areas we've made mistakes in before. >> Two more >> Jordan with having Shawn back, you know, and what kind of the rapport you guys built at center during the second half the last season. Just what do you think that meant to you guys the offensive line kind of you guys the direction you're headed? >> Yeah, it was great. Um you know, I think anytime, especially a center, um a guy who's snapping you the ball every play, you want to have that relationship. You want to, you know, build something with a guy. So to be able to get Shawn back was huge. I was excited to to hear that news. Um, and like you mentioned, if he wasn't going to be back, who knows what, you know, if we'd be trying to uh bring a guy in, who knows? So, just trying to know that you have a guy that you've built chemistry with, understand each other, the communication, all those things are on point. So, to have him back, I think he did a phenomenal job last year stepping into that role, something he hadn't really done as much. Um, you know, he's been at guard, so I think he did a great job at it. And now for him, it's just keep finding ways to improve, be as consistent as possible. Um, but I think for the O line as a whole, having that guy who who's making the calls, knowing what to do, uh, you'd love to have that. >> I remember when when Aaron was here, he would, if there's a young receiver or a young corner, he would purposely test them at training camp just to see what they got. >> Will you take that approach, whether it's throwing the ball to the Savan Williams of the world or throwing it at Brandon Cece just to kind of see what they got and get those guys ready for what's to come? >> I mean, I'll try not to throw the ball to Brandon Cece. Definitely not. Try not to, but uh, >> what his direction? Yeah, I mean you definitely want to test guys. Um, especially young guys like you mentioned. I think on the offensive side, it's more of, you know, you right now is a time to to train guys on where to be at, where as a quarterback you you're expecting guys to be for certain looks and um, you know, if guys might not be running the right a route the certain way is kind of just putting the ball in an area where you're expecting them to be. And that's how you grow and learn and and tell a guy after the rep, hey, this is where I need you or um you know, I think all those little things, but just understanding each other, feeling it out, talking after the play, uh hey, what' you see here? You know, this is kind of what I was thinking on this rep. Um just continue to build that chemistry. And then on the defensive side, yeah, I mean, you want to I I love watching some of the young guys out there, seeing what they're doing, seeing what they're capable of. Um yeah, you you want to attack guys when when you see them out there. um just see what kind of plays they're going to be making. But yeah, try and avoid throwing the ball to the defense as much as possible, for sure.

title: Packers Unscripted: OTA observations
text: Hi everybody. Welcome to another edition of Packers Unscripted from Packers.com. I am Mike Spoffer joined as always by my trusted colleague Wes Hodkitz. We're coming to you here from the Podawatami Sportsbook studio. I got it first time and I got it right. >> He knocked it out of the park by home run right out of the park. Uh first time being out this year. >> Had very modest expectations, but I think if you ask Pahad, I carried our our four like scramble. I carried our team, our foresome. So, >> uh was very happy and I mean, as you can probably attest to too, >> you could not have beaten the weather in Wisconsin, northern Wisconsin, where I was, uh over the weekend. And I mean that was picture perfectesque uh conditions. So I was hitting them across the links. You were catching uh carpy >> crappie. >> Crappie. Sorry. >> Big fisherman over here. >> Yes. Um the weather the weather was great and uh the fish were biting a little bit. Um rough day on Saturday, much better day on Sunday, but >> um but had some fun and uh um but we've got some Packers football to talk about >> because last week we got to watch one of the Packers OTAA practices shortly after we are done recording this episode. We're going to head out and catch another OTAA practice that we can talk about on our next show. But as far as week one of OTAAS and what we got to witness out there at Ray Nichki Field, Wes, I'll just open it up to you. What caught your eye? What stood out for you uh during that workout? >> The first thing that stood out for me isn't necessarily anything we saw directly during the practices, but Matt Laflur coming out and saying straight away that Tucker Craft, the hope for him is be back for training camp or early in training camp. And honestly, Mike, the way we all everything we've seen, the little bit we've even watched him now doing rehab off to the side. I mean, Laflur said it himself. I mean, Tuck looks like he could go today. Yeah. uh you know, he's had a tremendous recovery from this, a great rehab, obviously clocked the hours, spent a lot of time in Green Bay, uh took a little time to himself in Arizona with his family, but otherwise, it's been all systems go working towards this season. Obviously, still looking to lock up that long-term deal uh with his rookie contract expiring after 26. So, not that he ever needed any additional motivation, but boy, it sure looks like Tucker Craft is locked in. >> It's very reminiscent of last year with Christian Watson, isn't it? because we there were so many times that we saw during practices Watson was continuing his ACL rehab off to the side and and everybody's looking at him saying, "Yeah, he looks like he's ready to go, right?" But there's a timeline. There's a process to this and uh um and the Packers are going to follow that with regard to Craft just as they did with uh with Watson. So uh so patience will be required. Um certainly the way Watson came back last year, everything turned out quite nicely. The other update of course, Micah Parsons, everything from what we've been told, the rehab is going well. The expectation is he will start training camp on PUP. Um and we'll see how uh we'll see how things play out from there. >> And Matt's saying too, he expects him back. Actually, I think he he will be back because we got the softball game this week, I think, for him coming up now, too. Um whether or not he's able to participate in that remains to be seen, but I think it's him and Jordan Love have that coming up on the horizon as well. So um when you look at Micah um we haven't obviously seen him as much as as Tucker in terms of our eyes. You know, Tucker I I seem like every time I walked in the building, he was driving through. Uh but but by all accounts, a really good recovery for him. Devonte Wyatt was with the rehab group during practice as well. So, uh, for the Packers, I mean, for to get the guys back, the key playmakers back, um, and to have them making progress is is really, we'll talk about some of the other observations from OTAAS, but that that's what you want to get the most out of this. Zack Tom also with the rehab group, but the hope is he'll be ready for training camp. So, um, Packers, when you look at last year and how it ended with the reserve list, you can make a case that like half of their top eight players were all on IR at that point. So, um, to to have a little bit of positivity there, I think is really important and and certainly I think would be uplifting for this roster, uh, if you see number 85 and these other guys get back during camp towards this goal now of 26. >> Yeah. And we'll, uh, uh, we'll just have to see where things go. I mean, because we still just turn the calendar to June. There's there's a lot of a lot of time to go here. The other thing that was addressed by Matt Lafleur right before last week's first open practice to the media, the situation with Josh Jacobs, um after we recorded our episode last week, the news broke about Josh being arrested for a domestic incident. Then the following day he was released, the county prosecutors have not made a decision on whether or not he's going to be charged or what he may be charged with. So the Packers have made it clear they're letting that situation play out. The legal process is going to have to run its course here. So, um, with that in mind, turning back to the on the field action during practice, what did you like about what you saw or what caught your eye? >> Well, let's starting with the running backs, right? Because I mean, Chris Brooks is a guy that you don't want it to be under these circumstances, but he's a dude that has sort of been under the radar for Green Bay for a while, but the Packers made it a point to sign him to not just in restricted ten. They gave him a two-year contract this off season. I mean, this is one of those jack-of alltrades players. I I always compare him to Tony Fischer. He reminds me a lot of that. Not only just with what his role is, but also his physical frame. Just he's a he's a guy that can stand up to bowl rushes. He's a guy that can take on linebackers. And also the hope here, and again, we'll go out to practice and we'll see where things are at. But Marshon Lloyd uh has been with the Packers all off season. He's gotten some answers after going out to the West Coast. The Packers have him on a plan. Uh he took part in the individuals last week, but did sit out of the team periods. So, it was PR Strong and Chris Brooks handling those first team reps. Um, but you and I said it on the sideline when we're watching them in the individual drills. It when you draft a running back, when you actually put that investment into a player that's one of the top of the line coming out of college, they just look different. And we we spent a lot of time focused on, you know, Marshon's size when he came out. I wrote a feature on him and and kind of the way he's built, but his speed and his explosiveness for a guy of his caliber, when you tie it all together, we all know he could be special. >> It's just a matter of if he can finally put this this rash of injuries behind him. So, um I I thought it was a good day for the for the RBs. And then, you know, just spinning it forward a little bit more. Um man, it seems like every offseason I say this, but Christian Watson, dude, just looks fantastic. uh just his physical makeup and just watching a guy that has this amazing frame and tremendous speed for a guy that's 6'4 um but just the way he's built. I mean when you look at the picture the portrait of what a receiver looks like in the National Football League it is Christian Watson. So I just thought there was a lot of positive things to draw from that practice. You know Matthew Golden running with the ones, a lot of passes going his way during the team periods. >> I thought so too. >> It was just a really good flow. >> Yeah. Yeah, I mean I it it uh and this is typical for the springtime when it's uh when it's no pads and you know everybody's kind of learning the offense and from what we've heard from Matt Lafleur they they sort of tore things down to the bare bones and and rebuilding like where to go and you see in these OTAA practices the ball kind of goes like lots of different directions right I mean it goes to Watson it goes a couple times to Golden they get the ball in Savon Williams hands you know I mean and and uh and then you know you're working the running plays as well as you mentioned And we didn't see Marshon Lloyd in the 11 on 111. It sounds like he has done some 11 on 111 in OTAAS, but the Packers are not going to run him into the ground regardless of the Josh Jacobs situation. There's a plan for Marshon Lloyd that is completely separate from the Jacobs situation because of everything that he has gone through with his body and with his health. So, um I I hope uh I hope we get to see a little bit more of him um you know, here this month. But again, it's really going to be more about training camp when the pads are on and him getting action in the preseason games for somebody who has played so little in the first two years of his NFL career. Um there's there needs to be a ramp up for him to uh to get to where he wants to be, to get to where the Packers want him to be so that he can play a full season and um and help out this offense. With regard to the injured players, we did get a look at the first team offense, first team defense, and some rotations and whatnot that were going on. It's worth pointing out that in Micah Parson's absence, the two the first two edge rushers with the number one defense, Lucas Vaness and Baron Serell, the fourth round draft pick from last year. Some other guys were rotating in for that. But then also on the offensive side, the right tackle replacing Zack Tom as he continues his rehab is the veteran Darien Canard. Um some other depth chart observations if you want to share them, but those were the two I think that jumped out the most to me. >> Sell's a big one. Uh because you have Brentton Cox Jr. there too and I pontificated a lot about Cox last week. I I I said I mean this guy what he was doing on the second team unit. I mean the the second team tackles are having a hard time getting a hand on him. uh a guy that we'd all sort of forgotten about a little bit, right, because of the core injury last year. Uh but Brenton is still very much in this thing. But the fact that they did give Serell that opportunity to work across from Lucas Vaness in these practices speaks to the offseason he's had and also the way he finished last year, uh a very positive note in Minnesota and and I thought was one of the real MVPs of that game. And you could tell afterwards how much pride being in the locker room that he took because it it was a long wait for him. There's a lot of bodies at edge rusher last year. >> Um especially when Micah Parsons was playing because this is a guy that doesn't really come off the field that much once he was healthy. >> You know, Micah's playing 82% of the defensive snaps and and Rashan is the type of guy too that was in that 50 to 60 range. So it was tough to get to the trough, so to speak, right? So now Baron's going to have that opportunity. You would have loved to have seen Colin Oliver out there. unfortunately he was one of the DMPs in this practice was with the rehab group but the Packers have so many different options at edge rusher right now and um I'm just excited who who comes out of that the thing I thought is the most interesting and it's been more of a philosophical change that we've seen really since co I would say and that's seeing the young guys and the rookies getting involved with the first team starting offense and defense >> that was the next thing I was going to ask you about because uh because while they weren't taking the initial like the very first reps with the first teamers. We saw Brandon Cece at quarterback, Chris Mlullen at defensive tackle. Those two draft picks in particular were in the rotation with the number ones before they kind of blow the whistle and and the uh and the second units go in. So, those guys were getting uh getting some snaps with the first unit. And yeah, as you said, it's it is a little bit of a philosophical change. Um, I think that that may be partly because of just so many more practice limitations even in training camp now compared to, you know, not that long ago like previous CBAs, um, where players would always have would always have that chance to to ramp themselves up in in training camp and get those opportunities. Now, um, there aren't as many of those in in a training camp. So, if you want somebody, you know, to if you want a rookie to really be ready to play um and to help out your team in some fashion in week one, um they have to get used to running with the ones, as they say. And I think that's partly where that comes from. >> Yeah. And and this is no disrespect to Mike McCarthy. I'm sure if Mike heard me say this, he'd probably end up punching me in the shoulder. But uh I I always when I first started covering the team, it was just it was so I don't want to say it's antiquated, but it was like all the rookies had to run with the second and third team offense and defense. And I just I always go back to that 13 training camp. I know I write about it a lot and I talk about it a lot, but I'm watching Alex Green and James Starks run with the ones. Alabama and UCLA and they're they're going against these guys that probably aren't going to be in the NFL uh this upcoming season. I just was like, "Oh, like kind of what are we doing here?" Because the Packers very when we went into 2013 coming off the 12 season and Cedric Benson and the litany of guys that Green Bay brought in at the end of that year, they needed to draft a running back and they got him and Eddie Lacy. Get the guy out there was the thing that was in the back of my head. Yeah. >> Because it's not just about, okay, well, this is going to be the starter. It's about, hey, Brandon Cece, Keshan Nixon, and Carrington Valentine come out. You're in. Benjamin St. Juice wasn't practicing. Get over there. Get in the get in the game. And you need to have you need to be familiar with that. You need to get comfortable with that. You know, Cece's 20 years old, but you and I discussed it after practice. I felt like there's a lot of Javon Bullard to him where it was like this dude is not afraid. Now, obviously they're not in pads, but I mean this guy, he attacks it and it's instinctual and that's what you want to see from a guy that has that type of speed and that type of size. So, >> to get him and also Chris Mlullen and I I've said it numerous times now. I don't know if I've covered a defensive lineman here that has the type of body type that Chris Mlullen has. Yeah. Um he he's a little bit bigger than Mike Daniels, but he's long and his hand you we talk about the hand size. I mean, this dude brings a different dimension. He was hustling out there, too. So, um I I just like seeing those young guys get incorporated. And one other reason I bring up the offense or the number ones and and going on is because they do split squad now. So, you very easily could have Cece and Mlen down with the twos taking every rep as opposed to, you know, being down there and rotating in. Back in the McCarthy era, a lot of times it was we were watching one offense and one defense and then the other ones would sub in. >> So, it's just another philosophical thing that you've seen change. But, it's good to see. >> I I think part of it just to just to touch on the McCarthy thing, I think there was a little bit of an old school mentality with him that any rookie that walked in the building, >> you had to earn a rep with the first team. And so, right at the beginning, you're not just going to be handed that opportunity. And yes, things are different now. As I mentioned, there's not as much practice time. There are more limitations in OTAAS. There are more limitations in training camp and in the regular season for practices. So, it's it's taken on a whole different dimension. But, I think when you're talking a dozen 15 years ago, we were in a little bit different world and and there was there was kind of a mentality of of, you know, a rookie is never just going to be handed anything. You're going to have to earn it against the guys who have been here, even if the guys who have been here are not expected to beat you out, right? I mean, and that's uh um that's kind of how that works. >> And that works at Iowa, but in the National Football League, it's like sometimes you need to make a little push there, you know. >> Very, very true. text: A lot of people look at three four change, three down lineman. Where you sit in that? Defensive tackle, defensive line, defensive end. What What do you say? >> Uh defensive line. Um they've made a big emphasis on nobody's accustomed to just one position. Did you have to adjust your game if you're in a three or four eye based on the guard or tackle? >> Um, yes. Switching the technique um from attack react to react attack. They were a high level defense, top five in the league. So, you know, I'm glad to have coach Leonard here. It is a breath of fresh air. He's a um he he doesn't really talk, but he's very smart. Like, you can talk he can talk ball off for days, and you know, you can you can't do nothing but respect that. You know, I played the four down last year. So, I'll say I was used to both. You know, I'm just coming in. My main goal during the offseason was myself, my body, you know, getting down, getting stronger, bigger, faster. So, >> how much of a change did you see? >> I'm down like 10 pounds right now. A little something. >> What did you play last year? around 338. >> So you're down about 320 something. >> Yeah, 328. I was 328 this morning. >> Then what do you think about land putting on the muscle he's put on? >> It's such a he he's crazy. Like he he loved the weight room this offseason and you know he did, you know, he was frustrated last season with the injury and all that, but you know that just shows how much work he put in, how much dedication he's poured into himself and his investment into itself. So you can't do anything but love and respect that. I don't think we've talked to you since you made the all rookie team last year. How cool was that for you? Have >> Yeah, it's cool. I don't really I don't try to look at it stuff like that as much because it's football. You're just playing football. No matter if I get one tackle, 10 tackles, I'm going to try my best, you know. So, it is cool though. My My dad tells me about it. My mom loves to see it. But, you know, I try not to look at all that. >> What's the biggest adjustment for you in the new defense? Um, just playing different blocks. It's different angles that the offensive line has given us. Different type of I'm not going to say different type of technique from us. It's more of he's given us more free range. If we see something from the offensive line, he lets us play it like and it just lets us play freer like lets us play running 100%. That's Coach Brady's mentality right now. like no matter how many guys we can have 11 22 guys, 11 offense, 11 defense, those same guys can play special teams.
