What what kind of elements do you bring to the offense? >> Yeah, I think for me, the sky's the limit, you know, however they want to incorporate incorporate me in the offense, you know, putting me at different positions, whether that's X, Z, F, no matter what, in the slot, outside, you know, whenever whenever I can go out there and make a play. um No necessarily goals for myself personally, but I think we all know that the goal for the team is to, you know, put a ball on the ring. So, that's how I I'm going to contribute however I can. >> With lining up inside, is that something that you think is kind of an underrated ability to have as a pass catcher? >> For sure. I think, you know, being a big receiver, you know, being able to go in there and line up inside and, you know, go against linebackers or nickels and just make plays in there is is definitely a, you know, a benefit to us. >> The coaches mentioned The coaches mentioned your physical improvement from last year to this year. Where do you think that will show up in the game? And what was kind of the goal to see that help the version of your game? >> Yeah. You know, honestly, I think it will show up in all aspects. You know, route running, you know, just being stronger, being able to break tackles, you know, just being quicker, and then, you know, just being smarter. You know, a lot of times we're we're playing against zones and things like that. So, knowing where to sit, you know, knowing where to take high angle or low angle, that stuff's really important. So, I think it will help out a lot. >> Jaylen, what kind of things have you noticed that's different this OTA versus last year? I know you're probably learning like crazy last year. But now, what is it for you personally, but for the offense in particular pre-snap? What's different and why is it different now? >> I think, you know, I think pretty early we realized that the starting point where we started last year was a lot farther behind than where where we started this year, of course. I mean, obviously, because everyone is very familiar with the plays and everything of that sort. But, you know, really just I think it comes down to, you know, Nick giving us confidence and just trusting us to be be able to go out there and execute those plays. >> Jaylen, have you seen anything different in year two with CJ and what you see in terms of growth and confidence in him this year? >> For sure. I think, you know, CJ has always been the same person day in and day out. He's a great leader. A guy that you could tell really cares about the team. I think this year you know he seems very focused. You know I was able to train with him in the off season as well and you know he was just very locked in. The little details really matter to CJ now so it's definitely going to be exciting year. For sure. I think the same thing I said for me you know the sky's the limit for him. You know you know that guy special in any way they want to use him whether it's the return game at receiver. I think for him he's obviously had a big jump too as far as his physical traits. You know he's getting even faster even though he's already fast. Getting stronger but you know just working on those little details and understanding certain routes and how they need to be ran at certain times. He's definitely done a good job at doing that. Yeah. For the tank question I would say you know just the the type of guy he is. You know he's from Florida I'm from Florida. I feel like you know Florida people are just like overly confident. You know we're always confident we got that swag. So just kind of taking that swag from him. Always being confident and knowing you're going to go out there and make a play and you know celebrate for sure. And then it was actually my third annual camp but it was awesome. We had about like 110 kids show out. It was a free camp in my community. They had a good time with the coaches. Coaches did a great job. Yeah it was really really fun day. Yep. >> experience now. And I know you've been to Florida. You've got a chance to really what it's like to fish in this area compared to even the need of wild world of sports either way. >> The The difference between here and in Texas? >> Uh I don't know, man. It's hard. I think in Florida, um it's easy to just go to a pond and and just go fishing. In Florida, I feel like you always catch fish. At least where I live, I feel like it's a lot of development. So, you know, there's not a lot of fish in there. But, uh I've definitely been able to go out to Galveston and uh go fishing on the water. It's been fun. Um I got to go catch a sheep's head, but catching huge red fish. And then, you know, in in Florida, you know, I like to fish the mangroves and catch snook, snapper, things like that. >> Your conversations with Nick Caley and also David Caley, what are some things they're telling you about their vision for you for the offense and uh what do you like about that? >> For sure. I think the The biggest thing they kind of been telling me is just, you know, the versatility I can bring to the offense. Kind of just like I said, you know, being able to play all three positions, inside, outside. And then, really just create mismatches. Um at the end of the day, I feel like it just gives me an opportunity to get the ball in different ways. So, yeah. >> You said that you think uh Jaylen's getting faster. Uh How do you Is that something that you measured? Is that something that you wanted to emphasize? Something you tell? >> Um well, you know, we have certain data data It tells us if we're we're getting faster or how fast we're running miles per hour wise. Um so, the the stats never lie. Um but, you know, you can just see it in his body. Um and you know, Jaylen's a confident guy, too. So, you know, he always is going to want to race and and do things like that as well. Appreciate it, guys.

title: Will Anderson Jr. on Leadership, Defense and the Texans Standard | Full Q&A
text: What's up? What's up? >> What's up? Hey, William, on last week, coach Ryan said that he may have to consider taking you out a couple of plays because you keep working at on CJ. But, when you are when your mindset is on that field, it doesn't matter whether it's OTAs, practice, or anything like that. You only know one speed. >> Yeah, most definitely. Um I believe in the process and preparation. Anytime I step on the field, it's an opportunity to get better. And like you said, no matter if it's OTAs, training camp, walk-through, jog-through, I'm learning how to be a pro still. I'm not I can't do jog-through cuz I ain't going to lie, you got to I'm going to be on the sideline or I'm going full speed. But, that's me training my body to be in these positions that I'm going to be in in the game, training my hands, training my footwork, turning the corner, throwing by, setting edges, everything like that. So, for me, it's like I've only been wired one way, and that's to go full speed. >> Well, um you've been in the playoffs six straight years, stopping in the same place. Is Is it fair to say that Super Bowl expectations are something for this squad? >> Oh, most definitely. Most definitely. I think like the additions that they went and got, you know, in the offseason have been great. I think what we want as a team is right in front of us. Um I told the guys today when we broke it down, I said, "Man, it's a confidence thing." I said, "Look, everybody in this circle will believe that this is a Super Bowl team." And everybody raised their hand. And I said, "Well, the front office, the coaches, they made the decision to bring you here because they thought they thought that you could help us win that Super Bowl. So, you're a Super Bowl caliber player." And so, for me, like I look at this team, man, and we got Super Bowl caliber players all over the field. And it's just about taking that next step. And I thought, since the 4 years I've been here, this is like This is being on the team that's so fast, getting together. This has been the best OTAs that we've had offensively and defensively, man. Everybody's locked in. I love the rookie class that we got, man. They're adapting really well, getting getting into the building early, taking care of their bodies, staying extra, doing meetings, staying extra on the field. But that's the culture that's been built here. Um everybody's buying into like I said, like this OTAs has been like the best OTAs I've seen with everybody buying in offensively, defensively, offense doing their thing pre-snap or whatever it may look like, defense getting lined up, coverage stuff, D-line stuff. So like, it's just been a a great a great sight to see and I'm excited for the future of this team. >> Will, there's a lot of great defenses over the past couple of decades, whether it was the old Ravens or the Seahawks, etc., Buccaneers. When you think about that, how much is that something to beyond the winning and trying to set yourself up to that kind of standard where people are talking about the the Texans as one of those kind of defenses? >> Yeah, yeah, most definitely. We want to be a staple uh a staple defense. We want to be a household name defense. Like we want to be one of the greatest defenses to be out there. But I think it starts at this time. It starts doing OTAs. It starts in meetings. It starts getting out on the field for pre-practice. Like, that's how you become a great defense. Um taking the little details in your game and fine-tuning them. And it was like, if you think you know you know the standard, if you think you're doing the standard, you're not cuz the standard is so much higher. So like, more is required, you know, for us. You know what I'm saying? So like, everybody's been buying into that standard. But we talk about being the best defense in the league, you know, it starts now at this time. And I think everybody's buying into that and believing that in their heart. >> Will, when you look at the guys in the defensive end room, Dylan Horton, some of the new faces there, what kind of have been your early impressions of those other guys in the defensive end room? >> Yeah, man, super athletic, really long, man. Uh can get off the ball really well, use their hands really well. They know the attack system. They bought in super early. Dylan's been a guy that's been here with me for four years. To see his progression, to see how he's been doing. He's having a heck of a OTAs and I'm excited about him. Um Dominique, he came I think from the Chicago Bears. A good guy, can pass rush, man. I'm excited about him as well. And we have a rookie, um Harsh. He's been great, man. I told him I said, "Man, you're way more advanced than me when I started as a rookie." So, I'm excited about that room. Uh young room, excited, they're hungry. And we just got to keep the ball rolling, man. Keep buying into the system. Keep buying into the culture. And great things will happen. >> Will, I know you have a good relationship with him. So, how sharp do you expect to see Miles Garrett in the coming months and seasons? >> Man, it was crazy cuz like this has been like an ongoing conversation like when we work out or we just spend some time together and hang out, man. And like I I think Miles is a great guy. You know what I'm saying, man? He's put so much into this game, put so much into the Cleveland Browns, man. He gave it his all. Um I'm happy for this opportunity that he has, man. A a new a new start somewhere, man. I know he's going to be the same Miles, man. So, like huge shout out to him, huge congrats to him, man. I can't wait to see. I told him I'm happy you're leaving the AFC. He can go somewhere else. >> [laughter] >> But, man, I'm super excited for him. Yeah. Yeah, that's a good question. I think for me like I think taking that next step of leadership and differentiating the difference between talking to Will and talking to somebody else has been like a really big challenge for me, man. But, I've been taking the step of like grace. You know what I'm saying? Because I know I remember how it was when I was a rookie and how hard it was. And like it wasn't easy, especially coming to a system like this, coming to a place where the standard is super high. So, man, just giving the rookies grace and be like, "Man, you're okay. You're good. You're here for a reason. They chose you for a reason because they thought you were going to you're good enough to help this team get somewhere that we never been before." But, like I said, like their their mindset has been really good. They have been great in the building, great on the field, great in the meeting room. So, it's like it's not a lot that needs to be said to them because they're already on it so much. But, man, just telling them like, "This is only your first second week of OTAs, man. Don't be too hard on yourself. You know, take some time to reflect on the good things that you've done. Don't always look at the negative like you did it good. How can I be consistently at doing this every single day?" >> Well, kind of a two-parter off of that question. What's that fine line as a leader of, "Okay, grace, but also we have a standard here that you need to live up to." And then I'll ask the second one after. >> Yeah, most definitely. Yeah, I think that the fine line is just how you connecting with them and how you're saying it. Um there's a couple of times, you know, where it got a little like Will came out. But, it's just a couple of times you got to dial it back because not everybody responds to how you may talk to them. Everybody's different. So, but I think the sense of urgency that I I led with and what I'm talking with is, you know, becoming easy to understand because like I said like I told the guys I've been here for 4 years and in the last 3 years we hadn't got past the second round. You know what I'm saying? So, the sense of urgency in the building is high. What we're trying to achieve is high. So, like you can get with the program or, you know, figure it out. But, I want everybody to figure it out because I want everybody to be here and I know that they're here for a reason. And so, just the talk of sense of urgency being on the field, being in Indy, being in practice, like how much more do you have to give? How much is your urgency going up? And I think the guys have been responding really well to that. >> Hey, real quick. The offense has been working on the recent a lot. You know, talk about saying stuff from the defensive side. What are you seeing that's so much better than the last year? The fact that he's coming in and playing center. >> Yeah, I I think it's I mean, you talk about C.J. C.J. has really taken that step, man. Um of watching the clock, getting the guys lined up, moving with urgency, but he's been the commander back there. He's taken that step as a leader back there to get everybody lined up, to, you know, take the initiative like, "Hey, man, like let's go." And everybody's rallying behind him. And then you got guys like Wyatt Teller, who I love, man. He's been that energy booster on the O-line, getting guys moving around, picking guys up. Um so, I'm excited about that group. I can just see the growth in them already, man. The offense is moving at a much faster pace. I think Kahlil's been doing a good job. They got Foster with the tight ends. Dalton Schultz, as you know, man, those guys are rolling. It's it's competitive and I laughed the other day. I said, "Man, this is going to be a fun training camp." Because you can see like the anticipation of everybody getting out there and like, man, it's going to be one of those where it's going to be a battle every single day. Like the physicality on the edges have up big time with Foster coming in as the tight end. Like I said, so like all of those things that um that they've been working on, they've been doing a really good job with that. >> With with you and C.J. coming in at the exact same time, I wonder what has the bond with him and your relationship with him meant to you and your career being in the city? >> Yeah, man, it's meant everything to me. Like I said, I I said in my press conference like it's it was great to come in with somebody and you wasn't alone. You know, we was two and three, so we piggybacked and relied on each other a lot during this process because we were going through the exact same thing. And to see each other's growth in this game and to see the leadership skills that we built and to see the way we connected with the guys and to see where we helped take this program to, it's been nice. So, just having him having my back and I'm having his back has been nice. >> Well, I understand that you put a lot of individual pressure on yourself when you signed this the the contract. Did that add more pressure to you or how did that make you >> Honestly, no. It didn't add any pressure. Uh I I know I kind of like changed my mindset when I look at pressure. I always think like it's not pressure, it's an opportunity. You know what I'm saying? It's an opportunity to go out and continue to be yourself. I think now my the only thing that's risen is like I want to hit that next stage of my game. You know what I'm saying? Not because of the contract, not because I owe it to myself because I know how much hard work I put in. I know what I put into this game, so like that's what I want for myself. So, it's really nothing about the money, man. It's just about the work that you're putting in, the preparation and the process. And that's why I'm always big on preparation and process just because I told him, I was like, "You can't get to your destination without the preparation and the process." So, for me like how much more can I up my preparation? How much more can I up my process to get to where I want to be as as a player? Appreciate y'all. Y'all have a good one. >> I will I'll be seeing you, appreciate it. I ain't seen you

title: DeMeco Ryans on Stingley, C.J. Stroud and OTAs | Full Q&A
text: Good afternoon. >> We still morning. >> We finished too early. >> No. Good to see you all. >> When you see the progress that continues to happen for Derek Jr., what do you see from specifically the growth each year? And what I've seen from Stingley this year is he comes out and he's as consistent as ever. He's in midyear form already here in May and June. He's making big time plays as we've all seen him make. He's doing a great job in coverage of being being sticky, being exactly where he's supposed to be. And one thing I'm most proud of and Sting is just and this is our entire group. Like when you see a young guy make a play, one of our young corners, they make a play, bat a ball down, like to see the excitement from Steen, Kamari on the sideline of them encouraging the young guys with the plays they're making, that's what I'm most excited to see. >> What have you seen most communications? >> The most improvement I've seen from our team is the pre- snap communication offensively. Our defensive communication has been been lights out. So, I'm we are way ahead of again where we where we've been in the past because of that communication. Us just playing smarter, being a smarter football team, understanding situations better. Feel like we're in a really good place right now. >> Coach two players had their season up and down. What have you seen from them as far as their off season? >> Yeah, starting with Jaylen Smith. I feel like Jaylen is has taken a a really nice jump in second year. Uh he's put in the work. Although he was down with injury, he's came back stronger, looks faster. He's making a lot of plays out here on the practice field. So, I'm excited and encouraged by his development of what he's been able to do. Also, Jaylen Reed can put him in the same category. young player. Second year, he was able to play, you know, more more snaps for us towards the end of the year until, you know, he had an injury, but man, he's been lights out when it comes to his communication, starting with the punt team communication, him being that PP for us, put a lot on their plate. He's handled it really well, doing a great job in the meetings and also making it translate to the field. So, I just love to see the growth and that's what I expect that that's what is expected for our, you know, year two players and I'm excited about that as a coach to see what they're going to do this season. >> What do you um how do you feel about your running backs catching a lot of the backfield and what can that skill do for an offense? Yeah, the backs they doing they've been doing a great job all all camp like we've been working more with our backs with the routes um catching some passes out of the back field some option routes some screen plays and all the guys have handled that really well uh coach Bear has done a great job working with those guys on that just landmarks hands all of the fine details that go into that but we have look we have a a good group of backs all guys that all the guys that have really good hands can catch it well secure the ball well So, um, that'll be a really good position for us this year. >> You talked about the pre-nap work with the offense gotten better that obviously situation last year. What What has happened to make it better? What are they doing to make it better? And what what's happening that you say it is better? >> Yeah, when I go back and I look at film from our last year OTAA practices, we we had trouble just snapping the football, getting plays started, right? And then communication, the play clock going down in last year's practice. So now when I look at it like we're when I say we're ahead, we're we're ahead. We're getting the we're we're doing a better job with our cadence from the quarterback position. All three guys are using voice inflection really well. They're getting our defense defensive line to jump offside several times. Uh they're using their snap points, the cadence, the rhythm and timing. They're changing it up a lot, which does wonders for our offense. When you talk about operating fast and you operate at your pace, you control the tempo and our offense is doing a better job of controlling the tempo this year and I'm excited to see how we keep going with it. >> Aziz and Henry have played a lot together at the linebacker spot for those guys behind them and linebacker. What are the big challenges they need to work on here at OTA be ready for training here? >> Yeah, there aren't many challenges for our guys at the back end feel. We have a very seasoned group, veteran group. They've played a lot of ball together. They communicate really well on on the field. They uh have a lot of good celebrations together. They they know each other really well. And they they're really tight, not only on the field, but off the field. And it it shows it translates on the field. You see the way everyone's in sync with our secondary. It's going to be tough to throw the football. And it's been tough, you know, for our offense during this camp to throw the football when the defense is exactly where they're supposed to be. >> There was a there was a familiar name on the list of college football hall of fame nominees yesterday. Demo Ryan was on that list, man. >> What? >> Yeah. >> What are your thoughts on that? >> Oh, wow. Wasn't expecting to hear that one. Caught me off guard there. Uh, man, that's uh haven't thought much about. That's humbling. A lot of man a lot of great players played college football. So for my name to be even mentioned on there, wow, that that says a lot. That's humbling. Oh man, uh I'm thankful for that. See what see what comes of it. Anytime you're on a list, you want to win it, right? So now uh but no, that's uh wow. That's uh credit to all the guys I played with too back at Alabama. take me back there to some had a rough rough start to my career in college playing for three different head coaches, but it taught me a lot about commitment, how you stick stick to your commitment no matter what. And I was committed to the University of Alabama, although we had three coaches, I wanted to impact the university in a positive way of getting them back on track. And so I got them back on track and then Sabin came in and just took it over and won all the championships. No, but I'm I'm a proud alumni fan of Alabama. Proud of everything, the institute, everything they stand for and the program that they have there now. Wishing them much success. >> How have you seen the bond between Will and CJ grow in their time that they've been here together. Do you think that them being so close despite being on opposite sides of the ball has helped with the leadership of your team? >> Yeah, our leadership has grown tremendously. Will and CJ now they're going into year four. So they are those veterans who when our young guys come in, those are the two guys that everyone is looking to for the leadership for how we do things here, you know, in Houston. And they do a great job of of carrying that banner for us. They represent everything that that I want as a coach and I'm proud to have those guys as our two leaders. They're they're close, of course, off the field, on the field. It's a little It's a little touch and go. Will gets a little close to CJ too many times, but they but they make up afterwards and they're all they're friendly. But, uh, it it's cool to see, you know, both of those guys going back to 2023 when we picked them to see the relationship that has blossomed over the past four years is pretty special. >> Along those same lines, as far as you have, especially with all your coaches, you talk about what did you have with Danny Barrett? And Danny Barrett, he's been man invaluable to me. Uh Danny has been he was here in Houston before I got here long time. Coach, played for a long time. So for me as a coaching staff, as you're building the staff out, you want wise people around you. And coach Barrett is one of those guys, that wise counsel that I need. And he's been a rock for me in the background. He's helped me with a lot of different things when it comes to scheduling, it comes to like how to better serve players. Danny has been there. He's done it. He's seen a lot of things. So, he's always cool, calm, and collected. Nothing, you know, gets Danny rock one way or the other, right? He's always steady. And that's what as a head coach, that's what you need. You need someone who can steady the ship. And Danny is always, he's been that guy for me for the past, you know, four years. And that's why he's my assistant head coach because he's he's that special. >> Coach coach, you talk about the cerebral side of these guys. You mentioned going back to T last year and this year, but you also bring new guys in their cerebral approach. Are you seeing a better maturation by the same all of them looks like James Jackson until they finally get in there and find how well they can retain it and then put it out on the field. When it comes to the cerebral part of the game, I feel like our our coaches have done a really great job, a better job of teaching our younger guys to get them acclimated much faster than we have in the past. So, the teaching techniques and methods, you know, changed and how we're trying to utilize that to better serve these younger guys coming in. I see it come to light on the field. We have rookies who are they're stepping in and they're playing and communicating just like the vets almost in some instances. So, as a coach, you stand back like, man, I'm proud of not only the rookies, but I'm proud of the coaches because I know all the extra work that they put in with our young guys. And seeing it on the field, it's it's uh it's special to see. And we have smart rookies, and that helps. You got really smart players, tough football players, but the above the net game is where you win in this league. And we have a lot of we've added a lot of young guys who are definitely mentally strong. DJ, >> uh, two part question. >> A little louder. >> Two part question. Uh, >> what have you kind of just seen from, uh, Jaylen Higgin? Quick update on EJ Speed. >> Higgins and speed was the question. Is that correct? >> Yeah. No, no, no. the update on EJ speed and uh how you see Jaylen Joy Higgins progress in here too. >> Yeah. Um Higgins has done a an outstanding job from from day one from him coming back. He just when I seen him for the first time coming back it's like well you see a physical difference right? You see a stronger you see more chiseled out receiver. Then we step on the field he's playing faster. He's playing stronger. He's making all of the tough catches. He's man playing extremely fast. So, I'm He's taking advantage of his off seasonason, right? And he's really improved in a ton of areas. That was the first area for him is just how can we play fast, consistently, and he's doing that right now. So, that he's going to have a a great year. Can't wait to see it. EJ Speed, uh, he had surgery last week, and we'll see, you know, how that recovery process goes with him. But that's the update so far. When you look at a guy like Arante Street, it's kind of hard to get a good gauge on how much he's progressed from year one to year two on the field, but in ways off the field and just in the short sample size, where have you seen him kind of improve last season? >> And one thing I've challenged Tay on is just taking more of that vocal leadership approach. Although he's a secondyear player, he's a rookie who came in, played a ton of snaps for us, starting at left tackle, he has leadership traits, leadership qualities. I just want to see I'm trying to empower him to allow those qualities to show allow the guys around him to feel that leadership that he does have. So, he's doing a great job so far. Uh this these OTAAS he's came back in shape. He's ready to roll. He's looking he's looking really good. So, he'll be in a good spot for us this year. He's just keep keep leading by being vocal, not just by what you do on the field. We'll close air. You've mentioned a couple times about CJ being here a lot this off season a little earlier than kind of previous years. Is there any light you can shed on his relationship with Nick? Anything they've done in particular to kind of help that grow and help that freestyle process and just them being on the same page? >> Yeah, with CJ and Nick, I've seen both guys, they're communicating much better and it's year two of a system. When it's year two, right, you you understand we're not going through the install for the first time, right? So there is some, you know, recall from what we've done in the past that allows us to speed up what we're doing in year two. It's to be expected. But the way they're communicating, right, CJ has ideas and thoughts on different plays of formations, things that he like, right? We try to do our best to implement those things as well. So it's just the coach player relationship is definitely I think is headed in the right direction. They're growing much closer. they're communicating better and that's what that's what it takes, right? For a good offensive coordinator, good quarterback, we have to work hand in hand and those guys are doing that has been outstanding and also Jerry's done a great job as well with the communication with CJ, what he's doing with Davis, Graham, all the guys. So, I'm pleased with where we are right now with our quarterback position. >> You mentioned the growth of the players. What about Nick Haley? Where are you seeing some specific areas where some of the offense getting better this year? just have a quick followup. Thank you. >> Yeah, for for Kaylee offensively, we've been able we've been able to, you know, install more plays, more wrinkles to what we what we did last year. So, it's u it's exciting to see a different look. You'll see some different things from us offensively this year. And he's growing as a coach, the communication, how he's meeting, you know, how he's calling the plays out here on the field, how he's leading the guys. He's doing a a great job. and not practicing. >> No. >> All right.

title: LIVE: DeMeco Ryans and players address the media
text: When you see the progress that continues to happen for Junior, what do you see from specifically of the growth each year? >> What I've seen from Stingley this year is he comes out and he's as consistent as ever. title: It's Not Another Triangle Of Authority, Is It?
text: It's not a triangle of authority. It just really, really, really, really looks like one. >> You are Locked on Vikings, your daily Minnesota Vikings [music] podcast, part of the Locked On Network, your team every day. >> Hey everybody, welcome to the Locked On Vikings podcast, where we're always trying to learn something new. It's part of the Lock on Podcast Network, the number one sports podcasting network. Today's town hall Tuesday. That means I'm answering your questions as submitted to me via the Google form in the show notes. So, if you have a question, drop it in there. I'll get around to it by the next Tuesday. First question comes from Illuminati Confirmed, who asks, "Oh, I get it." Uh, triangle is back, baby. Looking at the original Triangle of Authority for historical context, which flavor of personnel additions or decisions would you be most excited about? Um, okay. That's a really difficult question to answer because the triangle of authority I think we need a history lesson on the triangle of authority. Uh, because it's not really a thing that like favors a certain kind of player or it's just a power structure. So, here's let let's do it quickly. So, back in the 70s Bud Grant era and all that and Budrant was judge, jury, and executioner. He was making a lot of deals. He was the one working with players, figuring out contracts. Jim Fin obviously had his part to do with it, but he left in 1975. So for a long time, uh, Bud Grant was like the dude. And when Bud Grant left, Mike Lynn was the one waiting in the wings. And so then like an executive kind of took that job and became something more akin to what we would know as a GM today. And obviously that went horribly. Hershel Walker trade. So after the Hershel Walker trade, it's 1992, right? And Jerry Burns has just retired. Mike Lynn is now out of the picture. He's retired as well. So, the Vikings have this huge power vacuum. And this is where I think this the story kind of starts. When they hire Denny Green, they give him personnel control. They want to go back to having one guy be the mastermind like like Bellich was on the Patriots, right? You want this guy to be the dude that gets that that brings in the groceries and does the cooking. You want a guy with a vision that knows who what kind of players he wants and how to coach him. And Denny Green did that. And when Denny Green gets fired, they bring in Mike Ty. Now, Mike Ty does that and after Mike Ty gets fired, think about this. This is the Wolves. It's 2005 and the Vikings have been for a large portion of their history a team run by a head coach/GM combo package guy, one dude. And the Wolves, collaboration fans that they still are today, uh, want to kind of curb that. So, they bring in Brad Childris. That's their first head coach hire as owners as as owners. And they tell children, "Hey, you're not going to have as much power as guys have had in the past. You're going to have to work with Spielman, who's here, and Rob Brzinski, who's been in the or a little bit, these executives, and we want the three of you to be like a dynamic duo. We want not one singular perspective. We want you guys to be checks and balances on each other. We want you to talk about things, and we we think three heads are better than one." That was the idea of the triangle of authority was this collaborative thing. Um there's a question from uh critical of the critics who asks, "I don't understand the hate for the OG triangle of authority. We had our best team in 2009 and we were narrow and we narrowly missed the Super Bowl. We brought in multiple Hall of Famers through the draft in trades and free agency and even got a new stadium out of the deal. The first draft following its departure, we drafted Ponder. So I think uh or we the first draft following it departure we drafted ponder make it make sense. So, I think you've got your timeline wrong because the triangle of authority existed to my knowledge from 2006 through the 2011 offseason and they did away with it in the 2012 offseason was the first one where Rick Spielman was a true blue GM and Leslie Frasier was the head coach and that was the power structure and Brazinski had kind of been sequestered away to just be the cap guy and you weren't going to have this everybody talks about everything deal anymore. Um, so that might help it help you make sense of it, right? But you have a good point. It wasn't all bad, right? 2009 was great. They figured out how to get FV in. They had some good drafts. Uh, they also drafted Traveris Jackson and then the Ponder draft was like the last thing that the triangle of authority did and then it got done away with in 2012 and they had a much more normal structure that is closer to like what we would recognize now. So when they did that, the justification the Wolves gave was that we want a more clear chain of command. And it got a little muddy that who it wasn't 100% clear who was in charge of what? And you had somebody like Rob Rosinski talking to the head coach or talking to the GM about, you know, who should be drafted. And it's like, wait, who's actually in charge of the drafting? Who's actually charge in in charge of the coaching plan? And who's actually in charge of all this? Well, why don't we silo this a little bit more and have a a more clear delineation of responsibility. There's we're still going to be high level executives here, but let's put a guy really on the top. Have one guy where the buck stops with him and that was Rick Spielman. And then everybody else has very clear jobs and responsibilities and things to do. And that made Brzinski the contracts guy. It made Leslie Frasier the head coach. Um, I also think that when Childris was in the triangle of authority, he was much more of the power broker. He was the the much more like the brains of the operation. He was the one that brought in Brett Favre, right? He was the guy that insisted upon drafting Traverus Jackson. He was the guy that insisted upon drafting Adrien Peterson. So, for all the wins and losses of that, that was Childris. Leslie Frasier didn't quite take the power as much as Brad Childress and so it left a power vacuum and that made confusion that made things muddled and they went, "No, no, no. We're not doing this anymore." All right, that that 2011 off season, this was a mess. We're not doing this anymore. Let's go. Let's just give Rick Spielman the power. He's a scouting guy. Rob Brzinski is once again going to be on the business side. Um Kevin Oonnell is the head coach. Nolan Tiesley is the GM. they all are gonna kind of do their thing. What can that do for your game when your eyes are good? >> Yeah, I mean, in the run game when you got run game, pass game, you got somebody coming at you. If you're not looking at them, your power's not going to be there. So, I realized just playing the run a lot this off season and just learning where your eyes are is where your hands and your feet will follow. So, I learned that a lot. >> Derrick, you're a veteran player now, but do you still feel first round expectations of that kind of weight or do you just feel like I'm just another guy in this league? >> I mean, I'm never going to feel like I'm just another guy. Like I feel like I'm Chop, but the first round all that stuff is it's out the window now. It's just I'm a I'm a NFL player now and I just got to go out there and do my job. >> With that being said, you guys are at this week of practice, you guys have a couple days next week. After that, you guys have a good What will Chop Robinson be doing during that time off away from the facility? Are you being disciplined football shape working on your >> Yeah, focus on the weaknesses, stay in condition, especially with this weather, and then keeping my weight up. I added a few pounds this off season, so that's like the main thing is just just keep my weight up, trying not to lose or gain too much. >> And during the time too, the World Cup's also going to be here. Some other football is going to be played here at the home stadium. You're going to be watching the park taking in some of the international football. >> No, I'll be focused on what I got to do. That's it. >> About how many pounds? >> Uh I'd say like seven or eight. I was I was 258 258 when I finished last season. Now I'm at 265 now, so feel good, feel fast doing anything, so we'll see how it goes. >> What do you feel you play at? >> I'm playing at 265. I'm going to yeah, I'm going to stay this weight, maintain it. >> Do you feel like you can still be chopped at >> Yeah, I still I still feel fast and I still feel even stronger than I were before when I was a lighter, so now I feel I feel the the muscle and everything in my body. >> So, what do you like about what this defense has you doing that makes you think you could take that another leap in your game? >> I really just not thinking, just lining up and playing football and beat the man in front of you. That's the number one job is just whip the man in front of you and then that's it, make the make the tackle and everything. So, really just line up and just play. >> What kind of stuff do you have to do to put all the weight on and put on the protein shakes and do all >> Just eat good, work out, lift. That's really it. Main thing is nutrition, of course. >> Coach I mentioned earlier may want to play you at six eyes sometime, maybe at five by. I know you obviously had a lot of success out wide. What do you think about playing more inside and what that what what you can do in your game there? >> Yeah, I mean whatever wherever he put me at, whatever they the team need me to be, I'm going to do my job at the best, so with with with me putting the weight on, I feel comfortable being a four eye or a nose if I had to, so it don't really matter where they put me at. I'm going to just go out there and be my best. >> When you say weaknesses, what has happened kind of pinpointed that you feel like >> Really just like we've been talking about, just my eyes in the run game cuz that my eyes was affecting everything else, so now that I got my eyes right, I feel like it's my hands and my feet is is doing the doing the natural now, so really just my eyes was the main thing. >> I mean obviously this is your getting ready to play these three days in just past the off season. What's the exact thing >> Just keep keep learning my guys, spending time with the new teammates and everything. That's that's really the main thing, just connecting. Yeah, a lot of guys will hang out outside of this, go to dinner together. On the weekends, we'll hang out together, so we'll find some some outside of this to connect. Yeah, it's it's definitely different. A lot of new guys that's came in, but you could tell everybody got the same mindset. So, we're just going out there and learning about each other, just connecting. That's really the main thing. >> What makes it different? >> Just everybody just showing up and and doing their job. Like it's OTAs, it's optional, but everybody's here, so a lot of people don't miss days. It's a new scheme, new coaching staff, new players. We're all new here, so everybody's connecting and and coming in.

title: Aaron Brewer meets with the media | Miami Dolphins
text: How do you come out here and balance? Obviously, I know you want a new contract. How do you come here and balance that with working hard, you know, showing the guys the way and everything? >> Um just continue to do what I've been doing since I've came to the league. And I know one way to go about things and that's working, getting my head down and keep doing that. And so that's what I come out here and do every day. Lead the guys. I hope to be here for the long run. So I'm trying to put everything in me and into everyone around me to make us the best team we can be. >> And there's been a bit of a change on that left side with Proctor. Just what's it like? I mean, he he just looks massive out there. >> Great. >> So what does it look like? >> [laughter] >> Yeah, yeah, it's it's amazing, man. Just from after working with Andy like doing drills together, then these little team periods we're doing now. Like the mindset he's coming in with is is like almost like a vet, you know what I'm saying? Like he's looking at it as when he was a senior at Bama or junior at Bama. Like he had to young dudes he had come in and he know when you're young you're spinning, you know what I'm saying? So he's trying to do everything he can to get ahead of the eight ball to not act as a rookie. And so I love that from his mentality because he come out here and he's trying to work. He's trying to take in everything he can to be the best left guard next to me as possible. >> What do you feel about where contract talks are right now? Do you think it'll get done? >> Uh I have no clue. I'm letting my agent and the team handle that. >> And what do you feel for D'Onta Hightower watching him? >> Oh, that was amazing. I love it. I love when any player in the NFL get paid, you know what I'm saying? It's just it's to take care of their family and their future. And so I love to see it. I'm happy for him. >> Hey Brew, we've talked a lot about culture change and and that kind of stuff around here. How would you describe kind of the the workmen uh the the work atmosphere around here right now? >> Uh I feel like everybody here is like it's working. You know, it's like a bunch of young dudes and a lot of like one-year dudes as well. And so when you got a lot of guys like that, they're hungry. They're trying They got something to prove. They got something to earn. And so I feel that's the mentality everybody been walking around with. They're coming out head down and trying to work and prove theirself. And so I love it. >> It's obviously a a little bit of a change, at least seemingly to us, in terms of a philosophy shifting to like run first with obviously Achane getting paid. Just how has that looked out there? And then, you know, what's it Obviously, Achane hasn't really, you know, practiced, but like what does the future hold for this run first approach and this obviously this offensive line? >> Um I think it'd be huge, you know what I'm saying? Cuz we seen last year like when we started having success, we was running the ball 20 plus times. And when we did that, we came out with wins. And so, as offensive linemen, just from the results we seen last year, it look like that's the recipe. Then with a talent like Achane, now we got big uh KP right there, Jonah in his original spot he was at in college. Pat going into his third year, you know what I'm saying? Got the reps under him. So, I'm excited for it. It look good. >> How many days you guys have this week? And you guys have a couple days next week. And after that, you guys have a big break. What do you guys do like yourself and other guys to make sure, you know, you guys still stay, as you just mentioned, behind the eight ball, keep your reps up and all that, you know, make sure y'all are >> Uh most of the guys, they stay out here. And so, they be like even before we came to OTAs, we was out here working. Guys come up to the facility. We doing like me and Pat, we doing boxing on the side. A bunch of guys from offensive line, DBs, linebackers, we all be going to Solidcore together, doing Pilates. So, just trying to just still keep that camaraderie and team bond even when we not here in the facility. Like if you out here, we we sticking together, hanging out, doing something, getting some work together. >> And during that break, there's also a week of other football being played here at your stadium. You guys into the World Cup? And you guys been partaking in any games here at >> Uh I've never been to a football game. So, [laughter] um I might go out there and attend one, you know what I'm saying? See the vibes. Might take my shirt off, drink a couple beers, so, you know what I'm saying? So, yeah, we'll see. >> You mentioned Jonah switching back to that right side. Just how has he looked? And could you tell like he's a lot more comfortable there? >> Absolutely. Like he's he's very comfortable in that right guard spot. And me personally, like being a guy that played like multiple positions, I didn't think it was like that big of a difference, but like him going back to that right guard spot, it it look like you can tell he is a right guard, you know what I'm saying? So, just the development if y'all been seeing him as well, like just in the drills and the team team run, team pass, he look good out there. I'm excited for him. >> How how excited are you? I see you like explaining things to guys, you know. It's like it's natural for you? >> Uh absolutely, you know what I'm saying? Like I just be trying to be a a servant, you know what I'm saying? That's my job as a leader, like the best leader is the better servant. So, I try to do everything that was poured into me, everything I know, all the knowledge I got, the reps I've had, I'm trying to give that to the next guy. And so, they can give it to the next guy that come in and just keep it going and continue the greatness. Yeah. >> What what does Austin Jackson provide when when he's in there? And what does it mean to just have him around you as he's been working through it? AJ, he mean a lot in there, you know what I'm saying? Cuz he going on a 7-year vet, same as me. He got the experience on him, you know what I'm saying? He been in the room, he done seen a lot of football. So, he able to talk a lot of football, different things he done seen. His knowledge of the game is way ahead of KP or DJ or some of the young guys that came in, like guys on year two and three, he has way more knowledge on them. So, he able to explain things, tell them about different looks, different techniques they can use for different looks when they get them. >> We were just talking about solid core, Pilates, boxing. >> Mhm. >> What does that do for you personally for you guys as a group? And how y'all look out there, you know, doing doing some of these stretches? >> Uh is it I'd say like solid core and boxing like definitely for like offensive lineman, like boxing it get your boxing is a lot of footwork, you know what I'm saying? And then it get your hands good, like it kind of does I be saying all the time it's like your feet and hands are connected and disconnected at the same time, if you know what I'm saying? Like your feet got to be able to ground and move and your hands got to move as individuals as well. So, I feel like boxing is great for that. Pilates and solid core, that's for the little muscles, like that's what help you last throughout the season. Like we always Everybody do squats, bench press, power clean, such, but that's working the big muscles. The little muscles what that longevity, you know what I'm saying? And just how you nimble and better to move and last longer in this league. >> Is that something new for you, or you think that's something you've been working throughout your whole career? >> I've been doing it for a long time. So, I had like a guy back home in Dallas. He used to work with me. He do a lot a lot of mobility training. And so, it's always a lot of little muscles and like getting in uncomfortable weird positions and getting strong in those weird positions. And so, I feel like it correlates. Like I didn't have 3 4 years of not missing a game until last year. So, yeah. >> How How does this tie How does this Malik Willis compare to the youngster that you knew back in Tennessee? >> It's a lot different. Well, I wouldn't even say it's a lot different cuz he he's still the same guy, you know what I'm saying? But, you can tell his game been developed over time from him going to Tennessee, him going to Green Bay, and just having that experience and it's built. Like he has more knowledge of the game. I feel he's more comfortable in the game as well now. So, it's just dope to see the development and how far he came so far. >> What's he like with y'all in the locker room? I mean, you just see him here, he's a little quieter. What would you describe his personality here? he kind of the same way, but he he's real like he's he's a he's a he's for the boys, you know what I'm saying? But, he he's not over talkative, but he talk, you know what I'm saying? When he talk, it's meaningful. And so, he he cool. He hang out with the guys. He he a good guy. >> Yeah. I hadn't seen you since the All-Pro nod. So, first, congratulations. But then also, how do you build upon that success that you had last year? >> Uh keep pushing for more. I feel like every year is a new year. And so, every year you got to prove yourself again. And so, like this year, like I was second team All-Pro last year. This year, I want to be first team All-Pro. Wasn't Pro Bowler last year. Want to be Pro Bowler this year. Not a nominee for Defensive Player of the Year. Want to be Defensive Player of the Year. So, that's what keep pushing me and keep me thriving every year. Like every year is a clean slate new year. I'm not Amani Hooker from last year. I'm the Amani Hooker that going to put on tape this year.

title: Coach Jeff Hafley meets with the media | Miami Dolphins
text: Oh yeah, >> Kevin Sim cards and all kinds of stuff. >> He's the two phone guy. >> I would never guess that from you. >> Burger account says a lot now. All right. Tra, we notic Aram Brewer wasn't here last week at the OTAA session. Is he here now? And what was the reason for last week? >> Yeah, family obligation that we knew about. He's here and he'll be back out there today. >> Is is anyone missing >> from today? >> No, nobody's missing. >> We got them all here. >> What have you been told if anything about if there are any positive indicators regarding the ruer contract talks? Um, Sully and I have had talks, but I think those are between Sully and I as you'd imagine I'd answer. Um, I love Brewer. I love the way he's practiced. I love the way he's gone about his business, and hopefully that gets ironed out. >> For Brewer, he's going to have potentially a rookie on his left and a secondear guy on his right. Is this a time period where he builds trust in those guys so that when you get into training camp in the season, it's not he feels a need to overcompensate for maybe young guys making young mistakes? I think it's a whole line. I mean, I think those guys in general all have to work together probably more so than any other unit um on the field. Whether it's in the run game, in combination blocks, whether it's in pass protection when we're sending overloads and twists and stunts, it's got to be they got to feel each other. They got to communicate, but they all have to be on the same page. So, I don't just think it's one guy. I think it's all the guys who have to learn how to play together and help each other out. And anytime you have young guys on an offensive line, the older guys all got to step up and and help them out. So, um, yeah, I I think it will be Brewer. I think it will be Jonah. I think it'll be Austin. I think it'll be all of them. >> We know that, uh, Malik Willis is the presumptive starter. What do you want to see from Quinn Yers this this mini camp and in training camp? >> Yeah, I want I want Quinn to continue to get better and battle and and compete and do everything he can to show us that he's the best quarterback um, on the field. I want everybody at every position to do that. Um, you know, Quinn's done a nice job. He's got familiarity with some of the scheme. Um, you know, and I think he's gotten better. He's made some really good throws. He's learning the offense and, um, you know, I'm really pleased with where he's at right now. >> What have you seen from him specifically, uh, in the in the OTAAS that, um, impressed you or that he needs to work on? >> Yeah, he's smart. Um, just standing back there from a defensive perspective, he knows to go. He knows where to go with the football. He gets rid of it on time. and he sees the defenses really well. There's sometimes when he'll hide his eyes really well. A lot of quarterbacks like to start down the middle of the field early in the down. Usually when they hit their back foot, they got to kind of get into their pro uh progression, which you guys, if you watch, you'll see. Uh but he'll hide it for a long time. I mean, he'll even throw some no look passes where I'll go up to him, be like, "If there's a rush, buddy, that ain't happening." You know what I mean? Like he'll be looking over here and give one of these. And so I've had to tell him a couple times not to get too bored because the rush will be coming after him soon. and I'll make sure if a quarterback's going to give us no looking no looks that he'll get hit from the other side fairly quickly. Um, but I really have been pleased with him. He's he's really grasped everything well. He sees it well. He processes really quickly and I I think he's improved and um I like being around him. You talked about Malik and that for a guy who wins outside of structure as frequently as he does, how can you have him work in this stage when there's not a lot of quarterback runs that you can design? >> Well, he's got to play quarterback right now. There is no um there's not a lot of team in in any practice setting, right? I mean, anytime we practice, whether it's team run, team pass, uh just move the ball periods two minute in practice, I want to see him go through his progression. um you know, get rid of the ball on time. And at the same time, if it's not, then I want him to play the game like he would in a game. Don't just stand there in the pocket, take five hitches, and let guys run by you because any quarterback who does that is going to get sacked in a game. And I think you create really bad habits. Those guys who can't do what he can do, they better step up and throw the ball or they're going to take a lot of sacks. Now, Malik's got the ability to sit in the pocket, go through his reads, and if things break down, and he should work outside the pocket because he's going to put stress on the ends. He's going to make sure our pass rush lanes are good because if you don't have good pass rush lanes against him and you have a huge B gap or a gap, he's going to step up and he's going to be gone. So, he puts stress on the defense and he needs to practice like that, right? So, I think it's I think there's a fine line um when you don't want to do too much of that, but I want him to play the game within the game a little bit. Seven on seven, not a huge fan of seven on seven cuz I don't think it's real football. I think from a defensive standpoint, when you're playing some vision, bless you, when you're playing some vision and break coverages and you're just kind of setting as a linebacker and you're anticipating a throw, a lot of times you can feel the rush and break. So, I think it I don't think it's real for defense and I don't think it's real for the timing and the pressure of the offense. But seven on seven is a really good time for him where stay in the pocket and get rid of the ball on time and there is no rush. So, it's kind of like part to hole. Um, I thought Malik had a really good practice on when did we practice last Friday? Yeah, we practiced Friday. I thought he had a really good practice Friday. He looked really confident. He stepped into his throws. The ball came out on time. Um, he hit some big throws in the red zone. I thought it was one of his best days. And I think what you're going to see, and I know I'm being long with you right here, but I think what you're going to see is we've been really heavy on the installs and we're starting to come back to like install one and two now. So, it's a second time through. So, you can see the confidence almost the way he's stepping up and throwing because he's seeing it better, right? We've installed a lot just to try to get it in and, you know, have film of it as we get in the training camp in the season. Um, but I think you can see the confidence building now that we're kind of going back through it again. >> That's kind of an interesting segue. Then I wanted to ask like what changes between OTAA and mini camp? Is there a material difference or is it like a natural progression of everything you've been learning throughout your >> um no mini camp the the only if I'm just going to be completely honest with you guys the only thing different in mini camp is we're going to meet with them in the afternoon and watch tape. Now what I've said to both sides of the ball we've had a lot of install so for these three days I kind of want to go back and pull from the early installs and not continue to add at this point. So, I had that conversation on with the defense and the offense. Let's not add at this point. Let's just repeat some stuff so these guys can do it again. Um, that's probably the biggest difference. There's really not much. We'll do some more uh team combined a little bit more maybe, but you guys shouldn't notice a huge difference. >> Kind of connecting with that as well. You know, you've said the past couple practices, the voluntary workouts that everything's been going on that you've been observing, like what do you expect or hope to get out of the next three days from this group as you know, we kind of start evolving quickly and getting closer to training camp? >> A higher level of execution if I'm going to ask the guys to repeat installs for the second time and it won't be the first time they're doing it. I want to see who can retain and who can execute at a high level. Um, you want to see the chemistry, the chemistry on both sides of the football, the communication, and just a higher level of execution. We've got them to the point right now where I told him today, I love the way they're practicing, the way they're running to the ball, the way they're competing, the energy that they're practicing with, just the way they're running from drill to drill. And I kind of feel good about the structure of that. And I I don't think because it's mini camp. I think because it's a further week in and next week, I hope it's even better. I want to see the execution get better. Um, I want to see who can take what we've done over the past however many weeks and improve. I think that's going to be really important. >> Are Tyrell Dodson and Jacob Rodriguez essentially competing for the same green dot position? >> Um, I think they're just competing to play linebacker and we'll put the best linebackers on the field. um whether we have two in the game at a time, three in the game at a time or some different packages, I think there's competition amongst all those guys, but I wouldn't call it like a battle for the green dot. Um we've mixed around who's wore the green dot in practice. When I was in Green Bay, I in practice truthfully, I had the safeties in the green dot. I've had all the linebackers in green dot because I want them to hear how the call comes in so they can start training for that cuz I think the misnomer is um oh he's not he won't be able to handle the green dot. This guy can't handle the green do I don't believe in that. I believe you can teach guys and over time train them all so if they have to call it they have to call it. So when we get into training camp we'll figure all that out. T Dot's uh done a great job with the green dot in the past. He's a great communicator. Um, and and he's been doing a good job calling it here. Jacob's learning. Now in college, you actually have the helmetto helmet communication, which is nice because it's not the first time that they're doing it. But it will be good eventually to hear my voice and how I call it in. There's kind of a rhythmic cadence to that, right? Because some of the calls can get lengthy even on defense. So, it'll be good for all those guys to hear it. We don't have the safeties in the helmets now, but that's a good reminder. I should >> should make note of that. Along those same lines, I know in the past Jordan Brooks hasn't been, you know, necessarily a fan of having the green dot. Just with you what you just said, has he even, you know, >> Oh, he's worn it and he's called it and I just I I think he did a really good job with it. Um whether or not that's how we'll go during the season, that's that's not what's important to me right now. It's sometimes it's nice to force guys to be uncomfortable, get them out of their comfort zone, and then they start to realize that they can do it and they can get comfortable. It's just reps, you know, and it's just time and it's just, you know, straining to do it. And we'll figure that out in training camp, but for right now, we're rotating who's doing it, when they're doing it, and that's very important to me because you never know when he's going to have to do it in a game, and he's definitely capable of doing it. half. Last week we saw um you guys were doing a lot of uh running I mean passing plays and we saw Jaylen Wright in there and not a lot of Ali Gordon. What did that I guess does that tell us the way that you're thinking about using them that Jaylen would be more of a receiver and and and >> Ali I I just think that's like I can honestly tell you that's coincidence. That was not planned. So, it's just the plays you watched or maybe it was scripted or maybe Ali got plays in another period, but that's pure coincidence there. >> How would you describe the the chemistry building process between Malik and his wide receivers? >> I think it's it's a work in progress. Um, we've had six practices with limited reps. So, I just think it's going to take time. Um, I think it's improved. I just it's going to be a work in progress and it's going to take a lot of reps just like it would with any new quarterback and new wide receiver group. Um and then you add in that we got a lot of young wide outs that just came in. But whoever is playing quarterback right now, it's Malik, it's Quinn, it's Cam. Um it's just it's just going to take time with the rhythm. >> Just following up on that with the install with the receivers, the youth there. Is there anything that stood out in that wide receiver room for you? Can you tell at this stage any surprises or guys that you're like, "Okay, maybe maybe this guy can have a role for us this year." >> Um, it's hard to say because I don't know if I came in with any expectation or I hadn't really seen these guys live. I mean, I think that's a a group that, you know, I want to see who can continue to get better, learn the offense, run routes, what their skill set is, whether it's Malik in the slot, you know, I think he's done a really good job with the catch and run. I think he's get getting better as a route runner. Um, you know, then, you know, guy like Tolbert, you can move him around and do a lot of different things with him. I just from from those guys just in general, it's just going to be improvement and we'll tell in training camp. Um, but I I didn't really have any expectation when I came in to say, "Wow, that's a big surprise to me." Um, so we'll see as we get going and we start to play real football. >> What are the ways you feel your defense can benefit? Uh, what are the ways you feel your defense can benefit Chop Robinson? >> Um, well, hopefully he becomes an every down player. I mean, I think, you know, the easy answer is his pass rush, his get off, his ability to affect the quarterback, but I'm looking for a lot more from Chop. You know, he's going to play a position where he's going to line up in a nine technique and play on tight ends and he has to set the edge, and he's going to have to reduce down to a six technique and play through tight ends. He might reduce down and play a five technique. There's going to be pass rush times when he's going to be coming off the edge. We might slide him around, move him around uh to put him in good situations, but he needs to become a complete football player um going into year three. And we have high expectations for him. We need to coach him. We need to develop him. But the guy's got such a good attitude. He's working so hard and I'm excited to see where that goes. Thank you, guys. >> Thanks, guys. I'll see you guys out there.

title: Aaron Glenn OTA Press Conference (6/2) | New York Jets
text: Good morning. >> So, a lot hasn't really changed from the last time uh we have spoke. Um I I do want to commend the players of their [snorts] participation in uh in this phase. Um it really shows a sign that the guys are all in and um the phases have been good up to this point. Um also last time I talked to you guys ex exactly how we operate within these phases as far as the install is concerned and the one thing that we really been focused on is the detail and the execution about how we go about doing things. Um cuz obviously the physical part is something that you just can't do within these phases. So man, just making sure that we're on point with everything we're trying to do when it comes to the execution uh has been good. Uh just to give you guys a little insight exactly how we've been operating this week. Um so last yesterday we focused on really a third and two to six day which for the most part I expect our offense to win a lot of those. Um which is usually tough for a defense. So defense if we can get within 50% of that uh you really do a really good job. Today it'll be more third and seven plus which again it flips. So the advantage should be defense in this uh this situation and um man offense got to work their ass off to really get uh first downs and this. So um man, I want to really work those situations, make sure we get good at those situations. Then come tomorrow, we'll have a phase two day and then Thursday we get right in the red zone. So we're really hitting some situations this week which is really good for our guys and again the detail and the execution of it is what we've been focused on. So uh in saying that, uh any questions? In the practice setting, what do you want to see from the quarterbacks in a third and seven situation as far as weighing whisk or risks? >> Yeah. Um again, usually when you just look at the numbers, um like that's more an advantage of defense. So, as many times that we can get completions and that to get uh getting the first down, get our first downs is what we're really looking for. Um and actually just knowing exactly where to go with the ball. Um and making sure we just don't put oursel in a situation where we make mistakes of giving the ball to the defense. How how how has it been different for you now that you're doing competitive stuff, you were falling the defense. >> Yeah. >> As opposed to last year and how are you balancing like I know last year you wanted to be everywhere. >> How are you doing that? text: Afternoon. Welcome. >> What was your reaction, your thoughts when and who told you that you had been traded to the Patriots? >> Uh my agent. Uh let me stand up. my agent. So, >> where did this passion come from for the Patriots? And what do you say to the fans now that you're here that are going to be watching you every week? >> Passion cames from uh wanting to be like my big cousin. He was a big Patriots fan and I want to, you know, like I said, I want to be like him and as far as I can remember, you know, I was a Patriots fan and and uh to the fans, you know, it's time, you know, better late than never. We right on time and and I'm so excited. You know, I can't wait to get out there in Gillette Stadium and, you know, hit a crowd and make plays and have fun. >> What excites you about playing with Drake? >> Everything, man. So, you know, when I heard that, I was like, "Wow, I that was impressive." You know, obviously I I heard great things about him, but that part alone tells me a lot about him and how how much he loves his job and, you know, he studies and everything. So, yeah. >> TJ, um, first, welcome to New England. Um, but with Drake specifically, a lot of people talk about your abilities as a deep ball, uh, receiver and a lot of people talk about his skills as a deep ball passer.
