Have made it one of like the, you know, the best room in the team or one of the best in the league. just the passion that everybody plays with. We had some real passionate guys in our room last year. Um, you know, whether that was good passion or bad passion, it was just, you know, it was we have a very passionate group and sometimes we did have to get it under control, but that was that was the identity, you know, just playing with energy, playing with passion, and just being dominant. >> what is it like to have Josh back, Eric back from injury, and and how are they sort of progressed as as younger players? Um, it's obviously good to have everybody back. Um, it's it's cool to watch them progress, you know, being with them as rookies and watching them get better and get ready to take the next step. So, you know, it's it's exciting to see the young guys get better and get more opportunities. >> And no defensive tackle was drafted by the Pats last or this year, but, you know, they signed two young guys. Do you view that as sort of a vote of confidence that they didn't feel like they needed to draft? >> 1000%. you know, um, you see the teams I've been in in the past, you know, they've drafted two, three tackles every year I was there. So, you know, just to have a team not drafting the D tackles, it kind of says a lot. They have confidence in our room. So, >> what's up with the uh the brace? >> Uh, it's a preventative thing. I don't have anything wrong with my elbow. It's kind of I hyperextended it my first year in the league, so I just wear it so that I don't, you know, >> the cutup sleeve fashion statement, you know, starting a new trend. This thing doesn't fit inside. It's too big. So, >> thank you. >> Thanks, Carter. >> Thank you, guys. Y'all have a good one.

title: Patriots Offensive Assistant Coaches Address the Media | Patriots Press Conference
text: But it's it's interesting because I remember my first year last year with Josh and he would say things and you know a lot of guys like myself felt like we were drinking through a fire hose and then now that we have a grasp of everything that's going on then he mentions it again and I'm like oh that's why you're making such a big deal about it last year. Um so I think the quarterbacks are experiencing that. I think Drake uh being in his second year instead of focusing on the okay what is my job and my role now it's okay what were the little uh tidbits that Jos was trying to teach me and now we can grasp those things. Is there a value to have a rookie in the room? I don't know, every year, but just you got a new guy, you got to reexlain it to somebody, the other guys got to hear some of the basics again. I is that, you know, you're dealing with Baron a little bit. >> I I I think it's a positive because it forces the older guys to hear from scratch again, so they get uh just that reinforcement. >> Um and then for a young guy, it's cool to see his evolution from going from college to now into the National Football League. It helps your, you know, your teaching skills a little bit because you have to find different ways to reach him based on where he was at and what he's, uh, been exposed to in college. Um, but also keeps things fresh and light and, you know, the guys jab him a little bit because things that they had issues with last year, they're smooth sailing now. And now that Baron's going through it and he's maybe trying to figure out where he fits in it all, you know, they're poking fun at them. We got like a uh got a blender in the in the quarterback room that's plugged in and every time a quarterback gets confused, we press the blender. >> And so we press [laughter] >> No, it's a different machine. We got a couple appliances in the quarterback room. We got a blender, a juice machine, but Brener, uh Baron, we press a blender a little bit on them. [laughter] >> What I know it's been early, but what have you seen from since he's got here? >> Yeah, a kid that's super excited to learn. He's curious, which I think is the coolest uh thing about getting these young quarterbacks is just uh the amount of information that they want to know. So, he's curious. He's chomping at their bit to get as much information as he can. And I think the time of year we're in now is one where he can focus on learning the system. I don't think it's realistic to ask these guys to come in and compete as soon as they get here because there's so many things that they aren't necessarily used to. So, the spring we focus around getting them caught up to where the veterans are, uh being able to operate and execute. Um, so that's what he's been focused on right now. >> Knowing what you know about AJ Brown, just what are your thoughts on adding him to this offense? >> Exciting. Uh, and I guess the wheels would be spinning to about all the different things that you could potentially do with someone with his skill set, you know, strong, physical guy that can win in contested catch situations that still has the ability to stretch the defense and um, just excited about all the possibilities. Yeah. I I know there are some reports this offseason that different teams wanted to talk to you maybe to be offensive coordinator and you decided to stay here. Just for you, what went into that decision to come back here? >> I I think a number of things. One is uh just the um the culture that we've created here like working underneath Coach Brabel and learning from Josh McDaniels. I think that's an opportunity that I don't take for granted. Um and they're two completely different personalities, so I get the the best of both both worlds in that. I feel like there was a little bit of unfinished business with where things ended off. if I wanted to, you know, come back and continue to help uh Drake develop and Tommy and Baron and and all the other players that are on this team. I think lastly is uh personally I'm not in a rush to get there. You know, I I think I'm focused on developing staying power once I do get there as opposed to being the first to get there or being fast to get there. Um so I think I've just been really intentional throughout my entire career about trying to do things the right way. Um so all those three things went into Is your goal to get there and maybe even go head coach one day or >> uh one day, you know, but I feel like that's so far off from now, you know. I think my goal today is making sure we go out there and perform and execute and my goal tomorrow is to make sure we kill it in the meeting room and we learn something and we're 1% better uh tomorrow than we were today. Um I think all those things down the road if we do a good job will take care of themselves. So I don't put too much stock into that. I just try to focus on you know executing my job at a high level. Normally, normally we don't get that reaction when we show off faces. So, I like that. >> We'll see how it goes. Hopefully, you know, we put on a show for you guys today and go out and execute. >> How we doing? >> How you doing? >> Good. Uh, back at the combine, Vable said he wanted to challenge you guys to come up with new ideas as coaches, new schemes. What's that process like? Is it all of you guys in a room just throwing stuff against the wall? >> Uh, no. It's it's more intentional than that. you know, we we uh have things that we want to attack and coach McDaniels does a good job of setting us in the right direction on what we want to study. But it's fun because it sends us down rabbit holes. You know, I found myself watching division 2 football games and trying to figure out what guys are doing. Uh to be creative and what are the next step and if anything fits us, is it worth, you know, bringing to the table? Um so it definitely gets your creative juices flowing. Um but it's been a fun project this offseason and hopefully you guys see some of those things uh come today. I apologize if you've been asked this, but um Drake, a lot of people talk about him as a deep ball passer. His ability to do that, bringing a guy like AJ Brown, who is a known deep ball threat, what does that do for someone like Drake? >> Uh I I think it gives him a little bit of confidence knowing that he has someone who's uh had success uh throughout his career in the National Football League doing something that Drake excels at. Um, and I think it's just exciting for the entire offense cuz when you add a guy like that, it dictates coverages. Um, and it gives you favorable matchups across the board. So, I think everybody on offense is excited, uh, but should benefit. >> Two more guys. >> An extremely hard worker on the field. Um, and a a great teammate. >> How did you see him sort of grow? Uh it was it was um you know coach Moore did a heck of a job. Rob Moore was receiving coach at the time and just watching him come in and uh obviously he was a really good college football player, but then just watching him uh continue to grow in his work ethic and his work habits and uh just grow into a professional um through that toutelage of of Rob and obviously uh Todd and as the coordinator, Arthur and then Todd as the coordinators and then um obviously Mike was very involved and hands- on just like he is now. So with all the all the young guys, uh just him that process of coming as a rookie and learning how to practice the way that uh you do in the NFL and then uh and then obviously with Rob and uh Todd teaching him fundamentals and techniques of playing receiver in the NFL and he just took it all a shot, worked his butt off and uh developed into the player that he is today and beginning of the development of where he is today. >> Sure. Awesome. Thank you so much Paulo. Sorry. Uh I think it's going to be what Taylor was going to ask anyway. He was really productive when he was about 25% in the spot first two years when was tapered off a little bit last year the year before. So I need 5%. >> How do you envision him working in this stuff? >> I I try to teach all the players uh all the positions so that we can move them around based on matchups in the game plan wherever Josh wants to be or where we think we might be able to create a mismatch. Um, so I think that's going to you play itself out in the course this offseason in a training camp or whatnot. That's a cool right there, right? >> No, it's supposed to relax. [laughter] >> Uh, it's working. Uh, no, I I think that's, you know, that's going to play itself out. Uh, AJ certainly has the skill set to be able to play multiple PSA, so we'll see how that shakes out over the next couple months. >> And when it comes to teach when it comes to teaching conceptually, is that something that you've done in other places or is that more unique to the system that you've got here? Uh, I definitely try to teach that way most of my coaching career because I don't think it's fair to guys to say, "Well, you're just going to play this position and then all of a sudden there's a, you know, somebody needs a shoelace or a need at another position and you go somewhere else as opposed to, uh, you know, right to the next guy in line." And so, uh, I try to give everybody a chance to compete, see the field as much as they want to. I think the only way to do that to learn more in one spot. Well, you haven't known him for a while working with him in Tennessee. Just studying him the last year or two of Philly, what do you think the biggest difference is in his game now from when the last time you worked with him? >> I I think he's grown in a lot of areas both physically, you know, and mentally. You can see his understanding of the game continues to improve. Uh I think the way that he sets up different releases and moves has improved. Um obviously, you know, he's a a big physical and strong receiver, but he's done a really good job of working at the top of the route, the catch point. And so, you know, it's cool to see him continue to grow and and just in the couple of conversations with I've had with him today, I I anticipate him uh staying hungry to keep improving. >> When it comes to him getting him acclimated into the system, obviously new system for him, just what's that process like? like do kind of give them a little bit or what do you kind of do with >> Yeah, I you know I I think you have to go at a pace uh that is kind of sinking in and again my relationship with AJ is going to help kind of know whether it's landing or or whether we need to hover there for a minute. Um we'll bring him along as he's able to uh handle it. I I know from experience with him he's a pretty sharp guy. So I think it'll pretty cool. And you were you kind of see how did you see them broke in his like early years a little? So, uh, came in as a young guy with a bunch of the physical tools. Uh, you ever was raw and won a lot of fights just by winning with physical one-on-one matchup. Rob Moore did an outstanding job, but then he was our receiver coach. And I watched AJ for the first two years I was there as a tight end coach and kid, the coordinator, watching his understanding of the system. And then when, you know, when we got Julio in 2021, he moved over to Z receiver and did a lot more on the strong side. just his kind of conceptual awareness of where he fit in the big picture uh really became impressive. I think he did a great job with his hands at the line of scrimmage. Uh you know, Rob worked very hard at that with him and you know, I think he when he sets his mind to fixing somebody, he's going to get >> AJ Brown hasn't been shy about talking about variable and how he really got on him when he was a rookie trying to get him better. From your perspective, how did you see AJ kind of respond to that challenge and how did that impact his ability to be a player and professional? I think any college player uh who is kind of the guy at his program comes to the NFL and all of a sudden starts getting coached hard, it can be a little bit of like, oh, wait a minute, they're not throwing NIL money at me to keep me here, you know? It's uh it's now my job and my profession, you know. And uh I think anybody's going to have a little bit of kind of I don't want to say push back, but moments where they say, "What's going on here?" I think he very quickly realized uh that Mike cares about him and that uh he wants him to be the best version of himself both on and off the field and and so I think uh AJ got comfortable of it pretty quick. Todd on that, how what did you learn in Tennessee about the type of coaching he best responds to the competitive nature he has and how how do you break the bottom? >> Uh AJ is a very smart player so understanding the why is important to him. So explaining what he has to do is one thing. Why he has to do it is another. Uh I think sometimes players with that kind of football IQ can can kind of go rogue at times if they don't understand exactly why they're supposed to do what they're supposed to do. And and uh AJ always asks those questions. He's not bashful about saying why do why do I have to do that? If you give him a good answer, he's usually going to do it. >> Two more questions here. >> Last year during media day, you mentioned to me how special this wide receiver is. Can you talk to me about the importance of the fit with AJ and how you'd like him to blend in with this group? >> I I can't speak for any of my bosses, but I think part of the reason we feel comfortable about adding him to the the mix is because we know what type of person he is. Um, I I'm very protective of the lighter super room because I know how hard those guys work, how much they celebrate each other, they push each other, the culture of the room that I'm fortunate enough to coach, uh, you know, is is pretty special. Uh, I think AJ is just going to enhance and augment that. And already in the first couple of meetings we've had together, I watch his chemistry with the guys around him and and the comfort level that the guys have uh, with him coming in. I I I anticipate it be a pretty brute. Did you know he was a Beatricer fan? >> I honestly did not. No, I I heard that got that as a tidbit uh walking out, but I I did not know that. Very excited to see him in the Patriot jersey. >> Thanks, Todd. >> Thank you. Thanks. Appreciate >> it. Have a great >> I mean, I would say huge for us offensively, but more so it's about him. I mean, he's a phenomenal dude. Having a chance to kind of get to know him some of the fact the past few months or so has been awesome for me as a coach with the room mentality. just the way he kind of brings that physical mentality, presence, veteran leadership as well. So, with some speedy recovery. >> Now, with him out, how does that kind of impact the way you develop some of those younger tight ends on the roster with them potentially having to see the field more early on? >> Uh, I would say no different. I mean, the entire room is going to be cross strains like I've always been. I have a good mix of what we call our wide tight ends, F tight ends, and fullbacks in my room as well. So, all those guys will know the same positions, inline tight end, being frustrated receiving position. So, that won't change. What was um just Julian? It seemed like he brought a lot of energy and things like that. Um what was it like to just I'm sorry like that. >> Yeah, I talk about that guy all day. Um so I just think the the mentality, the attitude he brought to the table was awesome for us. Um just from a veteran leadership standpoint, physical presence, you can kind of feel the energy when he walked into the room. He practiced the right way, worked his butt off. Uh super smart dude. So, you know, huge huge loss for us offensively, but more so just for him. I'm just praying for a speed of recovery. I'm making sure he stays in the right head space mentally wise. It's going to be a long road. And I told him just make sure during the recovery process you don't separate yourself too much from everybody else cuz I've unfortunately been there too many times already myself as a former player. So but awesome. >> Sorry. Sorry. How do you anticipate just filling that veteran piece of it? Obviously got Hunter in there, but the rest of that group doesn't have a a great deal of kind of NFL experience. How do you anticipate filling the void there? >> Competition. I mean, it's uh and I sometimes hate the phrase, hey, next man up, because every every man's not the same. They're all different, but they're all here for a reason. So, have an opportunity to compete, earn a role, and be consistent with it. Looking forward to it.

title: Josh McDaniels: "I Love the Opportunity." | Patriots Press Conference
text: How would you describe this skill set, Josh? >> Uh big. Very physical. Uh you know, aggressive, explosive. He's got to get hands. Um you know, he's just a competitive guy, you know, and you watch him play and uh there's a there's a force uh to the way that he plays the game. So, uh looking forward to um getting used to the things that he can do that I don't know about, which I'm sure there's, you know, many of those. Had an opportunity to, you know, have a few different receivers come into our system at times and you know, you just you you've heard about him, you've seen him, you watched him play on tape, uh but then to actually get him on the grass and watch him do different things, it just brings the picture to life. So, um looking forward to seeing all those things, you know, as as we can go. >> Trait wise, does this compare to anyone you coached previously? >> Um I don't know. He's uh distinctive. Um Randy was coiled, certainly, and and and fast and all the rest of it. Um I I think they're you know, and I say they meaning um I I've been fortunate to have the chance to be around some really good ones. Um not sure if I've been around one just like him. Uh maybe the closest thing I I've seen was Gronk. So, um he's a big guy, you know, so does a lot of things well and uh looking forward to seeing, you know, how we can acclimate him and fit him into the through the our system. >> Josh, how much do you enjoy this process? You've done it for quite a few years now. Getting a guy who's college and proven and has a catch a weapon that you can use in creative ways, how much do you enjoy this? >> I mean, I love the the opportunity. I love the challenge of um you know, our our system has always been the same in terms of you know, get the players, find out what they do best, and then try to figure out how to fit, you know, what we're doing around the players. You know, that's the most important thing. So, um, you know, could some things change or we do some different things based on you know, what we see Romeo do and what AJ can do and what some of the other guys did. Sure, you know, that that had that happens every year. So, um, that's an exciting opportunity for us as coaches to just evaluate it. Give everybody a bunch of opportunities and then, you know, hopefully we make some good decisions as we head through training camp into the regular season about the best way to use our guys and and to allow them to go out there and make plays. >> How do you go about matching up the skill set of what Drake does really well with a guy like him? >> Very similar. Uh, give Drake opportunities, you know, to to work with him. He's already started uh, you know, with our group that's here and I think they develop a chemistry. [music] You know, and those kind of things happen over time. I don't think >> you've been a force here. >> Um, certainly nothing that they have done apart from one another is going to be that significant until they actually get an opportunity to rep together. So, uh, I'm looking forward to that opportunity, you know, this week, rest this week, next week, you know, and and obviously to training camp. But, those things kind of have have a knack of figuring themselves out, you know, and uh, they'll, you know, I think one of the things that's [music] really cool about veteran players when you when you acquire them like this is you get to sit out and ask them you know, how they see the game. What are they good at, you know? Cuz they've done a lot of things that maybe I haven't done, you know, or or called or coached. So, uh, yeah, I've done that with players before. I'm looking forward to doing that with AJ. >> Remember asking you last when the season started, you know, any pressure on you or on Drake to get the ball to to Diggs at the time. Similar question now, like is there more stress on anybody in terms of the decision makers offensively to make sure you use a player like that. >> I mean, I think if if you get guys like this that certainly have a history of being super productive, >> I think it's just our job to make sure that they're involved significantly in what we're doing. You know, doesn't mean we can guarantee the ball goes to him on certain amount of plays, not necessarily, but you know, that's I think that all happen and and shake out over time as it did with Steph, you know. I remember our first OTA days with Randy. I mean, I don't know if he could complete a pass honest to God at that time. So, I mean, it was you know, it's a process. And hopefully if we're doing our job the right way, which I have a great deal of of faith and trust in our staff, we'll figure out what spots to put them all in and and then call those things that our guys do the best, you know, and we'll let Drake make the decision about where the ball goes. >> We can ask Drake. How would you describe what you've seen from him in the off season going forward and what you're looking for? Second year worker here. >> Yeah. Intentional. Purposeful every day. Um just you know, it's a different this off season is different than last. Last off season we were just getting to know the language and learning how to operate within a system of offensive football, you know, and this year we're trying to take that and then go to the next phase of that, the next level of that in his case, which is obviously playing the the position of quarterback. So, he knows a hell of a lot more than he did last year at this time. He's trying to either really turn the corner and put bets in things that that he has an opportunity to do that with or we're trying to to learn a few new things and and evolve as a player and as as an offense. So, he's had a great attitude. Super fun to be around every day. He's a sponge like he was last year. It's just that it's a more accelerated of the spot. I know you wanted to be there, but seeing the video did have you broken down his swing? >> Uh yeah, that I wish I was there. I had a a family thing, but uh it's not like the guys had a great time, you know, and and obviously a awesome purpose and cause, so. This group, man, I tell you they they they really rally around one another in in terms of the the things that they're all involved in off the field, which I think is is a great thing for our team, our community, so. Uh you know, that that looks like fun. I missed it. >> Josh, how how disappointed were you to lose Joe Mixon? >> Yeah, that that sucked. You know, he's a First Call for him. I mean, he's a great great kid, great person. He was going to be a really good addition this year. I still see that, you know, down the road, you know. Um but you talk about a team-first guy that works his butt off and was doing a whole lot of things right. Um you know, that's the game we play, you know, unfortunately there's going to be some injuries and you'd have to handle the adversity and move on and find other ways to, you know, to move forward, but I hate it most of all for him because of all the work and and and time that he's spent here and put in so far, so. Um look forward to him having a great rehab and hopefully, you know, getting him back as soon as he's ready. >> What say two more? >> Say it again. >> How's Eli doing rather than Joe? >> Uh good, you know, I mean, the the rookies are they're they're still in the pool. Uh you know, they're swimming a little bit, um which is to be expected at this point, but um making progress every day, learning something new every day. I've said this before you guys, you either do something right or you learn from the mistakes, so every rep should be a beneficial one for us at this time of the year, so. Um Eli has a good good uh attitude and approach, and he's coming out trying to get better every day. >> Josh, you touched on this question. >> touched on the work he's done as a Caleb. How would you assess his sort of maturity uh on both the left and the right side so far? >> Yeah, I mean, you know, that's that's a that's a different challenge, you know, and and you come in and you know, you're used to playing, you know, in in one spot and you know, when you play offensive line in the National Football League as a young player, a lot of times that is your that is your responsibility is to learn a whole bunch of different roles, you know, language is different on one side than the other. Certainly technique and fundamentals are a little different because you're you're working on different sides of the football. So, great attitude awesome kid, uh love his personality, practices his butt off every day, a sponge. Again, we've we've done a tremendous job of bringing a bunch of guys that just want to learn and try to get better and work hard. So, Caleb's at the head of the class in in terms of the rookies for us. >> All right, guys. Thank you.

title: Mike Vrabel on A.J. Brown: "Just Trying to Improve Our Football Team in Every Possible Way."
text: Hey guys. >> Hello. >> How are you? >> Good. How are you? >> Great. Uh, just a couple housekeeping items here. Hold on, Karen. Um, so Doug Marone is going to get his knee cleaned up. Okay. We work our coaches pretty hard here. Um, just like our players. And, uh, so I think it's best just to have that done now so that Doug will be ready to go for training camp and there won't be any setbacks. So, uh, if you don't see Doug out there, that's what's going on there. Uh we have moved uh after some deliberation the mandatory mini camp to next week June 9th, 10th and 11th. Um that'll give us you know Monday to clean up a couple physicals on some guys that weren't here previously and then uh three days of of really good work there. Um and then that will conclude, you know, the veteran offseason program. We'll have the rookies uh for a little bit of time after that and um joint practices. So, uh, as as well as those worked out last year, uh, certainly the one day with, uh, the commanders here and then traveling, uh, to Minnesota, we'll have Indianapolis on the 11th on August 11th, uh, which will be, um, you know, this very good team to go against. This a very good offensive uh, football team. You know, Shane's an excellent offensive coach and excellent head coach, but um very good offensive line, versatility on their defense. So, that'll be an important day for us. And then Philadelphia will come here for the 18th and 19 uh excuse me, 19th and 20th of August. So, that'll allow us to uh to work against an accomplished football team that's uh used to winning and and has a very good football team and great players and well coached. Uh, the last item. Where you at, Julia? Hi, Julia. Congratulations. So, Julia just decided to dabble in a marathon in Oregon and ran it in two hours and 50 minutes and two seconds. Yeah, I know. And and and won. So, congratulations, Julia. And don't keep those things a secret. So, she went and dabbled in a marathon and won. Um, what do you got, Karen? >> Uh, given your relationship with AJ Brown, knowing him as a person and a player, >> how important uh was it for you to make that deal happen? >> Well, not important. I mean, again, I I think that uh just trying to to improve our football team every possible way. Um, you know, give our offense multiple weapons to to build on what we did last year. Um, and I think having, you know, experience with the person, you know, it to be able to add an accomplished NFL football player, receiver, premium player at his position, uh, but somebody that that we also, you know, feel strongly about as as a person and a competitor and as a teammate. Um, you know, I appreciate Elliot for for being able to work and get that done. >> Knowing AJ in your eyes, what makes him such a special wide receiver? Well, I mean, I think he loves football. I think that he um has a physical skill set. I think he's got great body control. I think he's strong at the catch point, but I also think he as he's grown as as a as a player and as a receiver, uh just the nuances of um you know, releases verse press or playing verse bracketed coverages or zone coverages. plays physical with the football and uh you know again has has been productive and and a consistent player. >> You coached him. Did did AJ ever tell you that he was a Patriots fan? >> I think that that was known a long time. You know what I mean? I think I knew that, >> you know, I mean I think he showed me pictures when he was a little kid wearing my jersey and stuff like that >> that that he didn't wear my jersey. Um, yeah. I mean, I think I knew that uh just from the time that he, you know, like I think when we drafted him, he was like, "I wish the Patriots drafted me." And I said, "Well, that's that didn't happen. You know, we the Titans drafted you." So, you know, I think that um you know, there's a you know, the success that the this team had in in those years when, you know, a lot of our players were were growing up. you know, it would be easy to to root for a lot of the players that that played for this team in in the um you know, early 2000s. >> He had a tumultuous time in Philadelphia despite the production and success they had. Why are you confident that won't happen here? >> Uh well, I mean, again, whatever happens or comes up, I think that uh I can't say that there's not going to be things that come up with with AJ with, you know, any single player, right? to think that this is a competitive game, highly competitive. Uh players want to win, players want to do everything that they can to help their team. They want to make sure that people are on the right page. Um so I don't I don't get into a lot of that. I I think what's the most important is that, you know, those things don't carry into the to the locker room, that that they get handled. You see that all the time on the sidelines. Uh we want to have conversations in a meeting room. We want to have conversations at practice. and um you know sometime those conversations are animated but it's all in the the sake of trying to get on the same page and get right. So you know again I don't know what happened. I'm not not trying to figure out what happened in in Philadelphia. I'm I'm trying to focus on what's going to happen here uh and trying to get him acclimated to to what we do and how we do it. >> Mike, there's been a lot of reporting about him having a degenerative knee condition. You're obviously comfortable enough to make the trade for him, but is that something because of your past history you gain a little more comfort and you will have to manage this player though going forward? >> Well, there's a lot again when you get to you talk about 90 guys or 91 guys, there's going to be a different plan for for every single guy. >> Um, and again, I think that looking at the body of work and and the availability that he's been able to have and whether we have to to manage him or anybody else, it's a long season. So, you know, there'll be things that we'll have to deal with. Um, and we'll try to do that accordingly. But, you know, just based on looking at, you know, his his availability and and the games that he's been able to play in uh and be there for his team, I think that hopefully, you know, leads to to to future availability. >> Mike, what do you know about AJ that you hope we and his teammates learn about him? >> Uh, that he that he loves football, that he cares about his team. I think he is uh you know knowledgeable and you know again I think that um he doesn't have to prove anything to anybody. Nobody does. They have to go out there and practice. They have to know what to do. They have to play to to a certain identity uh and and do their job and and focus on that. Nobody needs to to do anything that's you know outside of what we've ever asked any of our players to do. And I'm confident that he'll do that. and you know he's humble, you know, like these are I'm excited to have him get to know our players and our players get to know him and everybody else as we work through the last couple weeks here. >> Mike, is the plan for him to play under the contract that he had with the Eagles? >> I mean, he' been here a day, so I mean, the plan is for him to practice and and try to get acclimated. Um, you know, I don't I don't see anything that would uh preclude him from doing that. I mean, right now, I mean, again, I just excited to add the player. I know the the football team is looking forward to um having him and in practice and get acclimated and whatever that looks like today. So, um you know, by all accounts, um you know, he's ready to go. >> You guys obviously gave up a first round you gave up a first round pick to get him. Do you view this as a win now move? >> Uh, we have, you know, I mean, we have to win. That's our job is to win. You know, that's it's the job and responsibility and the expectations in the National Football League. It's not to to go four and 13 two years in a row if that's what you mean. >> Mike, what went into the decision to put Julian on? >> Julian won't be able to to play the season. That that's plain simple. So devastating, awful. I really enjoyed the person and um want to have him around here as much as we possibly can, but uh just because he wouldn't be able to to play uh this season. So, um you know, that's just disappointing because of just the impact that he made in a short amount of time with his teammates and then just the person that he is, the way that he practiced and you know, so again, we'll we want Julian to be a part of us as much as possible. just not going to do that on the field this year. >> Football injury. Yeah. Was that something that happened in practice? >> That was something that happened in practice. Yes. >> Can I confirm, did AJ already take his physical? Did he pass it if so? And what do you expect from his practice? It's uh participation today. >> Yep. AJ uh passed the physical and we'll we'll be out there in some capacity. We'll have to monitor it. Um you know, just because he hasn't been with us and so I think it's important that that we do that. but also important that he be out there and kind of see how we do things. There's I'm sure there's 32 different stretching routines and 32 different individuals and you know kind of where everything goes and I think that's important process too and hopefully he can um you know know enough to to line up and and take some snaps in in some of the the team periods as well. >> 80% of the time I believe it was last year with the Eagles. You mentioned the intelligence. Do you see him as more of an X in your system or more of a chess piece you like? Well, I mean, I think all the guys right now are going to learn a lot of the different positions. I think that the ones that have been here, that's how Todd's tried to install the offense is to know um what each player has on each concept and and learn it that way. And I would imagine that AJ would would do the same. And um give the give guys the ability to line inside, Kyle or line outside and you use you know, Romeo inside. Um, so I think to try to just right now he's going to have to learn one position and I would imagine that's going to be outside, but as that grows I I know that that will be, you know, across the board and I think that that's hopefully something that he's looking forward to do. But you have to learn one before you can learn them all. curious with um the event with Drake the other day, what was it like to just see the team come together in that way and show support and also kind of have that little competitiveness but also just the camaraderie of a team. Well, I just, you know, I think it just speaks uh volumes to to Drake and and Ann Michael, just the people that they are to >> to organize something like that for the fans and, you know, where it was and the amount of the families that were out there that's uh 10,000 people and I would say most of them were were families. Uh the support that he got from from the players and I could imagine when they saw that it may rain and guys could have could have bailed on them and I think it was just an amazing night, a fun night. um a little bit of competit some guys that I thought were better at soft. Marcus Jones played a hell of a second base and you know I was pretty impressed um and and I think the guys had a good time and it was for a great cause. >> Saw you hit and I think it was like a crying face towards Christian at one point. Did your competitiveness come out a little bit? >> No, I was not. I was trying to coach and I you know we I the umpires were not interested in any of our replays uh that that we thought and you know at that point in time it was seven nothing. And I was like, we're going to have to try to keep this thing close and they they didn't want to try to do that. So, um, just having fun and it was, you know, it was great to see Gonzo and, uh, everybody else that came to support Drake and and Michael about AJ for quite some time now. At what point did you know that this was a move that you guys wanted to make and just could you >> Well, I think there were conversations early on and then you know those those stalled and uh had had to wait and then Elliot texted me yesterday afternoon you know sometime after 4:00 that that it got done and I said great job thank you and when's he coming in with >> the addition of Romeo and AJ obviously some guys in that wide receiver room won't get the same amount of opportunities as last year uh do you feel like you need to communicate with those guys about that or just let it play out in practice? >> Well, practice is critical. I think the opportunities that everybody gets are going to be earned. Um, and I think that there's a spot for everybody. I think that, you know, guys are um give us reasons to to give them opportunities. They create their own opportunities. And so, um, I can't predict the future. I don't know what that means. I know that I'm excited about the different versatility and the different skill sets that we have. Uh, and guys are continuing to improve. Um, you know, Kyle, there was, you know, maybe a a drop yesterday that led it led to an interception and, you know, quick conversation with Kyle just saying, "Hey, listen, that's the first quarter. There's nothing we can do about it." And, uh, hope the defense held him to a field goal shortly thereafter, was able to create a 60-yard touchdown and and make a hell of a catch. And those are that's why you practice and that's try why you try to script the practice is as similar to a game as you possibly can. It's a long game. There's going to be mistakes that happen early on in the game. It's how we respond to them and it was really good to see Kyle do that. So there's a lot of guys in there that are working hard and hopefully Drake just throws to whoever is open >> as an organization. Mike, >> there appears to be a contract situation involving Christian Gonzalez. Are you hoping or working toward resolving that so you see him at mini camp and down the road? >> Well, I think that there's um you know, the the contract is is the business and and the professional side of this uh the personal side. Um, I don't want to get let anything interfere with that. I want Christian to be ready when he comes back and and I would imagine that he would be here next week and if he is, then we'll coach him and be ready to move on and and get him ready and get him ready to help us and, you know, and help himself and and contracts are part of professional sports. I understand that. Um, but I also know that those should should remain private and uh like any contract, you know, you want to make sure or negotiation that that everybody feels like they get something out of it. And I'll leave it at that. Thank you. Appreciate it. Enjoyed practice.

title: The NFC West Just Got a Lot More Interesting!
text: [music] Hey, hey, hey. >> [music] >> What's up, twelves? Welcome to the Seahawks Collective presented by Hog Media. Clearly, I did not get the hat memo tonight, but what a Tuesday show we have for you. Lots to cover on this offseason show, but only 99 days until the Seahawks kickoff, which is going to come very quick. Uh, but the big topic for tonight is that the NFC West just got a whole lot more interesting. Uh, potentially some things to be excited about, but also to keep your antenna up. So, to break it all down with me tonight, Brian Nemhauser, our Hawk blogger, Rob Stton from the Seahawks draft blog, and Michael Shawn Dugar covering the Hawks for the Athletic. As always, please use the chat, ask these guys questions. If I don't ask a question that you have on your mind, use it. You have them here. They are the best Seahawks insiders in the world. Literally, we are global because we have Rob. So, use them. Uh 100%. But man, huge week. Lots of breaking news even just today. Uh but first, let's just check in with everyone. Rob, has it cooled down in England? I know last week, I think you said it was like the hottest day in history over there. >> Yeah, it has cooled down a little bit. It's still quite warm. Uh a little bit wetter this week, but um yeah, nice. And you know, we're all kind of hoping the weather's going to stay because the World Cup starts next week. So, what happens in England when the World Cup's on is it's everyone excuse to get the barbecues out. uh and and watch a whole bunch of football. So um so yeah, the country is kind of excited at the moment uh with with rich in hope that England are going to have a good tournament as well. >> And what's give us like the one thing we should know about England in this World Cup. >> Um no well everybody in the country is desperately hoping I you know I don't not not to say anything disparaging about the Mariners but the desperation of Mariners fans perhaps to win a World Series. I would probably times that by about 100. Uh that is how it feels over here for England to win a World Cup. So, uh we're all on uh on the edge here. Uh desperately hoping that this is going to be the year. I I can't say I'm overly confident, but they're probably one of about six teams to chance. >> All right. Well, we will see. And Brian, what's up with you this week? >> Oh, I don't know. massive trade coverage and [laughter] stuff. I'm sure we'll be talking about uh the rest of this show. But yeah, uh doing the single parent thing while my lovely wife is off on a solo road trip just enjoying the summer with my dog or our dog, which makes our household very quiet. Um which is kind of nice and a little bit eerie at times. You know, I'm used to the activity. So, uh but I think it was gorgeous today. Not quite Rob level record setting heat, but I think it's supposed to be raining for like the next 10 days here in Seattle. So, >> checks out. >> Just when just when you think you you got out of it and we're they're pulling us right back in. >> Right back in. Well, we we love Seattle regardless. And Mike, how is your vacation time treating you? >> Doing good. Doing good. Took my daughter and my son to the park yesterday again. Uh grandpa, my dad joined us. Grandpa has both kids currently. Uh, we're good. Nice quiet house. This is great. >> Good. Well, I hope the kids are tuning in, even if grandpa has them, because they can learn a lot, not only about the Seahawks, but about uh what's going on in the NFC West because a trade that got everyone back on their phones, Cleveland Browns traded the defensive player of the year, Miles Garrett, not just to any team uh but the LA Rams. And we've been spending a little bit of time talking about them on this show this off season, but man, adding a Hall of Famer to their defense. Brian, what was your initial reaction when you heard this news break? >> I think we're going to keep this a PG show, so I will not give you my initial reaction. >> Mike's kids are watching. They're watching with grandpa. Okay, it >> it was not great. A, you know, I literally just wrapped up my morning show. Had a great conversation with Arian over at Wide Left about how he runs his business. We had I had had a a whole show where I detailed what June 1st means in terms of salary cap and why this was a window when a guy like Miles Garrett could be traded and was getting ready to go on a hike with my wife and our dog. And as we were going out the door, I see a stream of texts with all caps no. And I'm like, one of my pet peeves is when you've got friends that do things like that, but then they don't include any reference for what the heck they're talking about. And so then you go and you check and you're like, "Oh man, this is terrible news." It just is. It's terrible news if you're a Seahawks fan and it's great news if you're a Rams fan. And so the Rams Collective, if that exists, they're probably having popping champagne. They're having a great old time. >> We can get a dual collective and see what what that six people or eight people on the show. >> We should we should we should make sure it happens while we are the champs and they are the want to be champs. But um as I've said on my show, I I think there's going to be a lot of people that find ways to cope with this and spin it. I I'm taking the tack of this was a massively impactful move for the Rams. It changes the whole equation for all of the NFL. I'm not sure we've seen a situation where there's been an MVP, a runner up for offensive player of the year, and a defensive player of the year all on one team uh with a bunch of other talent as well. Um it is it is a tectonic shift in power and uh at the same time I don't for a second sell the Seahawks short uh and their ability to compete with anybody out on the field. So yeah, it was uh it was a bit of a gut punch um to be honest. And uh now we're we're dealing with the aftermath. >> I wish we had that moment on film, Brian, when you're walking out the door, peaceful, ready for the hike and then just the look down. It's like out of a movie almost. Rob, what was your initial reaction? Was it the same as drama as Brian's? Yeah, it was very similar actually because I was doing my radio show for the BBC at the time and I got a text from Jeff Simmons that was a four-letter word beginning with F in all capitals and uh immediately figured that Miles Garrett had been traded and it was to either the Niners or the Rams. So, while I was speaking on the radio, I was I hope my bosses are watching this. It's 1:00 a.m. They're probably not. I was looking on my phone to see what the news was and saw this huge picture of Miles Garrett in a Rams jersey on Shfter's account or whatever. Um, and then, you know, I had to sit there for probably about another 40 minutes doing the radio show until I could sort of take it all in. I think it's a master strobe by the Rams. I think they clearly feel uh very disappointed with the way that last season ended. If you look at all of the contending teams currently in the NFL, I I don't think hardly any of them had really taken a big step forward this off season, it did feel as if we were going to go into next season as things were standing with pretty much the teams all in a very similar shape to how they were last year. And the Rams have just blown that out of the water by going and getting Miles Garrett. I think it's an amazing trade for them. I think you got to give them some credit, you know, for for getting it done. Uh, but I uh I I really really I I'm never going to I've always kind of had a soft spot for the Browns, you know, just because they're so bad and I kind of they seem like they've got a nice fan base who who I appreciate the honesty. >> Well, they can take a running jump now cuz I'm never going to feel sorry for them ever again. Like they've ruined everything. So, I I hate the Browns. >> You lost uh you lost Rob State in support Browns Collective. Mike, is this a move that you saw coming or was this something that completely shocked you? >> No, I figured um I don't remember what time in the offseason it was, but when they um changed Miles's contract around, that made him more more tradable. I think that was in like March or something like that. Uh I was like, "Oh yeah, he's out of there." Because it just really didn't make much sense to to keep him as their GM Andrew Barry has kind of acknowledged when he since now they got rid of him. It's like, you know, the timelines weren't the same. Miles keeps saying, "I want to win like right now today." And the Browns are just like, "Look, dude, we're not really there in the winning business. We're in the building business." Uh, and they just just don't align. Uh, and you know, the Rams are just always the Rams will just trade the the house for who, not whoever, but they're probably the most I would say the most aggressive team in the league in that regard. You know, they'll offer two first for guys and and whatever. I mean, them willing to give up Jared Verse in this shows that. Uh, so I mean if they were willing and cuz like and also the Rams don't they don't wait like they're they're cool with like all right let's try to get all the good players you know we don't just need to like stay as stay very good let's keep trying to get better like they called on AJ Brown uh I believe so I I I figured he was probably probably out of there um but man yeah that's a I was already high on the Rams I actually did think they got a lot better uh before this trade uh you know I'm I'm a Coug so I'm higher on Jaylen Watson the quarterback they added maybe and some others are but he's really good. Uh and then obviously going against Tre McDuffy, you know, because watching watching the Seahawks Rams and all three matchups, which I've watched the film of, looked at all the numbers of watched all three games multiple times that they were one in the margins all three times. Obviously, the score the scoring margins indicate that, but it's a play here, a play there. And while the special teams obviously a problem for the Rams, if I was a Rams fan, if I was a Rams coach, if I was a Rams executive and I watched those games, I'd be like, "We need a better defense." Which sounds crazy because they were obviously a very good defense. But Sam played his butt off in those games because he could pick on their DBs in particular. like that they've since before this trade from Miles they had they basically swapped Kobe Durant who's not very good uh and like Emanuel Forbes for Jaylen Watson and Trent McDuffy that that that alone is massive to me because that like if they had those two guys in the NFC Championship game it it go it looks way different the scoring is down Seahawks may still win but the scoring is definitely down and then now you add Miles that's just that's just nuts. Uh, so yeah, I already kind of thought I understood I should say that while the Rams were the favorites to win the Super Bowl, I believe this offseason, all offseason, now I think the odds have shifted even more depending on what sports book you're looking at. Make perfect sense. Uh, to me, this is kind of what happens when you know you're the for the Seahawks perspective, when you're the team that everyone's looking to, it's like, all right, how do we how do we catch the Seahawks? You know, uh, same thing like when teams in the AFC West try to make big moves like, "All right, the Chiefs keep winning the division. How do we catch him? We got to fire our coach. We got to trade for whoever. We got to get a new quarterback." Like the Chiefs kind of set that standard over there. And, you know, Patriots used to do that same thing. Uh, when they had Bellich and Brady was like, "All right, how do we beat the Patriots?" You know, we fire our coach, we get a new quarterback, new coordinate, whatever. The Seahawks are kind of the mini version of that right now. It's like, "How do we catch the Seahawks?" And the Rams are like, "Let's go get Miles Garrett." And now they're caught on paper. ever that is game's not played on paper, but on paper the Rams easily to me have the best roster in the NFL. >> Well, certainly a better game later in the season, but I remember that first Rams game did not go well for the Seahawks offense and so uh something to be concerned with. But when you look at this the schedule for the season, the R the Seahawks don't play the Rams until Christmas and then later in January. So, obviously some time, but just for you, Brian, when you initially look at the Seattle Seahawks roster and then you think about the addition with Miles Garrett to the Rams defense, what what jumps out at you? What's the first thing that comes to mind about, hey, this is where the focus really needs to be? >> Yeah, I mean, the first thing I did is went back and wa rewatched the game when Miles Garrett was in Seattle in 2023 and was going against Charles Cross and it was a little bit of a different line. You know, you're talking about Evan Brown at center and Damen Lewis at left guard, but you did have also Stone Forsythe at right tackle and uh I think it was still Anthony Bradford at right guard. And Miles Garrett did not dominate that game. Now, the Seahawks did what most teams do, which is they chipped him. They gave a lot of extra protection. He did not take over that game um the way that I think most people would expect him to against what was a really bad offensive line that year. and also a offense that was running with Shane Waldron that was troubled and didn't really know what it was or what it was trying to do. So that was the first thing I did. And then I had a conversation with Quandre Diggs today on my show and Quandre brought up a lot of great points that that I think make a lot of sense, which is I brought up to him that this move to me besides just being like, "Okay, you're going to add the defensive player of the year. That's good no matter what." It unlocks the ability for the Rams to do something they've been trying to do for the last two years, which is basically stick and dime. Everybody talked about the Seahawks playing nickel all last year with extra defensive back on the field and still being able to defend the run. The Rams have trying to go one step further and have like basically all defensive backs and then four rush uh linemen and get away with that. Well, the difference between the Rams ability to do that with Trent McDuffy in one inside corner spot, Quinton Lake at the other kind of dime spot is that neither one of those guys are Nicki Manor's size. They're not big nickels. And Quandre talked about himself not being a big nickel in his time. And that the Seahawks have four large tight ends. They have the ability to go 12. They have the ability to go 13. And if the Rams want to play dime defense, if they want to get all those DBs out there and and hope that their four is enough, the Seahawks have the ability to potentially really punish them for that. And I agree with what Mike said in terms of the games being decided in the margins. I don't point to the quarterbacks nearly as much as others do. I think it was the Seahawks ability to run the football in those games that actually was the key deciding factor. Ken Walker was a big part of that, but the offensive line also leaned on those guys. And so I think that that's the part of this that really is going to matter for the Seahawks is can they punish the Rams for getting small. And that's something you have to hope for. Miles Garrett is not just a pass rusher. He is an excellent run defender as well. So um yeah, I I think that's where my mind goes. >> Rob, can you elaborate on that? because obviously Brian giving us some confidence in not only the Seahawks line but some of the the strong tight ends that they have as well. But for people who might not be all in with the Cleveland Browns who are all the way out in Seattle or somewhere else in the country or globally and uh they don't know that much about Miles Garrett besides just Miles Garrett, defense player of the year. What should they know about this player and how he could potentially cause a threat to the Seahawks even with the talent that they have on their offense? Well, he's one of the best players who's ever lived and he may well be the best talent in the NFL currently. He's uh also the kind of person who strikes me as someone who could who will probably be an amazing athlete when he's 38, let alone 30. So, uh I I completely agree with Brian. Some of the copium that I've read over the last 24 hours is staggering. um people saying, "Well, this is a one-year window for the I like give me a break." Like, this is an unbelievable trade. And it reminded me, it's kind of like a it's it's like the Trent Williams and Christian McCaffrey trades on steroids. like they just for some reason there is another team in the com in the division that has able to acquire you know an amazing player who uh plays an important position and he's now for the Rams and frankly you know he can just destroy games on his own if you have a look at the number of pressures that Braden Fisk and Turner and Young created last season they were all quite high up on the list already and now you chuck Miles Garrett into the mix. The Browns had nobody like that. The Rams, I think, had the fourth DVA defense last year. Maybe I'm wrong. Um, Chuck Miles Garrett on start team now. It it it's frustrating and disappointing. Now, it doesn't mean that they're guaranteed to win the Super Bowl, but um I think if if Matthew Stafford can stay healthy and Miles Garrett can stay healthy, they're going to take some stopping. And um I don't know what you can do about it. There's there's nothing you can do really. They couldn't have outbid them. I don't think there's he was going to go to the Rams and now you've got to deal with it. Like I said, it doesn't guarantee anything, but um they are definitely going to be the favorites next year. >> Well, Mike, a lot of people kind of alluding to what Rob was saying, wondering, okay, now what do the Seahawks do? They do they need to make a big splash? What can the Seahawks how can they respond? Is there anything that you think the Seahawks could do or just putting people at ease if they don't have to do anything? >> Yeah, I don't think they have to do anything now. Um maybe at the end of the preseason, see how your team looks. Uh maybe the deadline you try to make a move. I don't think it's as simple as like, all right, the other team acquired a pass rusher, so let's add an offensive lineman. It may just be very similar to the Rashid Shahit trade, which like makes something you're already good at even better. Uh, I don't know who that player would be at at this point. Sometime the Seahawks have had some luck getting like getting a marriage between like disgruntled but good player or guy who peace with his organization but is actually like not like a toxic player uh acquisitions like Carlos Dunlap for instance, he was just like not rocking with the Bengals so they got him, you know, diggs the Lions didn't rock with him so they got him, you know. So I I'd have to do some more digging to figure out who that type of player is who's maybe not in line with his organization that may be available. Uh, but like some of my homies have been texting me like, "Mike, are we screwed? Like, what do we do?" I was like, "Just Brian Flurry needs to had a best run game in the league at this point." Like, I let me see what the Seahawks were in like rushing offense. I don't believe it was that great until like December. Um, but they should be the the goal should be like I have like a top five rushing offense because Miles can kill you no matter what you're doing, but like it's a lot harder to kill you if you're just, you know, running it down the the opponent's throat. Uh because that Rams front was already really really really good. Like remember Gray's able last year? Like Gray had a great year. You know what Gray said was his worst games whenever they played the Rams? You know, I think Gray only gave up two sacks all year and I want to say they were both to Kobe Turner in the same game. You know, uh the week 16 game I believe on Thursday Night Football. So like that that front is really really solid. Uh they can unlock so much stuff. You know, Miles can rush from everywhere. He's kind of one of those guys who has more gravity than than Jared verse too. Um like what you have to do to account for Miles, you know, you can like the Seahawks used to have to try to block Aaron Donald like I put three guys on him. Aaron would get triple teamed in some games. You got to do that same stuff with Miles and if you do, you're just allocating resources, you know, uh somewhere else to leave open to Byron Young or you know, Braden Fisk or whoever. Uh really. So that's a problem. But I don't think they need to do anything. It really is just make sure your run game is the best in the league. Not like really like legitimately the best. I don't know how you do it, you know? I think this is real. I've I've talked >> simple simple like simple just the best. >> I mean that's got to be >> it's got to be though. That's the thing cuz I don't think you can overell or you can if you're like really into coping, you know, as a Seahawks fan, you can kind of underell the impact, but like what I've watched I've watched a lot of good players in this like decade, you know, live, too. And Aaron Aaron, for my money, Donald is probably the best player I've I've seen uh live. Uh I think Christian McCaffrey is in that combo, too. And then Miles is right there. He did not dominate that 2023 Seahawks game as Brian was talking about. I think even Jason Peters might have played in that too. Very weird weirdly quiet Miles game, but he can. I know he can dominate and that's the point. Uh is is that he can. So the best way I think is to just have the best run game in the league, you know, just dominate on on that side of the ball, you know, because no pass rusher can just fly up the field, right? If they got to play their run keys on first, second, and third down if you're in third and short. So that that would be my advice to the Seahawks. Not the Seahawks de my advice, but if they were to solicit it, that's what I would tell them. That's what every Seahawk fan should be hoping for. Not a splashy trade to counteract this, but just like schematically now your goal should be run the ball better than anybody in the league runs the ball. >> I I want to jump in for a second there. Sorry. Sorry. Two things. One's a question, but first just a comment. >> People are like immediately jumping. Well, we got to get Max Crosby. I'm like, there is not a counter to acquiring the best football player in the NFL, the best defensive player in the NFL. Like, Miles Garrett is, I think, arguably the best player in the entire league, uh, regardless of position. Like, he is just an alien. Like, he is a different level player. And as much as Max Crosby, like great, I don't think that that eliminates the impact [laughter] of the Rams adding Miles Garrett. So, I don't think that there's some like other counter move that all of a sudden just makes this, you know, equal. Uh, it is what it is. title: Coach Mike McCarthy Media Availability (June 2) | Pittsburgh Steelers
text: Uh good afternoon or good morning. Um this is our official mini camp and frankly the what we're trying to accomplish this week is to complete our install. I know I've talked a lot about getting everything in before the 12th. This will give us that opportunity uh this week. We're also operating on a inseason schedule which I think is important because it is our first year here uh to give the give the men a chance to you know feel what a Thursday in season schedule will be like. So doing a lot of little things like that, but uh it's been great. You got excellent participation which we've had all year and u we're looking forward to a great day of work. You know, I didn't even take attendance today, so um it's it's been great. coach. I think anytime you can establish the room, um, you know, the the value in our room, you know, obviously with Aaron Rogers, you know, the experience and just, uh, what he brings to the table. And I'm not just playing talking about playing on the playing, you know, between the white lines, but you know, his experience and uh and what he can add to a conversation in the quarterback room is is has been extremely valuable for our younger players. Uh boy, I've really grown to have a, you know, a lot of appreciation for for Mason. Um I'm really enjoying our time together. He's a he's a hell of a football player. So, you know, another layer of experience for our two young players. So, and and Will and Drew are just soaking it up, frankly. I mean, they're just soaking it up and and they, you know, they've done a really good job in that in that aspect of it, too. So, uh, so that's the benefits of it to have a diverse group like that. Uh, because you never have enough quarterbacks and, you know, the challenges, frankly, is trying to find reps for these guys. Um, like for instance, today, you know, we have three um twominute drills in this in this seven on seven. We're going to let Mason and two young guys take it. So just trying to balance that out. Um so that's your really only challenge. But I I I'm really enjoying having four quarterbacks. >> Mike, you know 55 touches thing we were talking about last week. Have you hit that a lot in your career traditionally? It seems pretty ambitious. >> It is ambitious. U you know traditionally the number was 53. I think I I spoke on that. Um, but you know, I think just the way the league has gone with the rules and things like that and just the the way things have opened up, I think 55 is is a it's an attainable goal, but it's a definitely a higher goal. But it's more about the mindset of how you train. There's more to it than just achieve achieving a statistical uh goal that week. It it puts you on on a focus of how you want to play the game, you know, which also focuses on how you train. It focuses how you install, how you, you know, educate, interact with the players, you know, what their expectations are in each and every game. But to sit here and tell you statistically exactly how you're going to play every week, you know, that's that's not that's not practical because that's, you know, the NFL is so competitive. But it's definitely, you know, something that I've always paid attent attention to. I I got into the league in 1993 as a you know quality control coach and I've always you know have had game analysis as as part of my thought process. >> Mike, would you have to use this week um in the upcoming weeks before camp with Patrick Graham to find out different ways that maybe haven't been used yet or just more ways to use new? >> Well, we we have been doing that. I mean, as far as, you know, just the challenge, I think if you watch the pre, you know, the early team period, um, you know, the pressure drill has has been outstanding. Just the, you know, the conversations, you know, the protection adjustments, um, you know, changing some of the verbiage and things, just, you know, taking advantage of things that, you know, terminology wise that were used here in the past versus what we initially installed. Uh, and it's great to have Nick here. You know, Nick's excited about being here and so we'll definitely highlight the packages for Nick both uh this week and next week. >> Mike, when you have players who are in the middle of contract negotiations and they might choose not to participate or at least not full out here, what are your conversations like with them and especially with the new staff, how do you make sure that they're up to speed so that then when they do return, they're ready to go. >> I think it's like everything in life, frankly. Um, there's a personal side to this. There's a professional side to this. And when you break down the professional the professional aspects of of being in the NFL as a coach or a player, we all have contracts. Uh, so when those things occur, uh, you know, that I really frankly just put that into a business category. So, uh, been dealing with it for 20 years. Um, and the same advice I've always given. you know, it's it's a it's a business situation and do the things you need to do necessary, you know, but uh in Nick in Nick's, you know, case, you know, he's been in constant communication uh with us, you know, had had lunch with Nick in March out there in Scottdale still. So, I mean, so he's done the things necessary, you know, but he's been he's in a he's in a business situation. So, I think and you know, it's no different than any of our players, you know. I think you just you just separate that and and uh you know this is an important time in their lives. I mean you know their business decisions and business opportunities can change you know the course of their life and their family's life and I and I don't take that for granted. Uh but also you know I'm in charge of the football part of it. So you know we don't lose sight on that. And I just like I think like any time you have situations where you know you're not together you just make sure you communicate and I think our guys have done a good job with that especially being in year one. >> Mike in your short time with Darnell what what has impressed you about him and how do you see him? >> Love Darnell. I mean, he he can play nickel, he can play corner, obviously, you know, he he can play his, you know, dime and also he can play safety. So, um, I'm I'm really looking forward to working with them. Um, but yeah, I I think here's I can see why exactly why Joe says that. That's a that's an excellent comparison. >> Guys, two more quick ones. >> This is your first year in this division coaching, but can you imagine AFC North? >> I'm all for it.
